title: Headless workers pause on external_directory walls for /dev, /proc and their own temp roots; stale walls accumulate
body:
## Problem

Headless workers in a managed project repo keep pausing on "Maintainer permission required" for `external_directory` reads of system pseudo-paths and their own temp directories. The issue then stays `status:blocked` with `needs-maintainer-permissions` until a maintainer signs a withdrawal with sudo. Meanwhile it occupies a per-URL issue slot and counts toward the project's open-issue fuse, which stops new work from being filed.

## Evidence (one managed project repo, 2026-11-25)

Nine open issues are held by stale requests whose worker sessions ended 5 to 12 days ago:

- `/dev/*`: four requests (2026-11-15 to 2026-11-20)
- `/proc/*`: two requests (2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16)
- `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/*` or a subdirectory: two requests
- `~/.aidevops-private/tmp/*`: one request
- `~/*`: one request (broad; must stay held)

Three of these issues then passed through the project's three automatic retries and were marked unavailable, although their award sources were never tested.

## Expected

- Reads of `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdin|stdout|stderr`, `/dev/fd/*` and the worker's own temp roots under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/` should not trigger an interactive permission wall in headless sessions. For example, allow them in the generated OpenCode permission config, or have the worker brief route temp writes through the existing workspace paths.
- `/proc/*` on Linux (for example memory probes) needs an explicit decision: allow read-only access to `/proc/self/*` and `/proc/meminfo`, or keep it walled.
- Broad requests (`~/*`) stay held, as now.
- Consider auto-withdrawing, or at least surfacing in the pulse, requests whose session has ended. The current rule needs a signed decision for every request, and stale walls accumulate unseen.

Start from the headless worker permission profile in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-permissions.mjs` and the broker that raises the wall (`permission-broker.mjs`, `permission-broker-read-target.mjs`). Stale-request handling lives in `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`. Confirm the exact generation path before editing; extend the existing tests in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs` and `test-worker-permission-grant.mjs`.

### Files Scope

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=gh40255-integration -->
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-permission-grant.mjs`

Brief repaired: the config hook calls managed-directory registration followed by signed-grant registration; baseline runtime permissions need an explicit hook call, independent of grants. The broker dispatches its bounded read-target classifier through both permission APIs. The existing grant suite verifies generated worker rules. Collision discovery found no competing PR or claim on these paths. Verify with the existing broker, grant and managed-directory Node suites plus the worker-permission-helper shell suite. Keep /proc walled and retain signed withdrawal for stale requests; no blanket /dev, home or private-temp grant.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-permissions.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-read-target.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`

## Verification

- Run a headless worker that executes `cmd 2>/dev/null` and writes under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/` and confirm no permission request is raised.
- Confirm a `~/*` read still raises a request.
- Existing permission broker/helper tests per `reference/dispatch-blockers.md`.

title: t19357: feat(worktree): clone pnpm workspace node_modules (root + members) into fresh worktrees instead of full install
body:
## Task


Make a fresh linked worktree of a pnpm workspace monorepo ready to run its tests without a full `pnpm install`. That means restoring the root `node_modules` and each workspace member's `node_modules` (`packages/*`, `apps/*`). Do it with copy-on-write clones on APFS (`cp -c` / clonefile) or reflink on Linux, gated by the existing lockfile identity checks.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make a fresh linked worktree of a pnpm workspace monorepo ready to run its tests without a full `pnpm install`. That means restoring the root `node_modules` and each workspace member's `node_modules` (`packages/*`, `apps/*`). Do it with copy-on-write clones on APFS (`cp -c` / clonefile) or reflink on Linux, gated by the existing lockfile identity checks.

## Why

In a private pnpm monorepo, headless workers ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` in every fresh worktree. Over 3 days that was 123 runs, median 369s. The prompt cache also expires during the wait, so each install forces a context re-write. That repo's AGENTS.md tells workers that "the framework's copy of node_modules ... misses packages/*".

Code-reading evidence (line numbers from `main` at the time of filing):

- `_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py:160-190` does a validated byte copy through memory, not a clone.
- `worktree-dependency-provision.py:58-59,83` hard-caps the copy at 64 MiB and 20,000 entries. A pnpm monorepo's `node_modules` is far larger. `worktree-helper-add.sh:439-458,503-506` then rejects it with `source-exceeds-budget`.
- `worktree-helper-add.sh:599` and `pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh:141-145` only try directories that have their own lockfile. `_worktree_dependency_identity.py:150-155` (`matching_lock`) requires the lockfile in the package directory. Workspace members whose lock lives at the root are skipped, and the comment at `pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh:142-143` says so.
- `WORKTREE_NODE_MODULES_RESTORE_MAX_DIRS:=2` (`worktree-helper-add.sh:39`) limits the attempt to two directories.
- pnpm workspace symlinks that point at `../../packages/*` would fail the `escaping-package-root` check in `_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py:106-113`.
- The headless path calls `_dlw_restore_worktree_deps` in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` around lines 575 and 665, which reaches the same `_provision_worktree_node_modules`. Rejections are only logged as "Dependency provisioning unavailable".

## How

1. Add a pnpm workspace mode.
   - Detect it from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` plus a root `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
   - Verify identity once against the root lock: the source and worktree `pnpm-lock.yaml` must be byte-identical, and the root `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml` must match.
   - Then restore root `node_modules` and every member `node_modules` listed by the workspace globs.
2. Use a copy-on-write clone for this mode. On macOS: `cp -cR` with clonefile; on Linux: `cp -a --reflink=auto`. Skip the 64 MiB byte budget, because a clone costs no data copy. Keep the byte-copy path as the fallback when clone is unsupported.
3. Allow relative symlinks inside the worktree root that point at workspace members. Keep rejecting links that escape the worktree.
4. Wire the mode into both the interactive (`worktree-helper-add.sh`) and headless (`pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh`) restore paths. Log one line per restore with the outcome and elapsed time.
5. If identity differs, fall back to the existing behaviour. That is either the owner-approved install, or the worker running `pnpm install`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_identity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_manifest.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_payload.py`

Brief repaired: terminal Qlty regression at PR #40260 head 9b1a0c965601 requires cohesive manifest-parsing and descriptor-payload modules rather than growing the identity and snapshot files. The separately assigned CI repair produced commit 97a5fa949392a75876bf12dcda8a240a7bd09dfb; these two adjacent implementation paths are recorded before the original executor adopts that repair. No explicit exclusions, permissions or security guarantees are widened. Verified no other PR/claim collision for the added paths after the repair executor released its push. Verify with python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py, bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh, and the pinned Qlty regression helper against the existing PR base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a pnpm workspace with identical lockfiles, a new worktree gets working root and member `node_modules`, so `pnpm exec tsx --version` runs from a member directory. No install runs.
- [ ] A lockfile mismatch falls back to the current behaviour and logs the reason.
- [ ] Symlinks that escape the worktree are still rejected.
- [ ] Restore time on APFS for a large monorepo is reported in the log, in seconds.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh`
- Manual check: create a worktree of any local pnpm workspace repo, then check the provisioning log line and run a member-package command.

</details>

title: t19358: Add prompt-cache keep-alive to the OpenCode v2 provider-auth adapter
body:
## Task


Give OpenCode v2 the prompt-cache keep-alive that PR #40256 added for v1, so long tool calls stop forcing full cache rebuilds there too.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Give OpenCode v2 the prompt-cache keep-alive that PR #40256 added for v1, so long tool calls stop forcing full cache rebuilds there too.

## Why

On v1, PR #40256 records each completed agent request. While a tool runs longer than the 5-minute cache TTL, it re-sends that request with `max_tokens: 1`. In one worker fleet, about 29.9% of cache writes followed 5–60 minute gaps; this removes them.

The v2 adapter does not record requests, so v2 sessions still pay those rebuilds. OpenCode v1 is the active host today, so this is not urgent. Without it, the saving disappears when hosts move to v2.

## Dependency

Blocked by #40251: PR #40256 adds `cache-keepalive.mjs` and the v1 wiring. Start only after that PR has merged to `main`. A worker that finds `cache-keepalive.mjs` missing should stop as blocked rather than recreate it.

## How

- Files to modify:
  - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-provider-auth.mjs`: in `createHttpResponseHook`, after a 2xx Anthropic response, call `cacheKeepalive.recordRequest(event.sessionID, <send context>, <pre-transform body>, status)`.

title: t19359: fix(disk-capacity): count APFS purgeable capacity toward the worktree percentage floor on macOS
body:
## Task


Count macOS APFS "important usage" capacity toward the worktree/dispatch percentage floor in `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`, so space that macOS holds as purgeable (Time Machine local snapshots, purgeable caches) and reclaims on demand no longer idles every worker slot.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Count macOS APFS "important usage" capacity toward the worktree/dispatch percentage floor in `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`, so space that macOS holds as purgeable (Time Machine local snapshots, purgeable caches) and reclaims on demand no longer idles every worker slot.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 on a 3.6 TiB APFS volume: `df` reported 47.4 GiB available (1%), below the 50 GiB capped 5% floor, so every dispatch attempt logged `disk space critical (reason=below-minimum-percent …)` (67+ blocks in one window) and worker occupancy fell to zero. Deleting ~12 GiB of disposable temp trees freed nothing visible because two purgeable Time Machine local snapshots (2026-11-16, 2026-11-24) pin the blocks; finished-worktree cleanup reports `reclaimed_mib=0` for the same reason. At the same moment `NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey` reported 666.8 GB: macOS guarantees that capacity to user-initiated writes and purges the snapshots itself when it is needed. GH#38026 capped the floor and added a read-only advisory, but the gate still reads raw `df` and blocks until a human thins backups — the user-attention dependency aidevops exists to remove.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`: add a read-only Darwin probe (`osascript -l JavaScript`, Foundation `NSURL` resource value `NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey`, path passed as argv, bounded by the existing `timeout_sec`/`timeout`/`gtimeout` pattern used by `aidevops_disk_capacity_reclaim_hint`). Run it only when raw `df` headroom is below the percentage floor. Admit when important-usage capacity meets the floor; keep the absolute 5 GiB minimum and quota checks on raw numbers so ENOSPC protection is unchanged. `AIDEVOPS_DISK_COUNT_PURGEABLE=0` restores the raw-only policy. Never thin, delete or modify snapshots.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: log once per pulse process when admission relied on purgeable capacity (raw vs important KB) so the decision is observable.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh`: stub `uname`/`osascript` so the suite stays deterministic on macOS hosts and covers credit-admits, credit-insufficient, opt-out, and non-Darwin cases.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh`

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh` passes on macOS and Linux.
- ShellCheck clean for the touched scripts.
- On a Darwin host whose raw `df` headroom is below the floor but important-usage capacity is above it, `aidevops_worktree_capacity_check` returns 0 and Pulse logs the purgeable-admission line; with `AIDEVOPS_DISK_COUNT_PURGEABLE=0` it returns 1 `below-minimum-percent`.
- Raw headroom below 5 GiB still blocks regardless of purgeable capacity.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh
rg -n 'purgeable' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 3
```

title: t19360: fix(complexity-scan): reap leaked complexity-scan-tree clones and clean up on interruption
body:
## Task


Stop the weekly complexity scan from leaking `complexity-scan-tree.XXXXXX` clones under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, and reap clones that earlier interrupted scans already left behind.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the weekly complexity scan from leaking `complexity-scan-tree.XXXXXX` clones under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, and reap clones that earlier interrupted scans already left behind.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25: 41 leaked scan trees (2026-10-22 … 2026-11-25), ~9.3 GiB counted once across the set, in a temp directory with ~38,600 top-level entries and no sweeper. Each tree is a `git clone --local` plus a full origin/main checkout made by `_complexity_scan_pull_latest` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh:821`). Only `run_weekly_complexity_scan` removes it (`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:726-728`), after `_run_weekly_complexity_scan_in` returns, so any interrupted scan leaks the tree: a killed `complexity-scan-runner.sh run`, a pulse stage timeout, or a reboot. One live runner had been inside a 3-hour-old tree for 1h47m. On a host whose disk gate was already blocking dispatch, the leak was a direct cost.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh` `run_weekly_complexity_scan`: guarantee removal on interruption. Use a RETURN/EXIT/INT/TERM-safe cleanup scoped to this function, and restore any previous trap. Model it on `_release_lock` in `.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-runner.sh:118-146`. Never remove the canonical `aidevops_path`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh` `_complexity_scan_pull_latest`: before `mktemp`, reap direct children of the temp base that match `complexity-scan-tree.??????`. Reap a directory only when it is a real directory (not a symlink), older than 24 h (env override `AIDEVOPS_COMPLEXITY_SCAN_TREE_MAX_AGE_HOURS`), and has no process cwd inside it (`lsof -n -Fn -d cwd` when available; skip reaping when `lsof` is missing). Log one summary line `Complexity scan: reaped N stale scan tree(s)` to `$LOGFILE`.
- Reference implementation of the same safety checks (one-off, already run on the reporting host): validate-then-remove by name pattern, age, cwd-in-use and origin remote, with dry-run by default.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh`

## Acceptance

- An interrupted scan (simulate by sending TERM to the subshell running `_run_weekly_complexity_scan_in`) leaves no `complexity-scan-tree.*` directory behind.
- Stale trees older than the threshold are removed on the next scan; trees younger than it, or with a live cwd inside, are kept.
- The canonical repo path is never removed (the existing non-git in-place path keeps working).
- ShellCheck clean; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh` passes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh
fd --max-depth 1 -t d -g 'complexity-scan-tree.*' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp
rg -n 'reaped .* stale scan tree' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 3
```

title: t19361: fix(opencode-db-archive): support the session_inbox schema generation so the 92 GB interactive DB is archived and event-expired
body:
## Task


Teach the OpenCode DB archive, event-expiry, retention and restore paths the current OpenCode session-schema generation. The generation is the one introduced by migrations `20260812181746_session_inbox` … `20260910120000_clear_v1_session_permission`. Today every run against it fails closed with rc=3, so the largest active DB is never archived or event-expired.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Teach the OpenCode DB archive, event-expiry, retention and restore paths the current OpenCode session-schema generation. The generation is the one introduced by migrations `20260812181746_session_inbox` … `20260910120000_clear_v1_session_permission`. Today every run against it fails closed with rc=3, so the largest active DB is never archived or event-expired.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 (archive log, 50 consecutive runs): the interactive aidevops DB under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/project-aidevops-<hash>/opencode/opencode.db` is 92 GB (22.5 M pages, 4,553 sessions, 0 free pages). Every inventory logs:

`Unsupported or unavailable OpenCode session schema: table=session_input actual_columns=[missing] … reason=column-mismatch; active data was left untouched.` → `rc=3`.

The runtime that owns it (OpenCode 1.19.6, the current interactive build) migrated the schema as follows:

- dropped `session_input` and `session_context_epoch`;
- added `session_inbox(id,session_id,type,payload,delivery,enqueued_seq,time_created)`, `session_pending(id,session_id,type,data,delivery,admitted_seq,time_created)`, `instruction_entry(session_id,key,value,removed,time_created,time_updated)`, `instruction_state(session_id,epoch_start,through_seq,initial_values,current_values)`, `instruction_blob(hash,value)`, `session_v2(...)` (no `session_id` column), `kv`, `worktree`;
- added a `created` column to `event` (`id,aggregate_id,seq,type,data,created`).

`session`, `message`, `part`, `todo`, `session_share`, `session_message` and `event_sequence` keep their supported column sets. All of the new session-scoped tables are currently empty, so the data lives in tables the helper already moves. Because `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh:130` validates the schema first, the GH#38491/GH#38630 event-expiry pass also never runs here. That pass is what kept the `event` table from regrowing to ~78 GB on older DBs. As more DBs open under the current runtime, every one will stop being maintained.

## How

Keep the fail-closed contract for unknown generations; add this generation as a known one.

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh` (`opencode_archive_table_schema_supported`, `opencode_archive_schema_supported` ~L190-289): add supported column sets for `session_inbox`, `session_pending`, `instruction_entry`, `instruction_state`, and the `event` set with `created`. Make `session_input`/`session_context_epoch` optional when the session-inbox generation is detected (for example `session_inbox` exists). Extend the `unknown-session-table` allowlist with the four new `session_id` tables. Keep `instruction_blob`, `kv`, `worktree` and `session_v2` out of the session-scoped set: they have no `session_id` column, so the existing checks never treat them as session-scoped.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-schema.sh` (`_archive_session_schema_sql` ~L161-215, `_archive_migrate_schema_columns`): create the new session-scoped tables in the archive DB and migrate `event.created`.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` (count/copy/delete blocks around L1199-1245, L1300, L1411-1530, L1457): copy and delete rows of the new session-scoped tables with their session, using the existing `has_session_input_table` optional-table pattern.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-retention.sh` (~L151-168) and `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh` (~L37): include the new tables in retention deletes and restore copies.
- Never write to an active DB that fails validation. Keep transactional batches, idle/heartbeat gating and integrity checks unchanged.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-schema.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-retention.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`

## Acceptance

- A fixture DB with the new generation's schema (build it from the column lists above, or from `sqlite3 -readonly <db> .schema` on a host DB; never copy production data) passes validation. Inactive sessions archive with message/part/event rows and any `session_inbox`/`session_pending`/`instruction_*` rows. Restore round-trips them.
- The legacy generation (with `session_input`/`session_context_epoch`) still validates and archives as before.
- A DB with an additional unknown `session_id` table still fails closed with rc=3 and leaves data untouched.
- On the reporting host, the next scheduled run logs a non-3 outcome for the interactive aidevops DB, and the event-expiry pass runs against it.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive*.sh
rg -n 'project-aidevops-.*rc=' ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log | tail -n 3
```

## Related

- GH#35902 (V2 parity tracker; its "DB archive path and schema" item covers the V2 data dir, while this is the current V1 runtime's schema)
- GH#38491, GH#38630 (event expiry)

</details>

title: Storage lifecycle: worker-built Docker images and build cache have no owner (175 GB observed); escalate npm cache advisory under low disk
body:
## Problem

Worker test/verification runs build Docker images (names like `<app>-gh<N>:candidate`, `opendesk-gh45:verify`, `netbird-smoke:<tag>`) and accumulate BuildKit cache. No aidevops store owns their lifecycle, and `aidevops cleanup` does not report them.

Observed on one macOS install (OrbStack), with the system disk at 99%:

- `docker system df`: 231 images (22 active), 113.5 GB, 80 GB reclaimable. Build cache: 2364 entries, 107.5 GB, 0 active. 367 local volumes, 57.8 GB, 48 GB reclaimable.
- The OrbStack disk image takes 175 GB on the host.
- Most images are per-issue worker artefacts that are 1–5 weeks old.

The npm cache (`~/.npm/_cacache`) reached 387 GB on the same machine. `aidevops status` only warns about it (10 GiB threshold), and that warning did not prevent the disk filling.

## Proposal

1. Add a `docker` row to `aidevops cleanup`: a read-only `docker system df` summary with the owning cleaner.
2. Producer-owned retention for worker-built images. Label images built by workers (for example `sh.aidevops.issue=<N>`, `sh.aidevops.created=<ts>`), then prune labelled images whose issue/PR is terminal or older than N days. Run `docker builder prune --filter until=<window>` under r922.
3. Escalate the npm cache advisory when free disk space is under a threshold (for example <5% free). Keep mutation on the explicit `npm-cache-helper.sh clean --apply --confirm clean-npm-cache` path.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh` (report row and dispatch)
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle.md` (inventory row: Docker images/build cache, external/joint owner)
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-store-policies.md` (policy)
- Worker build paths that call `docker build`: find with `rg -n "docker build" .agents/`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/npm-cache-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle.md`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-store-policies.md`

## Verification

- `aidevops cleanup` shows a docker row with sizes, or a visible timeout.
- A dry run lists only labelled worker images and never unlabelled user images or volumes.
- ShellCheck clean.

title: t19362: Auto-retry stopped OpenCode sessions after terminal provider Overloaded errors
body:
## Task


Interactive OpenCode sessions stop with a terminal "Overloaded" provider error and never resume. Add a plugin-level session retry that waits about one minute after a terminal provider-overload error and then continues the stopped primary session automatically, with a bounded attempt budget and user-visible toasts.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-overload-retry.mjs` — event-driven module:
  - classify terminal overload errors: `APIError`/`UnknownError` with HTTP 529 or `/overloaded/i` in message/response body (covers Anthropic `overloaded_error`, OpenAI `server_is_overloaded` / "servers are currently overloaded", and OpenCode's "Provider is overloaded");
  - root interactive sessions only (skip headless runs and subagent sessions);
  - remember the session's last agent/model/variant from `chat.params` (same source as `compaction-loop-guard.mjs` `chatParams`);
  - after the terminal error, schedule one continuation after `AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS` (default 60);
  - cancel the timer on user takeover (new user message, session busy, session deleted);
  - before prompting, re-check that the live session status is idle;
  - send a synthetic continuation via `client.session.promptAsync` that preserves agent/model/variant (pattern: `compaction-loop-recovery.mjs` `continueSession`);
  - budget `AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) per overload episode, reset on a completed assistant reply or user takeover;
  - disable entirely with `AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY=0`;
  - toasts for "retrying in 60s (n/N)" and "gave up".
- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-overload-retry.mjs` — focused synthetic-event coverage for the scheduler (state machine with timers and cancellation is high-risk; this is the cheapest proof).
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — wire `event` and `chat.params`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-turn-outcomes.mjs` — suppress the contradictory "Nothing was retried automatically" toast for overload errors while auto-retry is enabled.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/configuration.md` (or the nearest plugin env-var reference) — document the three env vars.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-overload-retry.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-overload-retry.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-turn-outcomes.mjs
- .agents/reference/configuration.md

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Interactive OpenCode sessions stop with a terminal "Overloaded" provider error and never resume. Add a plugin-level session retry that waits about one minute after a terminal provider-overload error and then continues the stopped primary session automatically, with a bounded attempt budget and user-visible toasts.

## Why

OpenCode 1.19.6 already retries overload errors inside a turn, but only briefly: the embedded retry policy uses `zc=2000` (2 s initial), `Hc=2` (doubling), `Xc=30000` (30 s cap without headers) and `Qc=5` (attempt limit). Once those attempts are exhausted the session emits a terminal `session.error` and goes idle, so a provider overload lasting longer than about 60-90 s stops the session until the user types "continue".

Evidence (local runtime events, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db`, 2026-11-25):

- Three root `claude-opus-5-5` sessions ended at 04:56:52Z, 04:56:54Z and 04:57:12Z with `session.error` → `APIError`, HTTP 529 (`overloaded_error`), `is_retryable: true`, followed by `session.idle`.
- In one of those sessions, ~10 `session.status` busy/retry cycles over ~95 s preceded the terminal error. Nothing resumed the session afterwards.
- The plugin's turn diagnostics toast currently tells the user "Nothing was retried automatically."

## Acceptance

1. A terminal overload `session.error` in a root interactive session schedules exactly one continuation after the configured delay, using the session's last agent/model/variant.
2. User takeover before the delay cancels the retry; a busy live status at fire time skips the prompt.
3. Headless and child sessions are never retried; non-overload errors (403, 400, aborts, context overflow) are never retried.
4. Attempts stop at the cap with a "gave up" toast; a successful reply resets the budget.
5. `AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY=0` disables the feature and restores the existing diagnostics toast.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-overload-retry.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-turn-diagnostics.mjs`
- `node --check` on the changed modules; repository plugin test runner/linters as configured.
- Runtime: deploy via `setup.sh --non-interactive` and confirm the plugin loads (plugin health stage) in a fresh OpenCode session.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: Maintainer gate: blocked start still allows worktree edits; author lookup fails only inside interactive-start-helper
body:
## Problem

Two gaps let an interactive session work past the maintainer gate on a linked issue.

### 1. A blocked start does not stop edits in the worktree

`interactive-start-helper.sh` correctly refused to start full-loop (`Maintainer gate pre-check BLOCKED`), but it had already claimed the issue and left a linked worktree. Afterwards nothing stopped the session from editing source files in that worktree: `pre-edit-check.sh` passes because it only checks "linked worktree, not canonical". The model then edited code despite the recorded blocker. No commit or push happened, but the edits should never have been possible.

Expected: when the gate blocks, the worktree and branch carry a durable "gate-blocked" marker (or the claim stays in a blocked state). `pre-edit-check.sh`, the OpenCode edit/write tool hook and the pre-commit hook then refuse writes on that branch until `approval-helper.sh verify issue <N>` returns VERIFIED, or until the author check passes on a re-run. The only escape is the signed approval.

### 2. The author-authority lookup fails inside the start helper but passes standalone

The issue author had `write` permission (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/collaborators/<author>/permission` returned `write`). Inside `interactive-start-helper.sh` → `_linked_issue_author_allows_start` the gate reported `authority=permission-lookup-failed:api-failure`, twice, several minutes apart. Calling `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority <repo> <author> COLLABORATOR` directly from a script that sources `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` returned `rc=0 reason=trusted-permission` (HTTP 304, stored verdict `write`). `github_app_is_configured` was false.

Side effect: the failed check applied the `needs-maintainer-review` label as containment. After that, a trusted write-access author's issue needs a signed approval, and `approval-helper.sh reconcile` returns NO_APPROVAL. A transient lookup failure turns into a permanent hold.

Expected:
- The start helper resolves authority the same way the standalone call does. Find which environment difference (sourcing order, admission/cooldown state, `GH_TOKEN`) makes the lookup fail.
- `api-failure` is "unknown": retry once, then fail closed without adding the containment label (or add it with a reason the next successful lookup removes automatically).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh` (start flow, claim before gate)
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh` `_linked_issue_author_allows_start`, `_linked_issue_trust_blocks_start`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority`, `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup_uncached`
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh` and the OpenCode plugin edit/write hook (refuse writes on gate-blocked branches)

## Verification

1. A test where the gate blocks start: a later edit attempt in the left-over worktree is refused by pre-edit, and a commit is refused by the hook.
2. A test where the permission lookup returns api-failure once and then write: start passes and no `needs-maintainer-review` label is added.
3. The existing tests `tests/test-full-loop-external-issue-author-gate.sh` and `tests/test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh` still pass.

title: npm-cache-helper: prints 'No cleanup was performed' after a successful clean/verify
body:
## Problem

`npm-cache-helper.sh clean --apply --confirm clean-npm-cache` cleared 387 GB but finished by printing:

```
npm cache: 6.5 GiB (~/.npm)
[SUCCESS] npm cache is below the advisory threshold
No cleanup was performed. npm remains the cache owner.
```

The last line is wrong after a successful clean or `verify`. An operator or agent reading the output could conclude that nothing happened and run the clean again.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/npm-cache-helper.sh:217`: `_npm_cache_status` always prints `No cleanup was performed...`. `_npm_cache_verify` (line ~238) and `_npm_cache_clean` (before and after the npm call) call it after mutating.

## Fix

Have `_npm_cache_status` take an optional mode argument. Example: `_npm_cache_status read-only` keeps the current line, and `_npm_cache_status post-clean` / `post-verify` prints `npm cache clean completed through npm.` / `npm cache verify completed.` The pre-clean status call inside `_npm_cache_clean` should not claim either outcome.

## Verification

- `npm-cache-helper.sh status` still prints the read-only line.
- `npm-cache-helper.sh clean` (dry run) prints no "completed" line.
- `npm-cache-helper.sh verify` ends with a "verify completed" line.

title: t19363: fix(worker-lifecycle): index compaction reservation lookups so journal mainte...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19363` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(worker-lifecycle): index compaction reservation lookups so journal maintenance stops refusing hook admission with database-locked

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Cut worker-lifecycle journal compaction from ~10 s to ~2 s, so it no longer holds the SQLite writer long enough to refuse tool-hook admission with `database-locked`. The second compaction query in `compact()` should look up the indexed `generation_admissions` table instead of a JSON copy of it that is rescanned for every candidate event.

## Why

- Workers fail on their first command. `BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable (database-locked); no write authorized` refuses even `gh issue view` and `git status`, so the worker ends with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`.
  - About 35 worker failure excerpts in `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts/` show it since 2026-11-13.
  - Four workers died together at 2026-11-24T21:10Z, on issues 32323, 32746, 32971 and 32994.
  - Interactive and bounded-operation sessions are refused too: 7 to 53 `database-locked` refusals a day in `~/.aidevops/logs/lifecycle-admission/*.jsonl`.
- Root cause, measured on a read-only copy of the live registry (89,386 events against a 100,000 cap):
  - `automatic_compaction()` (`journal.py`) runs inside every write connection (`storage.py` `connection()`), under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, once events reach 90% of the cap.
  - `compact()` takes 10.8 s. Query 2 accounts for 9.9 s of that.
  - `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows `CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY ... SCAN json_each`. The `reservations` CTE parses a JSON array of all 2,346 `generation_admissions` rows once per candidate event.
- Hook admission (`worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py`) allows about 7 s: a 2 s busy timeout per attempt, plus retries of 0.25 s and 0.75 s. The plugin kills the helper at 10 s.
  - When the hook itself is the writer that triggers compaction, the kill rolls compaction back. The next writer then repeats it.
  - Evidence: duplicate same-size `events-archive-*.json` files a few seconds apart.
- Every refusal window lines up with an archive write:
  - From 2026-11-24T21:08:46Z to 21:10:27Z the journal recorded no events. The next archive was written at 21:10:27Z.
  - The 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25 refusals match archive timestamps too.
- With roughly 12-16k events a day and about 1,000 archived per trigger, compaction fires about 15 times a day.

## How

- In `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/journal.py` `compact()`, when the `generation_admissions` table exists, have query 2 reference it directly:
  - `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generation_admissions a WHERE a.generation_id=g.generation_id)`;
  - `a.path=json_extract(e.payload,'$.source') OR a.generation_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(e.payload,'$.generations'))`.
  - `generation_id` is the primary key and `path` is UNIQUE, so both are indexed lookups.
- Schema-1 stores have no table. Keep an empty reservation set there, for example a CTE yielding no rows, so the SQL never names a missing table.
- Keep the eligible row set identical. On the live-store copy, the indexed variant ran in 1.26 s against 6.13-9.92 s and returned the same 27 rows in the same order.
- Change no policy: retention, the event types eligible for archiving, the archive-first write, tombstones and the lock sweep all stay the same.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/journal.py`

## Acceptance criteria

title: Automatic checkpoint post-transfer verification strands a never-launched continuation
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Automatic checkpoint continuation fails after ownership transfer and cannot compensate

## What

Diagnose and repair an automatic exact-head draft continuation that passes admission, writes a prelaunch lease and transfers issue ownership, then fails `checkpoint_post_transfer_verification_failed`. Its compensation also rejects the target, leaving an in-progress/self-assigned issue with no worker. Preserve every existing exact-head, trust, lease and human-hold safeguard. Do not recover by deleting coordination events, weakening predicates or fabricating a release.

## Why

Observed on deployed framework3.39.279 at06:05UTC November25,2026 in an owner-requested handoff on a private managed repository. Private repository identity, source hashes, paths and lease capabilities are intentionally omitted from this public issue. Use modeled regression data, not production credentials or mutation of that live claim.

## Verified evidence

1. Existing draft retained `origin:interactive` plus `origin:worker-takeover`; tracking issue initially available/unassigned with auto-dispatch. Trusted unedited handover comment was newer than unchanged PR head. Complete canonical brief was worker-ready, score5/no structural errors.
2. First bounded caller was interrupted before launch after posting claim/prelaunch. Local executor PIDs were subsequently absent; no ready lease or worker session existed. The full prelaunch expiry was respected, then ordinary `dispatch-claim-helper.sh check` returned1 (no active claim).
3. Fresh lower-cost standard model canary passed and the normal guarded dispatch facade was retried with a600-second caller budget. No timeout of that second call occurred.
4. Scanner at06:05:01 recorded prepared exact-head worker-owned takeover worktree while leaving owner worktree untouched.
5. New claim at06:05:08. At06:05:24 automatic orphan cleanup appended `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=claim_only_no_worker` for the older claim. At06:05:25 a prelaunch renewal for the newer claim was appended. Issue became in-progress/sole authenticated assignee.
6. At06:05:40 state persisted `analysis_complete=true`, `blocked_by=code`, `maintainer_attention=true`, `attention_reason=checkpoint_post_transfer_verification_failed`, `blocker_reason=checkpoint_post_transfer_verification_failed`.
7. At06:05:44 scanner recorded `restore skipped` because checkpoint claim/target no longer valid. Normal facade returned1/deferred and inner launch result13. No worker/ready/terminal evidence existed and capacity remained0active/1available.

The older orphan release's timing is evidence, not established root cause. Determine the actual rejecting predicate before changing code. Native wrappers currently suppress the verifier output at this boundary, limiting diagnostics. A separate earlier facade result claimed rc0/launched while its caller was interrupted; do not mistake that for durable worker launch evidence.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-automatic-checkpoint.sh` to fix only the reproduced claim/transfer/verification defect.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_admission.py` if the exact snapshot/event-identity predicate is responsible.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/checkpoint_admission_cases.py` to add a focused regression alongside existing admission cases.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` only for necessary safe compensation or bounded diagnostic evidence. Extract helpers rather than growing complex shell functions.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-automatic-checkpoint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_admission.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/checkpoint_admission_cases.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-automatic-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-compensation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` calls automatic claim then target verification; `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-automatic-lib.sh` builds the admission envelope and metadata check.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-automatic-checkpoint.sh` writes claims; continuation helper transfers issue assignment/status and compensates. Live issue recovery is not authorized by this bug brief.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_admission.py` owns snapshot/claim event identity; preserve existing serialized contract and model selection settings.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** source under `.agents/scripts/` is authoritative; installed agent mirrors are not editable source. Deployment requires existing authorized release path, not this issue's implementation authority.
- **Migrations/backfills:** no database migration or event backfill is required; `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-compensation.sh` must preserve append-only history and existing recovery state.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-compensation.sh` may restore only identity-bound never-launched transfer; unknown outcomes remain held. No manual claim deletion/expiry change.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/checkpoint_admission_cases.py` is the modeled fixture surface; discover its existing invoking test before edits rather than inventing a runner.

### Implementation Steps

1. Reproduce the event order with synthetic issue/PR data and exact deployed admission semantics. Isolate whether snapshot revalidation, oldest/newest coordination identity, current assignment, edit evidence or another gate rejects.
2. Preserve rejection of later human claims, changed head/brief/holds, foreign lease/device/session, real worker launch, unknown metadata and edits. An old release is never authority to terminate or replace a newer executor.
3. Apply the smallest source repair and meaningful existing-test regression. Verify both original available-issue admission and post-transfer fence, plus safe compensation when a never-launched transfer is rejected. Do not change routing, credentials, runner capacity or gate thresholds.
4. Run existing focused shell/Python checks and the existing admission test entry point. Record immutable evidence in the PR. Do not deploy, force-recover private issues or change live coordination history from this task.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** bind claim, snapshot, PR head, issue and current owner at every transfer boundary; no relaxed newest-event assumptions.
- **Migration/rollback:** no migration; revert source repair normally if qualification fails, preserving current deployed code and all live event records.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_admission.py` must continue rejecting unsupported/malformed legacy evidence, not reinterpret it as approval.
- **Idempotency/retry:** compensation may append an exact missing event only when its original fence still proves authority; retries must not fabricate a worker launch/release.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** distinguish never-launched, may-be-running and unknown outcomes; retain protected state with concrete diagnostic/action when uncertainty remains.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Use the existing test that invokes `.agents/scripts/tests/checkpoint_admission_cases.py`, plus `shellcheck` on changed shell files and Python syntax checks on changed Python. Confirm exact invocation from the maintained test source first.

```sh
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-automatic-checkpoint.sh .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** modeled event-order regression proves admission/transfer/compensation predicates; existing negative cases prove changed-head/claim/hold/edit boundaries; shell/Python checks prove only source validity, not live worker execution.
- **Broad verification trigger:** dispatch trust boundary is shared runtime infrastructure; run its established relevant characterization suite, but add no new test infrastructure/gates. Release/deployed smoke remains separately authorized.

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=maintainer-review-root-cause -->
## Maintainer review: verified root cause and fix direction

Reproduced with synthetic issue/PR data at `dfd9185c41` (no live data). The older release is the trigger, and the dispatcher posts it itself:

1. **Producer.** `_pcc_claim_checkpoint` (`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:216-229`) exports the per-PR `AIDEVOPS_PR_CHECKPOINT_SESSION` after the claim. That session key is fixed per PR (`_pcc_session_key`, `:350-357`). The function then renews prelaunch before it transfers assignment (`:239`). The renewal runs `cmd_transition` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:1459`), which calls `_fetch_claims`, then `_filter_orphan_prelaunch_claims` (`:529-585`; the issue is still unassigned), then `_post_orphan_claim_release` (`:642-670`). `_dch_orphan_release_valid` (`:674-701`) accepts the interrupted earlier claim because both its device and its session match. So the dispatcher appends `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=claim_only_no_worker` for the **older** claim inside its own new claim episode. The claim-race read at `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-automatic-checkpoint.sh:44` does not post this release, because the session is not exported yet and falls back to `issue-<N>`.
2. **Rejecting predicate.** `own_events()` at `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_admission.py:90` requires every coordination comment after the claim to be a single `DISPATCH_LEASE` line for this lease. Two callers reach it through `_dch_verify_automatic_checkpoint`, and both refuse at line 90:
   - post-transfer verification (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:245`);
   - the automatic compensation fence (`:773-781`, run with `AIDEVOPS_PR_CHECKPOINT_REQUIRE_PRELAUNCH=1`).
3. **Why it recurs.** No sweep releases an expired automatic claim before a new claim:
   - `cmd_sweep_pr_checkpoint_claim` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-checkpoint.sh:261-268`) only selects `checkpoint_mode == "revision"`.
   - Only revision claims enter the device ledger (`:175`).

   So any never-launched automatic attempt on an unassigned issue strands the next retry from the same device.

**Fix direction (producer side; `own_events` stays strict).** Every change stays inside the existing Files Scope:

- In `cmd_claim_automatic_pr_checkpoint` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-automatic-checkpoint.sh`), before `_dch_automatic_checkpoint_snapshot` freezes `before`, release this runner's own expired, never-launched `checkpoint_mode=automatic` claims for the exact `$session` on this device. Reuse the per-candidate fence from `cmd_sweep_pr_checkpoint_claim`, without editing that file:
  1. Read the claims with `_fetch_claim_marker_comments`.
  2. Check each candidate with `_dch_orphan_release_valid`.
  3. Skip the candidate if `_dch_session_has_live_executor` reports a live executor.
  4. Post with `AIDEVOPS_PR_CHECKPOINT_SESSION="$session" _post_orphan_claim_release ... "$comments"`.

  If posting fails, return 1 before any claim is posted. The release then comes before the new claim and is sealed into `history_sha256`, so the in-episode transition finds no orphan to publish. Mark the block `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
- Do not relax `own_events`: a later `CLAIM_RELEASED` must stay refused, even a same-runner release of an older claim.
- Bounded diagnostics: emit one allowlisted rejection reason on stderr from the admission or verifier boundary. Never include lease, nonce, device or session values. This lets the callers at `:246` and `:779`, which discard verifier stdout, log the cause.

**Regression (existing harness only).** Add these to `.agents/scripts/tests/checkpoint_admission_cases.py`:

- Event order *old claim → old release → new claim → renewal* is admitted at claim time, after transfer, and with `require_prelaunch`.
- The same release placed after the new claim is still refused. This is the same-runner variant of `test_later_coordination_and_edit_evidence`.
- Using the bash-stub pattern from `test_optional_claim_arguments_keep_nonce_position`, `cmd_claim_automatic_pr_checkpoint` posts the old-claim release before `_post_claim` and posts nothing for other claims afterwards. Extend that test's stubs to cover the new pre-claim read.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root rejecting predicate reproduced from synthetic evidence, not guessed from event timing.
- [ ] Legitimate unchanged exact-head transfer and compensation succeed under the correct ownership fence.
- [ ] Later human/foreign/ready-worker/edited/unknown/head-change cases remain refused.
- [ ] No live private claim mutation, forced unlock, credential copying, model config changes, deployment or policy bypass.
- [ ] Existing focused checks and admission regressions pass, with bounded diagnostic evidence that does not print lease capabilities.

title: perf(opencode-db): archive DBs never VACUUMed — 89% freelist, 33.9 GB reclaimed manually
body:
## What

OpenCode **archive** DBs (`opencode-archive.db`, global and per-project) build up free pages with no compaction path. On one host they reached 89% free pages. Archived-event expiry (`opencode-db-archive.sh --events-only`) deletes payloads but never VACUUMs archives, and `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh auto` / `maintenance-window` only compact active DBs.

## Evidence (2026-11-25, macOS host, disk at 98.7% full before cleanup)

`PRAGMA freelist_count` / `page_count` (4096-byte pages), measured read-only, then compacted manually with `OPENCODE_DB_PATH=<archive> opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh maintain --force` after `lsof` confirmed no holders:

| Archive DB | Free pages | Before → after |
|---|---|---|
| per-project archive A | 5,601,350 / 6,320,434 (89%) | 24.11 GB → 2.73 GB |
| global `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-archive.db` | 2,929,118 / 7,789,412 (38%) | 29.71 GB → 18.44 GB |
| per-project archive B | 206,359 / 361,432 (57%) | 1.37 GB → 0.60 GB |
| per-project archive C | 126,477 / 193,352 (65%) | 0.76 GB → 0.26 GB |

Total reclaimed: **33.9 GB**. `PRAGMA quick_check` = `ok` afterwards.

Code pointers:
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:880-881` — "Freed pages are reused by subsequent archive batches; this does not VACUUM archives." Reuse only helps if new archive writes catch up with expiry; after a large expiry pass they don't.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh` `_maintain_preflight` (~L1080) — refuses while *any* opencode process runs, even when the target archive file has no `lsof` holders. On always-on hosts archives can therefore never be compacted without `--force`.

## Related observation (not this issue's fix)

Active DBs with **zero** freelist were still 84 GB (global `opencode.db`) and 86 GB (one isolated project DB), and both are included in Time Machine. That points at live-data growth (compare closed #38491) rather than fragmentation. Check whether this needs its own issue.

## Proposed fix

1. After an archived-event expiry pass, or in `auto` / `maintenance-window`, inventory every `opencode-archive.db`. When the freelist is at or above `VACUUM_FREELIST_THRESHOLD` and `lsof` shows no holder for that exact file (plus `-wal` / `-shm`), run checkpoint → VACUUM → checkpoint → `quick_check`. Reuse `_maintain_vacuum_capacity` for the free-space guard.
2. For archive targets, gate on exact-file holders instead of the global opencode process count. Archives are not held open by TUIs.

## Reproducer

1. On a host with archived sessions, run `opencode-db-archive.sh archive-all --events-only --apply`, the scheduled path called by `storage-cleanup-helper.sh all --apply`.
2. `sqlite3 -readonly "file:<dir>/opencode-archive.db?mode=ro" "PRAGMA page_count; PRAGMA freelist_count;"`. The freelist grows and the file size never drops.
3. Run `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh auto` or `maintenance-window`. No archive DB is VACUUMed. `maintain` without `--force` refuses whenever any opencode TUI is running.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh`

## Verification

- Create a fixture archive DB, delete most rows (freelist > 50%), then run the new path with no holder: file shrinks and `quick_check` returns ok.
- Same fixture held open by `sqlite3` in another process: VACUUM is skipped with an explicit holder message and rc 2.
- `shellcheck` passes on both scripts.

title: fix(validators): serialized plugin test phase always exceeds the validator timeout under high host load
body:
## What

When the full-loop validator serializes the opencode-aidevops plugin suite under high host load, give it a time budget that a serial run can actually finish in, or route it to a gate that can. Today the serialized run is certain to time out.

## Why

`_validator_plugin_test_concurrency` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` exports `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY=1` when the 1-minute load is above 4 per CPU (GH#35499, GH#39133). `_run_scoped_node_checks` then runs `npm run test` with the same validator timeout as every other phase, which defaults to 300 s.

Observed 2026-11-25 on a 16-CPU Mac with load about 280 (17.5 per CPU) during `commit-and-pr` for GH#40283:

- default timeout: `TIMEOUT after 300s: npm run test (.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops)`
- `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT=900`: `TIMEOUT after 900s`, same command
- direct parallel `node --test tests/*.mjs` on the same tree and host: finished in 277 s (1512/1520 pass; the 8 failures were load-timing tests that pass serially or alone)
- `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` alone took 173 s serially

So the serial run lasts far longer than the default budget. The only remedy the message offers is to raise the timeout by hand or change the canonical project config. The plugin suite has no required CI check, so the existing defer-to-CI path cannot apply.

## How

Pick the smallest fix that keeps the suite enforced:

1. In `_run_scoped_node_checks`, when `_validator_plugin_test_concurrency` selects serial mode, scale that phase's timeout (for example `max(t, 2400)`, or `t * 4`), and print the effective value in the existing INFO line.
2. Alternatively, run only the affected test files serially (tests that import changed modules, plus changed test files) and the rest in parallel.

Do not weaken or skip the suite.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` — `_validator_plugin_test_concurrency`, `_run_scoped_node_checks`, `_validator_timeout_remedy`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-project-validators-shell-only.sh` — existing timeout/remedy cases (search `TIMEOUT after`)

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-project-validators-shell-only.sh` passes. Add one case showing that serial mode receives the larger budget.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` reports zero violations.
- Under a simulated high load (stub the load probe to return 1), the INFO line shows serial concurrency and the scaled timeout.

title: fix(plugin-tests): sqliteExec exit test fails with 'database is locked' because its verification read has no busy timeout
body:
## What

Make the verification read in `queued sqliteExec writes land on normal process exit (GH#39202)` wait for the SQLite write lock instead of failing immediately with `database is locked`.

## Why

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-runtime-events.mjs:664` runs `sqlite3 <db> "SELECT count(*) ..."` with no busy timeout. The driver process exits while its queued `sqliteExec` writes are still in flight in the detached `sqlite3` child, as GH#39202 intends. If that child still holds the lock when the read runs, the CLI returns `Error: in prepare, database is locked (5)`. `execFileSync` throws, outside the loop's retry-on-count logic.

Observed 2026-11-25 on a loaded 16-CPU Mac:

- On current `main`, run alone: `node --test --test-name-pattern="queued sqliteExec writes land" tests/test-runtime-events.mjs` fails every time with `database is locked (5)`.
- The same failure stops the full-loop plugin validator (`npm run test`) for unrelated plugin PRs, which blocks them from opening.

Product code already avoids this: `.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs:121` passes `-cmd ".timeout ${SQLITE_TIMEOUT_MS}"`.

## How

title: fix(plugin-tests): bounded-operation and process tests still fail at random inside the full suite under heavy host load

## What

Make the opencode-aidevops plugin tests below deterministic on a heavily loaded host. Each one passes alone but fails at random inside the full suite when the 1-minute load is 6–17 per CPU. Each failure stops the full-loop plugin validator (`npm run test`) for unrelated PRs.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 on a 16-CPU Mac running pulse workers, during `commit-and-pr` for GH#40283 and GH#40305. No changed file was imported by the failing tests.

Serialized validator run, load about 17/CPU (1519/1520 pass):

- `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` `helper-created process groups are contained on timeout and cancellation (GH#33514)`: containment `incomplete`, expected `owned_process_tree`. Passed 2/2 alone.

Serialized validator run, load about 6/CPU:

- `tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs:129` `tool passes bounded grace without changing the default and overdue progress is diagnostic`: `termination_cause` `post_exit_cleanup`, expected `null` (`:142`). Passed 3/3 alone.

Parallel `node --test tests/*.mjs` run, load about 17/CPU (1512/1520 pass):

- `start returns control and explicit progress reaches a private terminal receipt`
- `supervisor budget expiry cannot succeed when the manager timer is delayed`
- `tool passes bounded grace without changing the default and overdue progress is diagnostic`
- `helper-created process groups are contained on timeout and cancellation (GH#33514)`
- `uses the plugin repository directory when mutation tools omit workdir` (`tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`)
- `JavaScript waits for the live Python owner of the shared lock` (`tests/test-runtime-events.mjs`)
- `process listing redacts a credential-file value inside a provider command line` (`tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs`)

Prior work on the same class: GH#39971 (`post_exit_cleanup` on bare exit, `terminal()` deadlines), GH#35499, GH#39133, GH#34573. The `post_exit_cleanup` and `incomplete` containment results recur, so those fixes did not cover every path.

## How

1. Reproduce each case with `.agents/scripts/test-load-repro-helper.sh run --runs 20 --concurrency 8 -- node --test --test-name-pattern='<name>' tests/<file>.mjs`, run from `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`.
2. For `post_exit_cleanup` versus `null`: find out whether survivor draining after a bare exit classifies a slow-reaping child as post-exit cleanup. If so, the fix belongs in the classification in `bounded-operation-*.mjs`, not in the test budget.
3. For containment `incomplete`: check whether the process inventory in `process-start-identity.mjs` and the bounded-operation supervisor misses a descendant that starts late under load.
4. Fix the cause. Raise a per-test budget only with evidence that the assertion's timing really depends on host speed (see the GH#35499 rule).

title: quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh rejects same-major Node patch versions (exact .nvmrc match), blocking QuickFile MCP
body:
## Observed

`quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh` refuses to start the QuickFile MCP unless `node --version`
equals the `.nvmrc` value exactly:

```text
$ QUICKFILE_MCP_LAUNCHER_DRY_RUN=1 bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh
QuickFile MCP requires Node.js 24.19.0 from .nvmrc; got 26.12.0. Set NODE_BIN to the matching executable.

$ NODE_BIN=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin/node QUICKFILE_MCP_LAUNCHER_DRY_RUN=1 bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh
QuickFile MCP requires Node.js 24.19.0 from .nvmrc; got 24.22.0. Set NODE_BIN to the matching executable.
```

Homebrew `node@24` tracks the latest 24.x patch, and no nvm install exists, so on a
standard macOS setup there is no executable that satisfies the pin. The QuickFile MCP
cannot be connected, and `quickfile-helper.sh status` reports `quickfile-mcp: not found`
even though bearer tokens are configured.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh` (deployed lines 53-62) compares
`current_node != required_node` as strings. A patch-level difference within the same
major (24.22.0 vs 24.19.0) is rejected.

## Proposed fix

- Accept any Node.js with the same major version as `.nvmrc` and a version greater than
  or equal to it (or same major only), and keep the exact-match nvm lookup as the
  preferred path.
- Also try `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@<major>/bin/node` and `/usr/local/opt/node@<major>/bin/node`
  when `NODE_BIN` is unset and the nvm path is absent.
- Make `quickfile-helper.sh status` report the launcher's version refusal instead of
  "not found".

## Verification

1. `NODE_BIN=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin/node QUICKFILE_MCP_LAUNCHER_DRY_RUN=1 bash .agents/scripts/quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh` exits 0.
2. With only Node 26 on PATH it still refuses, naming the required major.
3. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/quickfile-mcp-launcher.sh` clean.
4. Existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-quickfile-rest-routing.sh` and
   `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-quickfile-mcp-registry.mjs` pass.

title: playwright-runtime: version bump leaves the new browser build undownloaded (launch fails until manual install)
body:
## What

After a framework update, the owned Playwright runtime (`~/.aidevops/runtimes/playwright`) resolved to `playwright@1.63.0` (Chromium build 1243, WebKit 2359), but the matching browsers were not downloaded. The browser cache only held the previous build (`chromium-1228`, `chromium_headless_shell-1228`).

Any script that loads Playwright through `playwright-runtime.mjs` (here, a project smoke test that falls back to the aidevops runtime) then fails at launch:

```
browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1243/...
```

The same smoke test passed about 3 hours earlier on the same machine, so the version bump happened in between, during routine framework updates.

## Workaround used

`node ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs install chromium webkit` (115 s, about 355 MB). The test then passed in both engines.

## Expected

When setup or update changes the pinned runtime version, it should also install the browsers that were present for the old version. At minimum, Chromium and its headless shell should be installed, as `installPlaywrightRuntime()` already does for a fresh install. Alternatively, `runtime-check` should report `ready: false` and setup should repair it.

## Where to look

- `.agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs`: `installPlaywrightRuntime()`, the setup idempotence check around `runtime-check` (`ready` computation), and `ensureRuntimePackages()`
- The setup or update path that bumps the pinned version (not identified here)

## Verification

Pin an older version and install it with its browsers. Then run the update path to the new pin, and confirm that the browser directories for the new build exist under `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/` and that `runtime-check` reports ready.

title: t19367: perf(pulse): size the prelaunch budget from observed prelaunch stage times so loaded runners stop aborting claimed launches
body:
## Task


The fixed 300 s prelaunch budget (`AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_PRELAUNCH_BUDGET_SECONDS`, set in `_dlw_begin_prelaunch`) adapts to observed prelaunch stage durations. Claimed candidates with a precreated worktree then reach spawn under host load, instead of aborting at the publication reserve after 7–8 minutes of ceremony.

## Done when

- [ ] With no env override and slow observed prelaunch samples, the budget rises above 300 s and never exceeds the cap or the remaining per-candidate watchdog.
- [ ] With no samples, or an explicit `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_PRELAUNCH_BUDGET_SECONDS`, behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Existing prelaunch publication-reserve cases pass.
- [ ] Runtime, after deploy: daily `pre_runtime_failure:prelaunch_*` count in `dispatch-stages.tsv` drops below 3 per 100 spawns.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` — `_dlw_begin_prelaunch` (around line 809). When `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_PRELAUNCH_BUDGET_SECONDS` is unset, use `max(300, ceil(p90 × 1.25))`, capped at `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_PRELAUNCH_BUDGET_MAX_SECONDS` (default 600). p90 is taken over recent successful prelaunch durations: the sum of `dedup.precreate_worktree`, `dedup.final_spawn_gates`, `dedup.final_ownership_fence`, `dedup.assign_and_label` and `dedup.worker_spawn` per launch. Alternatively, the `dedup.worker_launch_total` p90 minus its pre-`begin_prelaunch` stages; pick the simpler one that is correct and say which in the PR.
  - Read only the log tail (the pattern in `_dispatch_ceremony_reserve_seconds` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`, t19365: `tail -n 40000 | awk`).
  - An explicit env value keeps today's exact behaviour.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh` — add a case: a stages fixture with slow prelaunch samples raises the budget (capped); no samples keeps 300; an explicit env value wins.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- The deadline must never slide once set (the existing invariant in the `_dlw_begin_prelaunch` comment). Only its initial size changes.
- `_dlw_renew_prelaunch_lease` derives the lease TTL from the remaining budget, so a larger budget lengthens the prelaunch claim lease. That only affects takeover delay if the dispatcher dies. Keep the 600 s cap; check that `dispatch-claim-helper.sh transition prelaunch` accepts the longer TTL.
- The per-candidate watchdog (600 s, or adaptive `timeout_used_ms`) still bounds the whole candidate. If the budget can exceed `watchdog − pre-prelaunch elapsed`, clamp it there so the watchdog does not kill a spawn in progress. Verify against `_dispatch_with_timeout` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

Interactive session, Pulse throughput mission (parent GH#40108). Filed for worker implementation.

## What

The fixed 300 s prelaunch budget (`AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_PRELAUNCH_BUDGET_SECONDS`, set in `_dlw_begin_prelaunch`) adapts to observed prelaunch stage durations. Claimed candidates with a precreated worktree then reach spawn under host load, instead of aborting at the publication reserve after 7–8 minutes of ceremony.

## Why

Evidence from the macOS runner, `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` and `pulse.log`, 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-25:

- `pre_runtime_failure:prelaunch_reserve_insufficient` and `:prelaunch_budget_exhausted` occurred 6, 5 and 11 times on those three days. On 2026-11-25 that was 11 aborts against 95 spawns, about 10% of attempts that reached prelaunch.
- Each abort comes after the claim was won and the worktree was created. For example, two candidates in a managed product repository returned rc=2 after 497 s and 507 s. In both, the claim comment was deleted and the worktree discarded, so the next attempt repeats all of it.
- At load average 242 on 16 CPUs (desktop apps plus workers), stages after `begin_prelaunch` took: `precreate_worktree` 139 s (`git worktree add` 79 s), `final_ownership_fence` 47 s, `assign_and_label` 62 s. The publication check then needs 75 s more. This load is outside Pulse's control, so a fixed 300 s fails exactly when ceremony is already slowest.

## Tier

tier:standard. A bounded adaptive default in one function and a regression case in the existing test.

title: fix(validators): rerun failed plugin tests serialized and report flaky passes instead of blocking
body:
## What

When the full-loop plugin validator (`npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`) fails, rerun only the failed tests, serialized, up to 2 times. If every failed test then passes, report them as flaky in the validator output and the PR testing summary, and do not block. A test that fails again still blocks.

## Why

On a heavily loaded host (1-minute load 6–17 per CPU from pulse workers), every serialized plugin-suite run in this session failed on 1–3 bounded-operation timing tests that no changed file touched (GH#40309). Each run takes 10–12 minutes, so the plugin validator blocked unrelated PRs (GH#40283, GH#40305) for hours. CI does not run this suite, so the local validator is the only gate, and `--skip-hooks` is correctly refused for code diffs.

The framework already treats this case as non-blocking for script suites: `workflows/full-loop.md` says "`flaky` (a head failure that passed on a rerun; `--retries`, default 2) does not block; report it the same way, naming the suite." `reference/ci-gate-policy.md` design rule 5 says flaky findings become follow-up tasks instead of blocking unrelated PRs. This brings the plugin validator in line. GH#40309 tracks the root-cause flake fixes.

Evidence from 2026-11-25 (16-CPU Mac, plugin suite of about 1520 tests):

- Run 1, load about 17/CPU: 1 failure, `helper-created process groups are contained on timeout and cancellation (GH#33514)`.
- Run 2, load about 6/CPU: 1 failure, `tool passes bounded grace without changing the default and overdue progress is diagnostic`.
- Run 3, load about 14/CPU: 3 failures in `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` (drain, restoration timing).
- Run 4, load about 6/CPU: 1 failure, `dispose, session deletion, external signals and supervisor loss have distinct causes`.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`, `_run_scoped_node_checks`: on a non-timeout failure of the plugin test phase, parse the `✖ failing tests:` section of the Node spec output. For each failing test, take its name and its `test at <file>:<line>:<col>` location.
- Rerun with `node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-reporter=spec --test-name-pattern=<escaped name>…` over the location files plus the `tests/*.mjs` files that import them. Locations can be helper modules such as `tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs`, which only register tests when another test file calls them.
- Count a rerun as passing only if it exits 0 and prints `✔ <name> (` for every failed name. A filter that matches nothing must not pass.
- Do not rerun, and keep blocking, when the failure has no parsable failing-tests section, a location outside `tests/`, or more than 10 failed tests.
- Record flaky tests in the snapshot directory and expose them as `FULL_LOOP_VALIDATOR_FLAKY`. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` adds them to the PR testing summary, the same way it handles `FULL_LOOP_VALIDATOR_DEFERRALS` (GH#40064).
- Document the behaviour next to the validator-timeout paragraph in `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-project-validators-shell-only.sh` passes. New cases with a fake `npm`/`node`: a flaky failure passes and is reported, a repeat failure blocks, and an unparsable failure blocks.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts.
- With the real plugin, a known flaky test reruns and is reported as flaky instead of blocking.

title: fix: report unavailable macOS marker inventory as incomplete bounded-operation attribution
body:
## What

On macOS, report containment attribution as incomplete when the bounded-operation marker inventory (`ps axeww`) stays unavailable, instead of treating it as a successful scan with no marked processes.

## Why

Review finding on PR #40319 (GH#40309). `darwinOperationPids()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs` returns an empty `Set` when every marker `ps` attempt fails or times out. `markedProcesses()` then returns `[]`, and `recordSnapshot()` / `track()` in `bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs` cannot tell that apart from a scan with no matches, so `containment()` keeps `attributionComplete: true`. An escaped, reparented marked process that was never recorded through its parent chain could then stay alive while the receipt reports `owned_process_tree`.

This gap predates PR #40319: base `main` made one 1 s attempt and also returned an empty set on failure. PR #40319 adds a 5 s retry, which makes the failure rarer but does not report it.

## Reproducer

Unconfirmed at runtime; this was found by code reading. Reproduce by making the marker listing fail on macOS, for example by temporarily pointing `PS_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUTS_MS` at `[1, 1]` in a local branch. Then start a bounded operation whose command spawns a detached child that reparents to launchd before the first basic scan, for example the "detached test servers" fixture in `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`. The receipt keeps `containment: "owned_process_tree"` and the escaped child is never attributed. Expected: `containment: "incomplete"`.

## How

1. `bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs`: make `darwinOperationPids()` return `null` when the marker listing never succeeds, and an empty `Set` only after a successful scan. Make `markedProcesses()` return `null` for that case on Darwin.
2. `bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs`: have `recoverMarked()` / `recordSnapshot()` report an unavailable marker scan, and have `track()` set `attributionComplete = false`, matching the existing handling of a missing basic inventory (`if (!snapshot)`).
3. Keep periodic ticks without a marker scan unaffected (`createMarkerScanGate` returns `""`, so no scan runs).
4. Trade-off to weigh: on a heavily loaded Mac this reports `containment: "incomplete"` more often, the symptom GH#40309 removed from tests. Make sure `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` "helper-created process groups are contained on timeout and cancellation (GH#33514)" still passes under `test-load-repro-helper.sh` on macOS, or document why an honest `incomplete` is the expected result there.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs`

## Verification

- `cd .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops && npm test` passes.
- On macOS: `bash ../../scripts/test-load-repro-helper.sh run --runs 20 --concurrency 8 -- node --test --test-name-pattern='helper-created process groups|detached test servers' tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` passes 20/20.
- Linux behaviour is unchanged (`hasLinuxMarker` reads `/proc` and has no timeout path).
