title: fix(gh-failure-miner): do not open systemic CI issues for cancel-in-progress runs superseded by a later run
body:
## What

`gh-failure-miner-helper.sh` opens "Systemic CI failure" issues from check runs whose conclusion is `cancelled` even when the cancellation is a deliberate `cancel-in-progress` supersession and a later run on the same branch succeeded. This produces false systemic clusters that consume a worker dispatch each.

## Evidence

- A managed product repo's issue "Systemic CI failure: Enrichment Phase Closure (2 events)", signature `##[error]The operation was canceled.`. Both cited runs are `status: completed, conclusion: cancelled` on two different PR branches. A dispatched worker verified that the workflow uses per-PR `cancel-in-progress` and that a merged PR's head commit shows the check as success, so no repo defect existed. Observed on 2026-11-25 by the pulse supervisor with `gh run view`.
- `filter_failed_check_runs()` (`.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`, around line 640) lists `cancelled` as a hard failure. GH#18978 only collapses duplicate cancelled entries for one check name. It does not drop a cancelled-only group that was superseded.

## How

Reference pattern: the GH#18978 cancelled-dedup block in the same function and the `job_not_started` handling near line 1548.

Change: in or just after `filter_failed_check_runs()` and its caller `process_failed_runs()`, treat a cancelled-only check group as a non-failure when it was superseded: a newer run of the same check name (or workflow) on the same branch/PR completed after it, or the check's `head_sha` is no longer the PR head. Keep reporting `cancelled` when no newer run exists (genuine abort, runner loss) and when conclusions mix cancelled with failure. Use data `process_failed_runs()` already receives (`commit_sha`, `pr_number`) before adding any per-check network call.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`

## Verification

- Existing miner tests still pass (`git ls-files '*gh-failure-miner*'` for the suite) and `shellcheck` reports zero violations on the edited script.
- A fixture or dry-run replay of two superseded cancelled runs followed by a successful run yields zero events for that check. A cancelled-only check with no newer run still yields an event.

title: t19368: perf(sandbox): share one macOS process-table read across concurrent worker wa...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19368` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `feat` `priority:high` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(sandbox): share one macOS process-table read across concurrent worker wait loops

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Share one host-wide process-table read between concurrent `sandbox-exec-helper.sh`
wait loops on platforms without `/proc` (macOS), instead of every worker's poll
loop forking a full `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=` every 0.5 s.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25, 16-core macOS runner)

- Host CPU was saturated: load average 208-272, `top` 0.0% idle, ~49% sys.
- Reaped-child-aware rusage (`proc_pid_rusage` self+child) for the live
  `sandbox-exec-helper.sh run` wrappers: 16 wrappers at 0.08-0.09 average cores
  each over 76-3,963 s lifetimes, almost all of it reaped `ps`/`awk`/`sleep`
  children (e.g. 328.3 s total = 18.2 s self + 310.1 s child over 3,963 s).
  That is ~1.3 cores (~8% of the host) spent watching workers.
- One replayed poll iteration (`ps -o stat= -p` + full-table `ps` + the snapshot
  awk) costs ~71 ms CPU; the full-table `ps` alone costs 43-48 ms CPU (35-38 ms
  sys) for ~1,490 processes regardless of columns (`pid=,ppid=` costs the same),
  so the cost is the per-process table walk, not the `lstart` format (t19345
  already fixed the zone-file reload).
- Cost scales with workers x host process count, i.e. superlinearly with
  concurrency: every extra worker adds a poller and more rows for all pollers.
- Launch ceremonies on the same host averaged 266.7 s (n=116); CPU contention
  inflates every shell/API stage, so freed CPU goes straight to workers and
  admission.

## How

File: `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`, `_sandbox_snapshot_descendants_ps`
(the macOS fallback; the Linux `/proc` subtree walk is unchanged).

1. Add a host-wide cached table: a user-owned file
   (`${AIDEVOPS_SANDBOX_PS_TABLE_DIR:-$SANDBOX_DIR}/ps-table`) whose first line
   records the refresh time from `$EPOCHREALTIME`, followed by the existing
   `TZ=UTC0 LC_ALL=C ps -axo pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=` rows. Reuse it
   while younger than a TTL (default 500 ms, matching the poll interval).
   Otherwise claim an exclusive staging file (`ps-table.next`, created with
   noclobber; it doubles as the refresh lock and is reclaimed after 2 s if its
   writer died), append the read and `mv -f` it into place. Loops that find a
   refresh in progress reuse a table up to four TTLs old instead of duplicating
   the read; a first benchmark without that lock refreshed on ~50% of polls.
   The awk skips non-numeric first columns, so the header needs no parsing.
   Implemented: the awk indexes rows by parent and splits/joins columns only
   for descendants (identical output; ~16 ms -> ~10 ms per 1,600-row read).
2. Trust the cache only if the directory and file are owned by the current user
   (`-O`) and the file is not a symlink; otherwise fall back to the direct read.
3. Keep the cleanup-time final snapshot (GH#38861) on a fresh, uncached read so
   the last view before signalling is never stale. Keep cleanup identity
   revalidation (`_sandbox_snapshot_identity_matches`) unchanged: it re-reads
   each PID, so a stale table row can never authorise a kill.
4. Bash without `EPOCHREALTIME` (3.2) keeps today's direct per-poll read.
5. Optional kill switch: `AIDEVOPS_SANDBOX_PS_TABLE_TTL_MS=0` disables sharing.

Reference pattern: the existing single-read awk snapshot in the same function
(GH#38858 / t19079) and the TZ=UTC0 change (t19345).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- Same descendant rows are recorded as before (cached and direct reads feed the
  identical awk program).
- Cleanup's final snapshot bypasses the cache.
- With N concurrent wrappers, full-table `ps` invocations drop from ~2N/s to
  ~2-3/s host-wide; measured wrapper average CPU drops from ~0.08 cores.
- `shellcheck` clean; existing sandbox tests pass, especially
  `tests/test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh` and
  `tests/test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh
```

After deploy, re-measure live wrappers' lifetime self+child CPU.

title: t19369: fix(update): aidevops update exits 0 and syncs projects when agent deployment fails on the new-commit path
body:
## Task


`aidevops update` exits 0 and goes on to sync projects after agent deployment fails on the new-commit path. Make that failure stop the update and return non-zero, as the same-version path already does.

## Done when

- [ ] When agent deployment fails on the new-commit path, `aidevops update` prints the existing error, skips "Syncing Initialized Projects", and exits non-zero.
- [ ] Regression: a successful new-commit update still prints "Updated to version X (agents deployed)", syncs projects and exits 0; the same-version propagation case from GH#36413 still passes.
- [ ] `shellcheck aidevops.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh` reports no new findings.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: aidevops.sh` — in `_update_existing_install`, change the `_update_apply_remote ...` call in the `else` branch to `_update_apply_remote ... || return 1`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh` — add a case alongside the existing "propagates verification failure" case (around the `_update_already_current` checks near line 327-364): make `_run_update_setup_transaction` (or the stubbed setup) fail on the `_update_apply_remote` path and assert that `_update_existing_install` returns non-zero and `_update_finish` / project sync is not reached through `cmd_update`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `cmd_update` → `_update_install_framework` → `_update_existing_install` → `_update_apply_remote` → `_run_update_setup_transaction` (all in `aidevops.sh`). `cmd_update` already does `_update_install_framework ... || return 1` before `_update_finish`, so the one-line fix makes it skip project sync and return 1.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none beyond the return-code change; `_update_apply_remote` already returns 1 on fast-forward failure, HEAD mismatch and setup failure.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh` (sources these functions; covers the same-version propagation), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cmd-update-sha-drift.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A — no config is read or written by this path.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `aidevops.sh` is deployed by setup; no generated copy to regenerate.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `_run_update_setup_transaction` already handles bundle rollback; unchanged.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- `aidevops-auto-update` and release postflight may now see exit 1 where they used to see a false 0. That is the intended change; check that `aidevops-auto-update check` logs the failure and retries on its next cycle rather than aborting permanently (read its handling of `aidevops update` status before merging).

### Scope Boundaries

Out of scope, but useful context for diagnosis: the failure happened because a second `setup.sh` reclaimed the setup lock from a live auto-update setup (pid alive, age 1807s > `AIDEVOPS_SETUP_STALE_TIMEOUT_S` 1800s) while that owner still held `~/.aidevops/locks/runtime-transition.lock.d` (30s wait in `aidevops_runtime_transition_lock_acquire`, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-runtime.sh`). The owner was slow under host load ~230, not hung, and finished about 8 minutes later. Do not change lock timing in this task; file a separate issue if the worker finds reclaiming a live owner's lock is avoidable.

### Files Scope

- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`aidevops update` exits 0 and goes on to sync projects after agent deployment fails on the new-commit path. Make that failure stop the update and return non-zero, as the same-version path already does.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 while updating to v3.39.281. The update fast-forwarded canonical `main`, ran setup, and printed:

```text
[ERROR] Unable to acquire the runtime activation lock
[ERROR] Agent deployment failed: setup exited with code 1
```

It then printed "Synced 22 project(s) to v3.39.280" and exited 0. The deployed runtime stayed at 3.39.280. Callers that trust the exit code (release postflight, `aidevops update` run as a bounded operation, auto-update) treat a failed deploy as success. A rerun after the lock cleared deployed 3.39.281 correctly.

Cause: in `aidevops.sh` `_update_existing_install`, the new-commit branch calls `_update_apply_remote "$local_hash" "$remote_hash" "$current_version" "$update_output_mode"` with no `|| return 1`, then the function ends with `return 0`. Its caller is `_update_existing_install ... || return 1`, so errexit does not apply inside it and the failure is discarded. The same-version branch (`_update_already_current ... || return 1`) was fixed in GH#36413 (PR #36415); this branch was missed.

## Tier

tier:standard — a one-line propagation fix plus a regression case in an existing transaction test.

## Context & Decisions

- Found during the GH#40283 release (v3.39.281, PR #40328). The failed run's output id was `out_1795602095_4913ea80`; the auto-update setup log is `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log` around 09:44-10:27Z, and stage timings are in `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log`.

title: t19370: fix(pre-commit): positional-parameter ratchet must ignore $N inside multi-line single-quoted programs (awk/sed/jq)
body:
## Task


Make the positional-parameter ratchet in `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`
(`validate_positional_parameters`, the `_awk_script` near line 264) ignore `$N`
inside single-quoted strings that span several lines, such as multi-line
`awk '...'` programs. Today it strips single-quoted segments one line at a time
(`gsub(/\047[^\047]*\047/, "", line)`), so `$1`/`$2` awk field references on
the inner lines of a multi-line awk program count as shell positional
parameters.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the positional-parameter ratchet in `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`
(`validate_positional_parameters`, the `_awk_script` near line 264) ignore `$N`
inside single-quoted strings that span several lines, such as multi-line
`awk '...'` programs. Today it strips single-quoted segments one line at a time
(`gsub(/\047[^\047]*\047/, "", line)`), so `$1`/`$2` awk field references on
the inner lines of a multi-line awk program count as shell positional
parameters.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- t19368 / GH#40332 added a multi-line awk program to
  `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh` (`_sandbox_descendant_rows`). The
  commit was blocked with `NEW direct positional parameter usage ... (new: 3)`
  for inner awk lines such as `$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {` and
  `kids[$2] = kids[$2] " " n`. None of these is a shell expansion.
- The workaround was renaming the fields through `awk -v pid_col=1 -v ppid_col=2`
  and `$pid_col`. That is fine once, but every multi-line awk, sed or jq program
  in a shell helper hits the same false block. Authors are pushed toward
  workarounds or `--no-verify`, which skips every other validator.
- The same per-line stripping likely shapes the pre-existing counts. For
  example, `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` reports 10 pre-existing usages, so the
  ratchet baselines are inflated by awk bodies.

## How

File: `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`, `validate_positional_parameters`
`_awk_script`. The same script runs over staged and HEAD content, so both counts
change consistently and the ratchet stays fair.

1. Carry a single-quote state across lines (`in_sq`). While `in_sq`, drop
   everything up to the next `'`. Outside it, strip complete `'...'` segments as
   today. An unmatched opening `'` sets `in_sq` and drops the rest of the line.
2. Do not let apostrophes outside shell single-quoting open a multi-line quote.
   This is the design risk, because swallowing lines would hide real violations
   (false negatives):
   - Pure comment lines (`^[[:space:]]*#`) must be skipped *before* quote
     tracking when not `in_sq` (for example `# don't`).
   - `'` inside double quotes is literal (for example `"it's $1"` must still
     flag `$1`).
   - Heredoc bodies may hold apostrophes. Either skip quote tracking between
     `<<WORD`/`<<'WORD'`/`<<-WORD` and the terminator, or treat the body as
     plain text for `$N` detection; quoted-delimiter heredocs do not expand
     `$N`.
   - `\'` outside quotes is a literal quote.
   - Keep the `'"'"'` idiom working (close, literal, reopen).
3. Fail safe: if quote state is still open at end of file, do not suppress the
   lines after the opening quote. Re-scan them with the old per-line logic so a
   parsing miss cannot hide a violation.

Reference pattern: the existing ratchet scenarios in
`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-ratchet.sh`
(`test_positional_params_preexisting_pass`,
`test_positional_params_new_usage_blocks`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-ratchet.sh`

## Acceptance

- A staged multi-line `awk '...$1...$2...'` program adds 0 to the positional
  count.
- Bare `$1` in shell code after a comment containing an apostrophe still counts.
- `"... $1 ..."` with an apostrophe inside double quotes still counts.
- A heredoc body containing an apostrophe does not suppress later shell lines.
- An unterminated quote does not suppress later lines (fail safe).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-ratchet.sh` passes, with new
  scenarios for the cases above (the repository already has this ratchet test
  file; add scenarios there).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` clean.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-ratchet.sh
```

Spot check: for every `.agents/scripts/*.sh`, compare old and new positional
counts. Each change must be a decrease attributable to multi-line single-quoted
programs. List any increase in the PR and explain it.

title: Footprint gate: dead-owner interactive stamp on a canonical checkout reserves Files Scope indefinitely
body:
## Observed

On one managed repo, four `auto-dispatch` issues (one is `priority:high` + `security`) have been deferred every pulse cycle for about 48 hours with:

```text
[dispatch_with_dedup] (t2117) Dispatch deferred for #<candidate>: FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#<blocker> files=README.md)
[footprint-defer] event=wake ... wake_reason=blocker_coordinator_recheck
```

The blocker issue is maintainer-claimed (`status:claimed` + `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive`) and has had no activity since its claim on 2026-11-23. It has no open PR. `interactive-session-helper.sh status <blocker>` reports:

```text
worktree: <canonical checkout path of the repo>
pid:      <pid> on Mac (owner dead)
```

The coordinator recheck runs (`blocker_coordinator_recheck`), but the live rebuild still counts the claim as active implementation, so the overlap repeats every cycle.

## Root cause

`_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence()` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` (Evidence 3, around lines 903-914) treats an interactive-claim stamp as evidence whenever `[[ -d "$stamp_worktree" ]]`. It never checks whether the stamp owner is alive. The stamp recorded the **canonical checkout** as its `worktree_path`. That directory always exists, so a stamp whose owner is dead keeps the Files Scope reserved until the issue closes.

This stamp is also never cleared. The dead-stamp reaper `_isc_auto_release_dead_stamp()` in `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh` (around lines 417-439) is designed to keep `no-auto-dispatch` stamps until the issue closes, which correctly keeps the maintainer's manual claim. Together the two rules leave a permanent footprint hold, which GH#36817 / PR #36835 was meant to stop. That fix covered claimed issues with no stamp, not a stamp with a dead owner.

## Fix

In Evidence 3 of `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence()`, count a same-host stamp only while its owner is alive. Use the same command-aware liveness check the reaper uses (`_is_process_alive_and_matches "$pid" "${WORKER_PROCESS_PATTERN:-}" "$owner_argv_hash"`, see `_isc_examine_dead_stamp()` in `interactive-session-helper-scan.sh:479-527`). Alternatively, accept a dead-owner stamp only when `worktree_path` is a linked worktree (not the canonical checkout) **and** holds recoverable progress (`_isc_worktree_has_recoverable_progress`).

Keep these unchanged:

- Cross-host stamps, and stamps with an unreadable or missing PID, still fail closed (keep reserving).
- Unreadable or malformed stamps still keep the reservation.
- Evidence 1 (dispatch ledger) and Evidence 2 (open PR) are untouched.
- No labels, assignments or stamps change. A claimed `no-auto-dispatch` issue keeps its claim and only stops reserving files while nobody is working on it.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`

The first file holds Evidence 3 in `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence`. The second is the existing test, which gains a dead-owner canonical-path stamp case and a live-owner case.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` passes, including the new cases:
  - dead owner PID + existing canonical `worktree_path` → no evidence (the candidate is not deferred)
  - live owner PID → evidence (still deferred)
  - cross-host stamp → evidence (fail closed)
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` reports zero violations.
- After deploy, the pulse log no longer shows `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` for the four deferred candidates, and `[footprint-coordinator] event=footprint_stale_coordinator` appears for the blocker issue.

body:
**Task ID:** `t19371` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(full-loop): check platform regression evidence before the native macOS suites in commit-and-pr

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` runs the Platform Fix Regression Evidence
gate (`_commit_and_pr_platform_evidence_gate`, GH#39136) only after the native
macOS suites (`macos_checks_evidence`). Check the gate before those suites so a
missing `--regression-evidence` rationale fails in seconds, not after the full
macOS run. Keep the existing final gate as the authoritative check.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- t19368 / GH#40332 (sandbox change, title contains `macOS`, no test file
  changed) ran `commit-and-pr` on a loaded macOS runner. All macOS suites passed
  after ~31 minutes (`op_1795604312182`, 1,859 s elapsed), then the gate
  refused: `Platform Fix Regression Evidence would fail in CI ... Nothing was
  pushed.` The rerun with `--regression-evidence` must repeat the whole suite.
- The gate's verdict cannot depend on the macOS suites. It reads the title, the
  changed paths, and body prose outside `Files Changed`/`Testing`/`Runtime
  Testing`/`Regression Evidence` headings
  (`platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh` `_platform_trigger_text`). The suites
  only append to `summary_testing`, which renders under `## Runtime Testing`.
- Every macOS-sensitive PR (`macos_checks_sensitive` paths: sandbox, platform
  detect, git guards, setup, ...) whose title or summary names a platform term
  and changes no test hits this, interactive sessions and workers alike.

## How

File: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`, `_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata`.

1. Resolve `pr_title` (the existing `_compose_pr_title` /
   `_validate_explicit_pr_title` block) before `macos_checks_evidence`.
2. Add `_commit_and_pr_platform_evidence_preflight <pr_title>
   <comparison_base>` that builds a subset body from the same prose the final
   body renders in gate-visible sections (`## Summary` = `summary_what`,
   `## Decisions` = `summary_decisions`, `## Regression Evidence` =
   `summary_regression`). It then calls the existing
   `_commit_and_pr_platform_evidence_gate`. All of that prose appears in the
   final body under the same headings, so a preflight failure implies a final
   failure. It must never refuse a body the final gate would accept.
3. Call it before `macos_checks_evidence`. Keep
   `_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata` at or under 100 lines (the function-length
   gate in `linters-local.sh`).
4. Tests that `eval` `_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata` must also load the new
   helper: `test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh` (extract_function list)
   and `test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` (sed eval list).

Reference pattern: the existing gate call at the end of
`_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata` and the GH#39136 helper in
`full-loop-helper-commit.sh`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`

## Acceptance

- With a macOS-sensitive diff, a platform term in the title, no test change and
  no `--regression-evidence`, commit-and-pr fails with the existing gate error
  before any `macOS suite:` line is printed.
- With `--regression-evidence` (or a changed test), behaviour is unchanged: the
  suites run and the final gate passes.
- Existing suites pass: `test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh`,
  `test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`, `test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`.
- `shellcheck` clean on changed files.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh
```

title: t19372: fix(ci): platform regression evidence gate must not count the PR closing line as rationale
body:
## Task


`.agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`
`_platform_has_regression_evidence` accepts placeholder rationales such as
`n/a` because it counts the PR's closing line (`Resolves #NNNNN` / `For #N`)
and later lines as rationale text. Stop collecting rationale at closing or
reference keyword lines and at the signature marker, so the placeholder and
20-character checks see only the author's rationale.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`.agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`
`_platform_has_regression_evidence` accepts placeholder rationales such as
`n/a` because it counts the PR's closing line (`Resolves #NNNNN` / `For #N`)
and later lines as rationale text. Stop collecting rationale at closing or
reference keyword lines and at the signature marker, so the placeholder and
20-character checks see only the author's rationale.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- `commit-and-pr` renders `## Regression Evidence\n\n<text>\n\nResolves #<issue>`
  with no heading between the rationale and the closing line
  (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_build_pr_body`). The section
  parser stops only at the next Markdown heading.
- Reproduced with the checked-in script: title `fix: macOS sandbox`, changed file
  `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`, body `## Regression Evidence` /
  `n/a` / `Resolves #40332` → `platform regression evidence: passed (PR
  rationale supplied)`. The same body with `Resolves #123` fails only because
  ` n/a Resolves #123` is 18 characters (< 20). Any five-digit issue number
  turns `n/a` into an accepted rationale.
- The CI workflow `platform-fix-regression-evidence.yml` runs this script on PR
  bodies, so the defect weakens the required gate, not only the local
  pre-push check.

## How

File: `.agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`,
`_platform_has_regression_evidence`.

1. While in the section, stop (break) at:
   - a line containing `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`, matching `_platform_trigger_text`;
   - a closing/reference line, case-insensitive:
     `^[[:space:]]*(close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?|for|ref)[[:space:]]+#[0-9]+([[:space:]].*)?$`.
2. Keep the existing heading break, HTML-comment skip, placeholder list and
   20-character minimum unchanged.
3. Add pass/fail scenarios to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`
   using its existing `run_pass_case` / `run_fail_case` helpers:
   - fail: `n/a` followed by `Resolves #40332`;
   - fail: a short rationale (`manual`) followed by `For #40332`;
   - pass: a full rationale followed by `Resolves #40332`.

Compatibility: GH#40340 (`_commit_and_pr_platform_evidence_preflight` in
`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`) mirrors the final body's closing line
after Regression Evidence so the preflight is never stricter than the final
gate. After this fix both drop that line, so they still agree; no change is
needed there.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`

## Acceptance

- The three scenarios above behave as stated.
- Existing cases in `test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh` still pass.
- `shellcheck` clean on both files.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh
```

title: t19373: OpenAI pool add on OpenCode 2: single email prompt, accurate callback message, docs and routing tests
body:
## Task


Finish the OpenCode 2 OpenAI pool-enrollment fix in `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh` so that on OpenCode 2:

1. The account email is requested **at most once** per `oauth-pool-helper.sh add openai` run.
2. The user sees **one accurate message** saying callback enrollment was selected because `opencode` is version 2 or later, not the extra `OpenAI device login failed — falling back to callback URL flow` warning.
3. `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md` describes the automatic selection correctly.
4. `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` has focused cases for OpenAI add-mode routing.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-25
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer review of #40134)
- **Conversation context:** #40134 was fixed by PR #40161 (merged 2026-11-24, shipped in v3.39.278). Post-merge review found that the fix covered the main failure but left out the guidance, user-facing messages, and focused coverage from the approved resolution plan.

## What

Finish the OpenCode 2 OpenAI pool-enrollment fix in `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh` so that on OpenCode 2:

1. The account email is requested **at most once** per `oauth-pool-helper.sh add openai` run.
2. The user sees **one accurate message** saying callback enrollment was selected because `opencode` is version 2 or later, not the extra `OpenAI device login failed — falling back to callback URL flow` warning.
3. `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md` describes the automatic selection correctly.
4. `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` has focused cases for OpenAI add-mode routing.

## Why

Current `main` behaviour (verified against the default branch after #40161):

- `_cmd_add_openai_device` (`oauth-pool-add.sh:145-200`) calls `_add_prompt_email` at line 148 **before** the version check at lines 155-163. On V2 it then returns 1, and `cmd_add` asks for the email again at line 450. Without a prefilled email, a V2 user is asked twice. With a prefilled email, `Using email:` is printed twice.
- After the new V2 warning (line 161), `cmd_add` also prints `OpenAI device login failed — falling back to callback URL flow` (line 437). Nothing failed, so this reads as an error.
- `opencode.md:230-231` still says the default device flow invokes V1 `opencode providers login`. It does not mention that a V2 `opencode` now selects callback automatically.
- PR #40161 was verified only with `bash -n` and ShellCheck. It added no routing coverage.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The pattern is known and limited to one function pair plus one docs paragraph. The worker still chooses how to restructure the email prompt and helper extraction inside `cmd_add` (which is 75 lines), so an exact `oldString`/`newString` contract is not supplied.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh:145-200` (`_cmd_add_openai_device`) and `:408-482` (`cmd_add`)
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md:216-236` (V2 OpenAI enrollment paragraph)
- `EDIT: tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` (add `run_test_*` cases modelled on `run_test_set_priority`: disposable `mktemp -d` HOME, `HOME="$test_home" bash "$SCRIPT_PATH" ...`)

### Implementation Steps

1. Extract a small helper, for example `_opencode_major_version`, that returns the leading integer from `opencode --version` (reuse the parsing added in #40161, lines 156-159). Return empty or non-zero when `opencode` is missing or the output can't be parsed.
2. In `cmd_add`'s `device)` branch, check the helper **before** calling `_cmd_add_openai_device`. When the major version is 2 or more, print one `print_info`/`print_warning` line naming the detected version and that callback enrollment is being used, then fall through to the callback path **without** printing the "device login failed" warning. Remove the duplicate version check from `_cmd_add_openai_device`.
3. Make sure the email is resolved once: resolve it in `cmd_add` before the mode switch and pass it as the prefill to both `_cmd_add_openai_device` and the callback path, or use an equivalent approach. The callback path must not call `_add_prompt_email` again for the same run.
4. Keep every existing behaviour: explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_ADD_MODE=callback`, V1 device login, fallback to callback when V1 device login really fails (that warning stays for the real-failure case), and rejecting an invalid mode with exit 1.
5. Update `opencode.md`: when `opencode` itself is V2, callback is selected automatically. Keep the explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_ADD_MODE=callback` example. It is still **required** when enrolling into the V2 companion pool (`AIDEVOPS_OAUTH_POOL_FILE=.../opencode-v2/...`) from a host where `opencode` is still V1, because device mode would otherwise read V1 credentials. That breaks the "never copy the V1 pool" rule in the same section.
6. Add test cases using a stub `opencode` placed first on `PATH` inside the disposable HOME. Cover V1 (`1.x`) device success, V2 (`2.x`) auto-callback, explicit callback, V1 device failure falling back, and invalid mode. Stop the callback path at a controlled point, for example an empty auth code at `_add_read_auth_code`, so no network or OAuth exchange happens. Assert the email prompt count and the message text, not token exchange.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `oauth-pool-helper.sh add openai` sources `oauth-pool-add.sh` (module split in #21504). `aidevops model-accounts-pool add openai` and the `model-accounts-pool` OpenCode tool route here. No other caller invokes `_cmd_add_openai_device`; verify with `rg -n "_cmd_add_openai_device|AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_ADD_MODE" .agents/`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `_add_save_to_pool` (lines 98-129) writes the pool file. This task must not change what is saved, only how the flow is chosen and what is prompted and printed.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` (3 cases today, none for add routing); `.agents/scripts/tests/test-oauth-pool-diagnose.sh` (unaffected).
- **Schemas/config:** the `AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_ADD_MODE` values (`device`, `callback`) stay unchanged. No pool schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` copies `.agents/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/`. Nothing is generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. No stored state changes, and existing pool entries are untouched.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. The explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_ADD_MODE=callback` workaround from #40134 keeps working either way.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** unchanged. The callback server serialises login flows, and pool writes keep their existing lock.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. This is prompt and message routing only.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** V1 `opencode` must keep the device flow by default (#6553/#6573 explain why). Unparseable or missing `--version` output must behave like today: try device, then fall back.
- **Idempotency/retry:** rerunning `add openai` is safe, and the same email updates the existing pool entry as today.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a real V1 device-login failure still falls back to callback, now without asking for the email again.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `cmd_add` in `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh`. It is 75 lines now; adding inline version logic could push it past the 80-line warning, so put the logic in the new helper (step 1).
- **Target function:** `_cmd_add_openai_device` is 56 lines and shrinks when the duplicate check is removed.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the test suite proves acceptance criteria 1-4 and the regression guarantees. ShellCheck and the changed-file lint cover the shell and markdown edits. A real OAuth login is out of scope and must not be run with live credentials.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. Only one module, one doc and one test file change.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no native V2 credential import, no changes to other providers (Anthropic, Google, Cursor), no new test runner or harness, no live OAuth calls in tests.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh`
- `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md`
- `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a stub `opencode --version` printing `2.3.2` and no prefilled email, `add openai` prompts for the email exactly once and prints one message saying callback enrollment was selected because of OpenCode 2. It never invokes `opencode providers login`.
- [ ] With a stub printing `1.19.6`, the default mode still invokes `opencode providers login -p OpenAI -m "ChatGPT Pro/Plus (headless)"`. **Regression guarantee:** the V1 device flow is unchanged.
- [ ] When V1 device login exits non-zero, the `falling back to callback URL flow` warning is still printed, and the email is not prompted a second time.
- [ ] `AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_ADD_MODE=callback` never invokes `opencode`. An invalid mode still exits 1 with the existing error. **Regression guarantee:** the mode override behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `opencode.md` documents the automatic V2 selection and keeps the explicit callback requirement for V2-companion enrollment from a host where `opencode` is V1.
- [ ] `bash tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` and ShellCheck pass on the changed files.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh:44-60` — `_add_prompt_email`
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh:145-200` — `_cmd_add_openai_device` (V2 check added by #40161 at 155-163)
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh:428-451` — OpenAI mode switch and second email prompt in `cmd_add`
- `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md:216-236` — V2 private-pool enrollment guidance
- `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` — existing disposable-HOME test pattern

## Dependencies

None. #40134 and PR #40161 are already closed and merged.

## What

Diagnose why the **t2007 cost** circuit breaker fired on marcusquinn/aidevops#40029 after 5 consecutive worker failure(s), and ship the systemic fix that prevents the same class of failure on subsequent issues.

The breaker tripping is the SYMPTOM. This issue is for finding and fixing the ROOT CAUSE — typically a dispatch path bug, a worker setup race, an exit-classifier defect, or a brief-quality gap that caused workers to crash before reading the brief.

## Why

The existing breaker (`t2007 cost`) halts dispatch with `status:blocked` on the original. Filing this meta-issue converts the trip into a self-healing cycle: forensics → hypothesis → fix → original unblocks automatically.

The original (#40029) gets a `blocked-by` label pointing at this meta-issue and clears automatically when this meta-issue's PR merges (handled by `pulse-merge.sh::_unblock_circuit_breaker_meta_pr`).

## Hypothesis (starting point — verify first)

The most common root causes for `t2007 cost` trips are:

- **Brief is unimplementable as written** — refine scope or split the task; flag for `needs-decomposition`.
- **Hidden blocker** — missing dependency, environment issue, design conflict that cumulative worker attempts could not resolve.
- **Worker stuck in a loop** — model can't decompose the task; consider tier escalation OR scope reduction.
- **Wrong tier assigned** — downgrade a `tier:thinking` task to `standard`, or vice versa.
- **Breaker firing too early** — calibration problem in `dispatch-cost-budgets.conf`; investigate whether the budget is reasonable for the tier.

## How (mentor's guidance for the next worker)

Treat the original (#40029) as evidence, not as the work to do. The work is **here** — diagnose the systemic gap that lets workers fail in this pattern, ship the fix, and the original unblocks itself.

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh::_handle_post_merge_actions` — meta-PR merge cleanup that unblocks the original.

### Reference pattern

- Existing structural breaker paths in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` (no_work) and `dispatch-dedup-cost.sh` (cost) for the trip → `status:blocked` → comment flow that this filer hooks into.

body:
## Consolidation target: #29693

**Parent issue:** #29693 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,source:ci-feedback,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #29693 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#29693 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 29693 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`).    Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #29693, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

_Supersedes #29693 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

## Why

Issue #40349 is blocked by the large-file gate. Reading oversized worker lifecycle code consumes workers' implementation context. The earlier split merged via PR #29702 reduced the file to 1837 lines, but did not meet the current 1200-line headroom target. The live `origin/main` file is now 2031 lines (verified during consolidation on 2026-11-25), so historical completion does not satisfy the renewed requirement. Current default-branch anchors: attempt/runtime evidence helpers at lines 76–350; session/process helpers at 351–858; formatting/statistics at 859–1126; escalation/body-quality helpers at 1162–1975; verbose library sourcing at 2028–2031. Reconfirm anchors before implementation.
- New `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common-*.sh` modules: extract cohesive groups without semantic changes. No matching modules currently exist on the fetched default branch; the original file exists. Exact new module names depend on the chosen cohesive boundaries.

1. Start from current main, retaining the already merged PR #29702 implementation; do not recreate or undo its fixes. Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable. No historical runner-local checkpoint is binding.

title: t19374: perf(profile): bound profile README SQLite reads so the hourly routine cannot...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19374` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `bug` `performance` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(profile): bound profile README SQLite reads so the hourly routine cannot pin the llm-requests WAL

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Bound every SQLite read made by the hourly profile README routine, so one run can never hold a read transaction on `llm-requests.db` (or the OpenCode DBs) for hours.

## Why

Observed on a busy macOS runner on 2026-11-25:

- `sh.aidevops.profile-readme-update` (r908, hourly, launchd `ProcessType Background`, `Nice 10`) had been running for 14h22m. Its `sqlite3` child had been running `_get_model_usage_from_obs_db` against `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db` for 7h06m and had used 16 s of CPU, on a host with 0% idle CPU.
- That read transaction pinned the WAL: `llm-requests.db-wal` grew to 11.3 GB because no checkpoint could pass the reader's snapshot. After the stuck routine was terminated, the WAL checkpointed back to 0.7 MB.
- At normal priority the same queries are cheap. On the live 17.5 GB DB (2.23M rows), the all-time and 30-day aggregates each finish in 2–4 s warm, and a cold sequential scan takes about 16 s. The 7-hour runtime came from Background I/O throttling under host contention, not from query cost.
- The original brief suspected that the `filtered_requests` CTE was being materialized because it is referenced twice. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on SQLite 3.51 disproves this: it shows no `MATERIALIZE` step, and `SELECT *` and a narrow projection produce identical plans. No query rewrite is needed.
- `profile-readme-helper.sh` never sourced `shared-constants.sh`, even though `profile-readme-data-lib.sh` lists it as a dependency "via orchestrator". So `timeout_sec` was unavailable to the routine.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`

### Changes

1. `profile-readme-helper.sh`: source `shared-constants.sh` first. No variable or function names collide with the profile libraries.
2. `profile-readme-data-lib.sh`: add `_profile_sqlite_read <db> <sql>`. It runs `sqlite3 -readonly -cmd '.timeout 5000'` under `timeout_sec "${PROFILE_README_SQLITE_TIMEOUT_S:-300}"` and logs one stderr warning on timeout. It keeps the existing fail-soft contract: the caller gets empty output and falls back to its next source, which is the same path a locked or unreadable DB takes today.
3. Route all four SQLite reads through it: `_get_model_usage_from_opencode`, `_get_model_usage_from_obs_db`, `_token_totals_from_opencode_db`, and `_token_totals_from_obs_db`.

## Acceptance

- Old and new `_get_model_usage_from_obs_db` return the same model set and aggregates on the live DB for both the all-time and 30-day calls. The only allowed differences are rows written between runs.
- With `PROFILE_README_SQLITE_TIMEOUT_S=1`, the all-time call returns empty output within the bound and logs the warning instead of hanging.
- ShellCheck is clean, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` passes.

</details>

title: t19375: Discover Nix-profile Node installs in project Node selection
body:
<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Problem

`_project_node_bin` in `.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh` enumerates
candidate Node runtimes from fnm, nvm, volta, mise, Homebrew prefixes, the
nodejs.org installer (`/usr/local/bin`) and `n`. It has no candidate path for
Nix, so on a NixOS host the only discoverable Node is the one already on PATH
from the system profile.

Observed consequence on a NixOS host (2026-11-25): every headless worker for a
repository pinned to Node 26.13.1 failed pre-launch in under 1 second with
`project_node_environment_failure`. `worker-activity-helper.sh summary` recorded
7 such failures in 24 hours across conflict-repair and ci-repair sessions.
Reproduced directly:

```
_project_node_bin <worktree> .
ENVIRONMENT FAILURE: node v24.22.3 does not satisfy engines
  "26 and >=26.0.0 <27.0.0 ..." (root/scope requirements; ...).
Install a matching Node or select it with fnm, nvm, volta, mise, Homebrew node
or node@<major>, the nodejs.org installer, or n; then rerun.
```

`nix eval --impure --raw --expr '(import <nixpkgs> {}).nodejs_26.version'`
returns `26.13.1` on the same host, so a matching runtime is installable but a
Nix install would still be undiscoverable: `nix profile install` links into
`~/.nix-profile/bin` (and `~/.local/state/nix/profiles/profile/bin`), and NixOS
hosts have no nix-ld, so the fnm/nvm/volta tarball managers the message
recommends cannot run downloaded Node binaries at all.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh`

### Change notes

In `.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh`, add Nix candidate paths to the
`candidates+=(...)` block in `_project_node_bin` (the `shopt -s nullglob`
section), and treat the Nix profile `bin` as a shared multi-tool directory so
`_project_node_private_bin` links only the Node toolchain (same GH#39156
reasoning as `/usr/local/bin`). Extend the environment-failure message's
installer list to name Nix.

In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh`, extend the existing
hermetic fixture pattern (see the `AIDEVOPS_NODE_BREW_PREFIXES` cases) to cover
a Nix-style profile layout.

Candidate paths to consider, newest-generation first:
`$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/node`,
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/nix/profiles/profile/bin/node`,
`/nix/var/nix/profiles/per-user/$USER/profile/bin/node`,
`/run/current-system/sw/bin/node`. Keep an override hook equivalent to
`AIDEVOPS_NODE_BREW_PREFIXES` so the new discovery stays testable hermetically.

## Reference pattern

`_project_node_private_bin` (`.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh`) already
solves exactly this shape for Homebrew and `/usr/local`: a shared bin directory
is never returned directly, only a private directory symlinking
`node npm npx corepack`. Nix profile bins are shared in the same way — they also
carry `git`, `gh`, `jq` and `python3` on this host — so they must go through the
same indirection and must not reorder the worker PATH.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh` passes, including the
  new Nix fixture case.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh` reports zero violations.
- With a Nix-installed `nodejs_26` present, `_project_node_bin <repo> .` prints a
  private bin directory whose `node --version` satisfies the repository's
  `engines.node` and `.nvmrc` pin, and PATH order for `git`/`gh`/`jq`/`python3`
  is unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` passes.

## Out of scope

Installing Node 26 on any specific host, and any change to how
`_project_node_requirement` parses pins.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

title: t19376: perf(headless): disable OpenCode fff file index for headless workers so workt...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19376` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `performance` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(headless): disable OpenCode fff file index for headless workers so worktree churn stops costing up to a core per worker

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Set `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1` for headless worker OpenCode runs. Each worker then uses OpenCode's ripgrep file-search backend instead of the native fff index and its background file watcher.

## Why

Observed on a 16-core macOS runner on 2026-11-25, with load averages of 65–113:

- 3 of 6 live `opencode run` workers had a lifetime CPU share of 0.66–0.90 cores (4–6.5 CPU-minutes in 5–7.5 minutes). The other 3 used 0.03–0.07. All hot workers were in worktrees of one large application repository (49,870 tracked files) while package installs and builds ran there. Each worker held about 1.3 GB RSS.
- A 3 s `sample` of the hottest worker put the on-CPU stacks in `fff_search::watch::background_watcher` → `FileSync::find_file_index`, and in `git_status_for_paths` → `git_status_list_new` → `git_diff_index_to_workdir` → `git_pathspec__match` → `dowild`/`__tolower`/`git__strcasecmp`, plus `read`/`open`/`stat`. fff re-runs a libgit2 status pass over the 50k-entry index on each watcher batch, so worktree file churn becomes continuous CPU.
- In OpenCode 1.19.6, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF` selects the v2 `FileSystem/Search` layer (`Kl = OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF || !Gl() ? Wl : zl`). The fff layer's `grep` runs with `timeBudgetMs: 1500`, so on a saturated host a worker's grep results can be silently truncated. The fallback layer runs live ripgrep for every `glob` and `grep`. Only its fuzzy `find`, which feeds the TUI file picker, reads a startup file list.
- A/B on a 9,953-file repo with `opencode debug file search`: same result, system CPU 1.06 s → 0.49 s, peak RSS 768 MB → 568 MB.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`

### Changes

1. Add `_invoke_opencode_disable_fff` next to `_invoke_opencode_disable_snapshots`, following the GH#38491 pattern. In the launch subshell, export `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1` unless the caller already set `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF` or set `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_OPENCODE_FFF=1` to opt out.
2. Call it from `_invoke_opencode_prepare_child_command`, beside the snapshot call. The worker sandbox already passes `OPENCODE_*` through (`build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`). Triage roles keep their explicit allowlist and are unchanged.

Interactive sessions are not affected. The TUI file picker still uses fff.

## Acceptance

- A worker launched after deployment has `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1` in its `opencode run` environment, and a 3 s `sample` of it shows no `fff_search` frames.
- In a comparable later window, the mean lifetime CPU share of `opencode run` workers is below the 0.34-core baseline (n=6), and no worker sits above 0.5 cores in fff frames.
- With `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_OPENCODE_FFF=1`, the flag is not exported.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed file.

</details>

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #40349 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #40349

**Parent issue:** #40349 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Circuit-breaker meta: diagnose t2007 cost trip on marcusquinn/aidevops#40029
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,pulse,tier:thinking,origin:worker,framework,consolidation-in-progress,circuit-breaker-meta,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #40349 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#40349 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 40349 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Tier (t19356):** copy the parent's `tier:*` label only when a maintainer set it. If the parent's tier was raised by a `Cascade Tier Escalation` comment, use the tier from before that escalation. Escalation is evidence about the parent's failed run, not about the consolidated spec, so the successor must earn `tier:thinking` through its own repeated failures.

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #40349, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 40349 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 40349 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 40349 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 40349 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/40349" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #40349 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #40349.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @vladimirdulov

title: t19377: fix(issue-sync): make refresh-body print why it refused instead of exiting 1 silently
body:
## Task


Make `issue-sync-helper.sh refresh-body` print why it refused instead of exiting 1 with no output.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make `issue-sync-helper.sh refresh-body` print why it refused instead of exiting 1 with no output.

## Why

Observed twice on 2026-11-25: `issue-sync-helper.sh refresh-body <N> --repo <owner/repo> --body-file <brief> --dry-run` on an open interactive issue claimed only by the caller exited 1 after about 20 s and printed nothing. The issue carried `status:in-review`, which `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` applies. `_refresh_policy` (`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-refresh.sh:128-135`) refuses `status:queued`, `status:in-progress` and `status:in-review` whoever holds the claim. GH#32652 made that refusal deliberate, because a worker may be reading the body. The refusal path at lines 80-83 writes only an audit receipt and returns 1, so the caller cannot tell a policy refusal from a crash or a missing permission, and the session gave up on the refresh. Other `|| return 1` exits in `cmd_refresh_body` (lines 78, 84-98) are silent in the same way.

The refusal policy stays as it is. This task only reports the reason.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-refresh.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-refresh-body.sh`

### Changes

1. In `_refresh_policy`, or a small `_refresh_policy_reason` helper beside it, find the first failing condition and print it with `print_error` before returning 1. Use one line naming the cause and the next step:
   - invalid state → `Refresh refused: issue state could not be validated`
   - not OPEN → `Refresh refused: issue #N is <STATE>`
   - non-self claim → `Refresh refused: issue #N is claimed by <login>`
   - status label → `Refresh refused: issue #N has <label> (a worker may be reading the body); retry after the label clears`
   Keep the existing `_refresh_audit blocked` calls. Do not change which states are refused.
2. Give every remaining bare `return 1` in `cmd_refresh_body` a `print_error` naming the step that failed (for example the empty `self_login` at line 78, temp-file creation, tail extraction and hashing). Follow the existing `print_error "Refresh requires maintainer authority"` style.
3. In the test, which stubs `print_error` to stderr at line 13, capture stderr for the CLOSED case (line 49) and the `status:queued` case (line 51). Assert each contains its reason line. Use the file's existing `if cmd ...; then exit 1; fi` pattern.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-refresh-body.sh` prints PASS, and the CLOSED and `status:queued` cases assert a non-empty reason on stderr.
- Running `refresh-body ... --dry-run` against an open issue labelled `status:in-review` exits 1 and prints the `status:in-review` reason line.
- Refused states and exit codes are unchanged: dry-run with a diff still returns 2, and a no-op still returns 0.
- ShellCheck is clean on both files.

</details>

title: hostinger.md: get a new Web/Cloud plan's server IP before any real domain points at it
body:
## What

Add a short section to `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` (under "Configuration", before "Lifetime SSL behind Cloudflare") on how to get a brand-new Web or Cloud plan's server IP before any real domain points at it.

## Why

Operators moving WordPress sites from another host to a new Hostinger plan report that hPanel shows no server IP until a website exists. Every DNS cutover needs that IP: the DNS-only A record for the first Lifetime SSL issue ("Lifetime SSL behind Cloudflare") and private `curl --resolve` tests before the switch. The guide currently assumes the origin IP is already known, for example from an existing Cloudflare A record.

## Evidence (Hostinger OpenAPI spec, read 2026-11-25)

- `POST /api/hosting/v1/orders/{order_id}/onboardings` ("Start website setup"): "When the order has no hosting account yet, the setup creates one first, in the datacenter given by `datacenter_code`"; "Omit `domain` to set the website up on a generated temporary free subdomain"; `datacenter_code` is "Ignored when the order already has a hosting account", so **the first setup fixes the account's datacenter**.
- `GET /api/hosting/v1/datacenters?order_id=<id>` lists the datacenters available to the order.
- `GET /api/hosting/v1/onboardings?domain=<domain>`: poll every 10–15 s until `status: completed`; while `running`, other endpoints can return 404/409.
- `POST /api/hosting/v1/websites` is deprecated in favour of onboardings.
- `GET /api/hosting/v1/websites` has no IP field for Web/Cloud plans. Only the Agency-plan website schema and the VPS schema carry `ip_address`/`ipv4`.
- The guide already notes `hostname -I` is empty on the host ("Per-site PHP version over the API").

## How

Document this sequence:

1. Owner buys the plan. If hPanel's purchase flow asks for a website, choose skip or a temporary domain, never a live domain.
2. List datacenters for the order, confirm one with the owner, then start the first website setup **without** `domain` and with that `datacenter_code`. This creates the hosting account and server on a temporary free subdomain without touching live DNS. A not-yet-launched site makes a good first tenant.
3. Read the server IP in hPanel (website dashboard or plan details). Do not take it from the temporary domain's public DNS (it may point at Hostinger's CDN), from `hostname -I`, or from the server's outgoing address.
4. Verify it privately: place a marker file on the temporary site and check that `curl -sk --resolve <temp-domain>:443:<IP> https://<temp-domain>/<marker>` returns it. Keep the IP out of notes and issues.

Optionally, add a read-only `hostinger-helper.sh datacenters --order <id>` subcommand. Not required.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `hostinger.md` has the section, with the four steps above and the "first setup fixes the datacenter" warning.
- [ ] The text cites the endpoints by path and method and matches the current OpenAPI spec (`curl -sS https://developers.hostinger.com/openapi/openapi.json | jq '.paths["/api/hosting/v1/orders/{order_id}/onboardings"].post.description'`).
- [ ] markdownlint passes on the file; the AGENTS.md size ratchet is unaffected (the change lives in a service doc).

## Files

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

title: t19378: fix(cli): recover deleted working directory before forking to stop getcwd noise
body:
## Task


`aidevops` commands run from a deleted working directory print dozens of
`shell-init` / `job-working-directory` / `chdir: error retrieving current directory: getcwd`
lines. `sudo aidevops approve issue N owner/repo` printed more than 200 such lines around its
prompt and result, which hid the confirmation prompt and the outcome.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`aidevops` commands run from a deleted working directory print dozens of
`shell-init` / `job-working-directory` / `chdir: error retrieving current directory: getcwd`
lines. `sudo aidevops approve issue N owner/repo` printed more than 200 such lines around its
prompt and result, which hid the confirmation prompt and the outcome.

## Why

Root cause: the invoking shell's cwd (a managed temp directory under
`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/`) had been removed. Bash prints a getcwd error once at every
child Bash startup (`shell-init`), and every forked job adds another (`job-working-directory`).
Neither the wrapper (`bin/aidevops`) nor the CLI (`aidevops.sh`) recovers the cwd, so each helper,
subshell and `gh` or `jq` fork repeats the noise. The approval still succeeded, so the problem is
noise, not correctness, but the noise buries security-relevant prompts.

Reproduction: create a directory, `cd` into it, `rmdir` it, then run
`bash ~/.aidevops/agents/aidevops.sh approve --help`. This gave 9 getcwd lines for help output
alone. The full approval flow forks hundreds of times.

## How

- `bin/aidevops` and `aidevops.sh`: right after `set -euo pipefail`, before any fork, check
  `builtin pwd -P`. If it fails, `builtin cd` to `$HOME` (or `/`) and print one `[WARN]` line.
  Builtins only, so the guard itself adds no noise.
- Children then inherit a valid cwd. At most the top-level Bash's own `shell-init` line remains,
  and it can't be suppressed.

## Files Scope

- `bin/aidevops`
- `aidevops.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running the reproduction above prints at most 1 getcwd line plus one warning, down from 9 or more.
- [ ] Commands in a valid cwd behave exactly as before. The guard is a no-op there.
- [ ] `shellcheck bin/aidevops aidevops.sh` is clean.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck bin/aidevops aidevops.sh
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>
