title: t19379: fix(ci-wait): treat a cancelled check with a same-name pass on the PR head as superseded in gh-checks-wait-helper --all
body:
## Task


Make `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --all` treat a cancelled check run as superseded when the same workflow and check name already passed on the same PR head. Today it fails the wait after the 180 s cancel grace.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --all` treat a cancelled check run as superseded when the same workflow and check name already passed on the same PR head. Today it fails the wait after the 180 s cancel grace.

## Why

Observed on 2026-11-25 (PR #40361, head `eb6292833c`): `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait 40361 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --all` ended with `FAIL: required checks reached a terminal failure` / `gate / review-bot-gate: cancel` while 56 checks passed and nothing was pending.

The cause is the Review Bot Gate concurrency in `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml`. All events share `group: review-bot-gate-<PR number>` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, and GitHub keeps one pending run per group:

- 14:33:09 `pull_request` run: `gate / review-bot-gate` success on the PR head.
- 14:39:53 CodeRabbit posted a review and an inline comment. The `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment` runs queued on the PR head, then were cancelled without a runner (check runs 139283297759 and 139283299394).
- 14:39:57 CodeRabbit's `issue_comment` run 45636522460 in the same group superseded them and succeeded. GitHub attaches `issue_comment` check runs to the default-branch SHA (`6d0e386558`, `main`), so the successor never appears on the PR head.

The PR head therefore keeps an earlier pass plus cancelled entries whose successor can never become visible there. The gate's real verdict is the `review-bot-gate` commit status on the head, which passed. This is not one PR's problem: 5 of the last 20 `pull_request_review` runs of Review Bot Gate across PRs were `cancelled`. `--all` is the mode recommended by the `gh pr checks --watch` refusal in `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh:96` and by `.agents/workflows/error-feedback.md:28`, so every session and worker that follows that advice gets a false failure after a bot review and spends time diagnosing a green PR. The merge path's `_merge_admin_fallback_required_checks_clear` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:929`) uses required-only mode and is not affected.

The existing cancel tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:482-608`) model a successor that replaces the cancelled entry in a later read. They never model the live shape, where a same-name pass and a cancel coexist in one read.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`

### Changes

1. Next to `only_cancelled_failures` (`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:623`), add a jq filter that removes `cancel` entries whose `(workflow, name)` pair also has a `pass` entry in the same read for the same head. Apply it to the check list before the failure test in the classifier (`:609-613`) and before `apply_cancel_grace` (`:1042`), so such a read classifies as `success` and the transition/heartbeat output still lists both entries.
2. Keep every other outcome authoritative. A same-name `fail` or `pending` entry, or a cancel with no passing sibling, behaves exactly as today: the GH#35830 grace, the GH#38537 hold while other checks are pending, and terminal after grace.
3. Add fixtures following the existing `write_fixture` / `run_fixture_wait` pattern:

   - `Gate` pass plus `Gate` cancel plus `Test` fail → exit 1, reporting `Test: fail`

title: t19384: fix(release): recover squash merges with missing PR association via GH# task reference
body:
## What

Release snapshots fail closed when GitHub drops a squash merge's commit-to-PR association (GH#38932). The fallback added for that case only reads a `(#N)` hint in the commit subject.

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` always passes a validated `--subject` with no `(#N)` suffix, for example `GH#40373: test(checkpoint): ...`. So every full-loop squash merge is unrecoverable when the association is missing.

Observed: PR #40378 merged at `34bd404936` during a GitHub 502. REST `commits/{sha}/pulls` and GraphQL `associatedPullRequests` were both empty. `aidevops release patch 40372 incremental` then failed with:

`release-snapshot: commit 34bd404936... has no merged PR association and no verified subject PR hint`

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh`

### Changes

1. **Prevention:** in `_merge_resolve_squash_subject` (`full-loop-helper-merge.sh`), append ` (#<pr>)` to the validated squash subject unless it already ends with `(#<digits>)`. This matches GitHub's default squash subject.
2. **Recovery:** in `_release_snapshot_hinted_record` (`release-snapshot-helper.sh`), also derive candidate PRs from `GH#<n>` references in the subject. Use that issue's GraphQL `closedByPullRequestsReferences`. Each candidate passes the existing check: the PR is `MERGED`, has the release base branch, and its `mergeCommit.oid` equals the commit. Two distinct verified candidates still fail closed. Read failures fail closed.
3. Extend `test-release-snapshot-helper.sh` with the issue-reference case and its forged/direct-push negative.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh` passes.
- `shellcheck` passes on the changed scripts.
- `aidevops release patch 40372 incremental` resolves `34bd404936` as PR #40378.

title: t19385: fix(gh-wrappers): fall back to REST on transient GraphQL errors for issue/PR create
body:
## What

`gh_create_issue` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`, around line 867) runs native `gh issue create`. It retries via REST (`_rest_issue_create`) only when `_rest_should_fallback` reports that the GraphQL quota is exhausted. A transient GraphQL server error with quota left fails the create outright.

`claim-task-id.sh` then reports `Issue creation failed for tNNN (non-fatal — ID is secured)` and prints `ref=none`. The task ID is spent and no issue exists. Callers often miss the warning in truncated output.

Observed twice in one session on 2026-11-25:

- t19383: issue creation output was truncated, and no issue was ever created.
- t19384: `[WARN] Failed to create GitHub issue: GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query on 2026-11-25T16:04:40Z`. Recovered manually with REST as #40379.
- Five minutes later, `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 40379` failed at PR creation with the same `GraphQL: Something went wrong` error. It left `LIFECYCLE_STATE=PUSHED_PR_PENDING`. The PR create path (`_rest_pr_create` and its caller) has the same quota-only fallback gate. Cover it with the same classifier and adopt-existing-PR check, using the head-branch lookup `pulls?head=owner:branch`.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` (`gh_create_issue`)
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` (add a transient GraphQL error classifier next to `_rest_should_fallback`)
- Existing REST-fallback tests: `rg -l "_rest_issue_create" .agents/scripts/tests`

### Changes

1. Classify transient GraphQL failures from `gh issue create` stderr. Match `GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query`, HTTP 502/503/504, and `GraphQL: ... timeout`. Treat these as REST-fallback eligible even when quota remains. Auth, validation and 4xx errors stay fatal.
2. Issue create is not idempotent. Before the REST retry, search for an open issue with the exact same title created in the last few minutes, using a REST `search/issues` or `issues?creator=` read. If one exists, adopt it instead of creating a duplicate. This covers a GraphQL mutation that succeeded server-side but reported failure.
3. Keep the existing quota-exhausted path unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A stubbed `gh issue create` that fails with `GraphQL: Something went wrong...` while quota is healthy produces exactly one REST create, and `gh_create_issue` returns 0 with the issue URL.
- When a same-title issue already exists after the failure, it is adopted and no REST create happens.
- Auth and validation failures still fail without any REST write.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed files.

title: t19381: fix(worktree-deps): fail fast on pnpm hoisted node-linker instead of walking ...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19381` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `bug` `performance` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(worktree-deps): fail fast on pnpm hoisted node-linker instead of walking every workspace member

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Reject pnpm `nodeLinker: hoisted` layouts up front in the worktree dependency
restore validator, with a named reason, instead of walking every workspace member
and failing late with `incomplete-package-inventory`.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- t19357 (GH#40257, PR #40260) added per-member pnpm workspace restore. The
  validator assumes pnpm's isolated layout: every importer dependency is linked
  in the member's own `node_modules`.
- A managed monorepo with `nodeLinker: hoisted` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has
  flat real directories in the root `node_modules` (1,857 entries) and almost
  nothing in member `node_modules`. A read-only diagnostic against its canonical
  checkout rejected 49/49 members: 40 `incomplete-package-inventory` (an
  importer entry missing from the member, e.g. `prettier`, `eslint`, `vitest`), 2
  `unrecorded-module-file` (the root, from `pino/test/fixtures/eval/node_modules`),
  1 `missing-dependencies` and 6 with no member `node_modules`.
- `pulse.log`: 4,350/4,350 `Dependency workspace restore` outcomes were `rejected`.
- `dispatch-stages.tsv` `precreate.restore_deps` for that repo: median 8.6s / p90
  15.1s (n=251, before 2026-11-25T06:00Z) became median 46.4s / p90 139.1s (n=130,
  after) — about 120 minutes of dispatch-critical time spent holding the restore lock
  for zero restores. A hoisted root also exceeds the 64 MB / 20,000-entry copy budget,
  so a restore of this layout can never succeed.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_identity.py`: add a hoisted-linker check
  (`nodeLinker: hoisted` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or `node-linker=hoisted` in the
  repo `.npmrc`) that raises `Rejected("unsupported-node-linker-hoisted")`. Call it
  in `workspace_identity` right after the workspace config comparison (before the
  lockfile reads) and in the non-workspace pnpm branch of `identity`.
- Effect: `--workspace-list` fails fast, the legacy root restore records the named
  reason for `worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh`, and member walks are skipped.
- Reference pattern: existing fail-closed `Rejected(...)` codes in the same file.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_identity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`

## Acceptance

- Hoisted config (either source) → `--workspace-list` exits 1 with
  `dependency-provision-rejected reason=unsupported-node-linker-hoisted`.
- Isolated-layout workspaces still provision (existing provisioning and bootstrap
  suites pass).
- Live: a read-only `--workspace-list` against the hoisted canonical returns the new
  reason in about 1s, and later dispatches for that repo show `precreate.restore_deps`
  back near the pre-t19357 baseline or lower.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh`
- ShellCheck/linters for any touched shell.

## Follow-up (not in scope)

Hoisted repos still start workers without restored dependencies. Supporting them
(for example an APFS clonefile copy-on-write restore of the root `node_modules`
under the same trust boundary) is a separate design decision.

title: t19386: fix(terminal-blocker): map a login input owner through verified repo permissi...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19386` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(terminal-blocker): map a login input owner through verified repo permission so input_required holds instead of looping as unknown

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a worker names the input owner by GitHub login
(`TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=<login>`) instead of a role, map that login
through its verified permission on the dispatch repository: admin → `admin`,
maintain or write → `maintainer`. The report then becomes an
`input_required:<role>` hold that publishes its question. Any other permission,
or an unreadable answer, keeps today's `unknown` class.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- An issue in a managed private repo (#20518 there) has been redispatched for days.
  Its latest worker said: "The 17th session finished the same re-verification a
  few hours ago … nothing has changed since … re-capturing without a new input
  only repeats earlier sessions." It ended with
  `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=input_required`,
  `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=<repo admin login>` and a
  `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION` (close out with held rows, or file a builder
  process issue?).
- `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` capture accepted only
  `user|contributor|maintainer|admin` as the owner, so it emitted `unknown`.
  Because the reason was explicit, AI triage was skipped
  (`terminal_blocker_triage skipped:explicit_or_empty` in the worker log).
  Unknown never opens a circuit (`terminal_blocker_circuit_comment` returns
  early) and only applies the 15 min → 24 h backoff. Merged partial PRs reset
  that count, so the issue went back to `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`
  after every release, and the question was never published or answered.
- Today's per-issue worker logs show 17 issues whose final report was a no-op
  ("made no changes", "nothing new to do"). This change fixes the
  login-owner subset.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
  - Capture program: when `input_required` has exactly one owner that is not a
    role but matches a login shape, emit `unknown` with `ask_login` and make
    `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION` eligible.
  - New `_terminal_blocker_login_owner_class`: one REST read,
    `repos/<slug>/collaborators/<login>/permission` (`role_name`, falling back to
    `permission`). It prints `input_required:admin|maintainer` or `unknown`.
  - `terminal_blocker_capture_output` calls it for `unknown` captures with
    `ask_login`, and clears the question unless the class becomes input_required
    (same pattern as `_terminal_blocker_permission_ask_class`).
- Trust boundary: the role only selects who is asked. Release still requires the
  existing OWNER/MEMBER answer, brief revision or retry evidence.
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`: document the mapping.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`

## Acceptance

- A login with admin, maintain or write permission yields `input_required:admin` or
  `input_required:maintainer`, with the question captured.
- A login with read or unknown permission, a non-login value and a missing owner stay
  `unknown` with no question. The existing `human` owner cases are unchanged.
- Live: replaying the real #20518 worker log through the patched capture yields
  `input_required` owner `admin` with the question. The deployed script yields
  `unknown` with no question.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (65 run, 0 failed)
- `shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- Live replay with `DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG=<repo>` and a temporary
  `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BLOCKER_LOG_FILE`.

## Follow-up (not in scope)

Other no-op redispatch classes from the same census: stale merge-conflict feedback
after the referenced PR merged; done phases left open by `For #N` PRs; and blocked
reports re-run before their dated hold. These are tracked separately.

title: t19387: Project Node selection: install the pinned Node with nvm when it is missing
body:
## Task


`nvm install 24.18.0`, alongside the already present 26.13.1. The selector then
picks `$NVM_DIR/versions/node/v24.18.0/bin` for the Node 24 worktrees and
returns rc 0, verified inside the systemd user manager as a worker runs. A
sweep of `_project_node_bin` over every registered worktree went from 17 hard
failures to zero. The runtime was the only thing missing; discovery and
selection already worked.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Problem

Workers need the Node version a project pins (`.nvmrc`, `engines.node`).
`.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh` finds runtimes that are already
installed (fnm, nvm, Volta, mise, Homebrew, n, Nix profiles) but never installs
one. `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/runtime-launchers.md:80` states the rule:
"launching never installs software or modifies personal runtime settings".

So every pin of every branch of every pulse-enabled repository has to be
installed by hand, ahead of time, on every host. Observed on 2026-11-25: a
pulse-enabled project repository moved its default branch from Node 24 to
Node 26 (`.nvmrc` 26.13.1), while older worktrees still pin Node 24
(`.nvmrc` 24.18.0, `engines.node` `>=24.0.0 <25.0.0`). With only a system
Node 26 present, 17 of those worktrees failed before launch and 25 passed.
The failure is immediate, under one second, and reported as
`project_node_environment_failure` by `headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`:

```
ENVIRONMENT FAILURE: node v26.13.1 does not satisfy engines "24 and >=24.0.0 <25.0.0 ..."
```

## What fixed it by hand

`nvm install 24.18.0`, alongside the already present 26.13.1. The selector then
picks `$NVM_DIR/versions/node/v24.18.0/bin` for the Node 24 worktrees and
returns rc 0, verified inside the systemd user manager as a worker runs. A
sweep of `_project_node_bin` over every registered worktree went from 17 hard
failures to zero. The runtime was the only thing missing; discovery and
selection already worked.

## Proposal

Follow the model of `actions/setup-node` in CI: the job installs the version the
project pins rather than relying on the image.

- When no installed Node satisfies the requirement and `$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh` exists,
  source it and run `nvm install <pinned version>`, then select as today. nvm
  verifies the download against the release checksums.
- Leave `nvm alias default` untouched, so the host's default Node does not
  change.
- Make it opt-in through a setting, for example `AIDEVOPS_NODE_INSTALL=nvm`,
  because it changes the documented "never installs" rule. Each version costs
  roughly 200 MB of disk, measured on this host as 203 MB for Node 24.18.0 and
  230 MB for 26.13.1, which counts against any per-account quota.
- Only an exact numeric pin may be installed. A requirement that is only a range
  must keep failing closed rather than resolving a version over the network.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh`
- `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/runtime-launchers.md`

## Reference pattern

`_project_node_bin` already separates a preferred exact pin from the hard range
requirement: `_project_node_requirement` emits `pref <version>` for a numeric
version-file pin and `hard <expression>` for `engines.node`. That `pref` value
is exactly the argument `nvm install` needs, and its absence is exactly the
case that must still fail closed.

`_project_node_private_bin` shows the established shape for returning a bin
directory without reordering the worker PATH; a freshly installed nvm version
directory is already Node-only, so it needs no indirection.

`AIDEVOPS_NODE_BREW_PREFIXES` and `AIDEVOPS_NODE_NIX_PROFILES` show the
established override pattern for keeping discovery hermetically testable, and
the new install path must stay disabled by default in tests.

## Verification

title: t19388: fix(pulse): drop stale merge-conflict feedback once its PR has merged so continuations work the remaining scope
body:
## Task


Stop stale `## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #N)` blocks from steering workers into
no-op runs after PR #N has merged. When a partial (`For`/`Ref`) PR merges, remove its
`feedback-route` block from the linked issue body. Add a dispatch-time guard that
leaves blocks for merged PRs out of the worker seed, so existing bodies are covered
too.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop stale `## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #N)` blocks from steering workers into
no-op runs after PR #N has merged. When a partial (`For`/`Ref`) PR merges, remove its
`feedback-route` block from the linked issue body. Add a dispatch-time guard that
leaves blocks for merged PRs out of the worker seed, so existing bodies are covered
too.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`, since 2026-11-25T00:00Z: an issue
  in a managed private repo (#26655 there) ran 6 worker sessions, each about 1 minute
  with `result=success`. Each relaunch also costs a full dispatch ceremony (median 258s
  per launch in `dispatch-stages.tsv`). A second issue there (#31608) ended its run with
  "The conflict feedback is stale, so I made no changes. PR #35217 is already merged".
- The latest #26655 worker (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse/pulse-<repo>-26655.log`)
  answered: "I made no changes this run, because there is nothing new to do … PR #35198
  merged on 2026-11-25 at 03:22:18Z … The conflict feedback in the seed prompt is stale
  … It is open on purpose, since the PR used `For #26655`. The coverage ledger lists the
  remaining windows …". The remaining scope was never started.
- The issue body still holds
  `<!-- feedback-route:start:conflict:PR35198:SHA777f52b… -->` /
  `## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #35198)` after PR #35198 merged.
- Repo-wide search found 5 open issues with such a block. 3 reference PRs that have
  merged (#33806 merged 2026-11-23, #35217 and #35198 merged 2026-11-25), so their
  feedback is stale. 2 reference closed, unmerged PRs, where the guidance is still
  valid and must be kept.
- After a partial merge, `_pm_restore_partial_continuation`
  (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`, near line 566) restores
  `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` but leaves the body untouched.
  `issue-sync-helper-enrich.sh` (near lines 270–291) deliberately preserves
  `feedback-route` blocks across body refreshes, so nothing ever removes them.

## How

1. In the partial-continuation restore path, after the restore succeeds, remove the
   `feedback-route:start:<kind>:PR<merged>:…` through matching `feedback-route:complete`
   block(s) for the merged PR from the linked issue body. Use the existing body-edit
   wrapper (`gh_issue_edit_safe` or the wrapper the feedback-route writers use), and
   retain the existing audit comment. Remove only blocks for the merged PR number.
2. Dispatch-time guard (covers existing bodies and a failed body edit): where the
   worker prompt embeds issue context (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` builds the
   prompt near `_dlw_seed_prompt_note`; `headless-runtime-launch.sh` writes it as
   `seed-prompt.md`), drop feedback-route blocks whose PR is MERGED. One batched PR
   state read per dispatch. Keep blocks for CLOSED-unmerged or OPEN PRs. If the issue
   body is not embedded there, record where the worker reads it and apply the guard at
   that point.
3. Reference pattern: marker extraction in `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` (near lines
   514–528, `feedback-route:${phase}:${kind}:PR${n}:SHA…`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

## Acceptance

- A partial PR merge for issue N removes that PR's feedback-route block from N's body
  and keeps other blocks and the rest of the body byte-identical.
- A dispatch for an issue whose body contains a block for a merged PR produces a seed
  without that block. A block for a closed-unmerged PR is kept.
- Live: after deployment, the 3 stale examples dispatch workers that work on the
  remaining scope (not a 1-minute "nothing to do" exit).

title: t19389: fix(headless-runtime): public-triage model selection skips Anthropic OAuth candidates it can never authenticate
body:
## Task


`headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage` (the route behind the OpenCode `ai-research`
tool and Pulse triage reviews) runs OpenCode pure (`OPENCODE_PURE=1`). Pure mode cannot load
the plugin that implements Anthropic OAuth. Model selection still picks Anthropic OAuth
candidates for this role, so the run is refused after launch by the trust-boundary check in
`headless-runtime-invoke.sh` (`_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`, exit 86). The
`standard` and `thinking` tiers are therefore always unusable for `ai-research` on installs
where Anthropic auth is OAuth, even when another configured candidate in that tier is
natively authenticated.

Make selection for the public-triage role treat "Anthropic OAuth under pure public triage"
as a structural exclusion, the same way `chatgpt_oauth_unsupported` excludes ChatGPT OAuth
models. Selection should fall through to the next natively authenticated candidate. If none
remains, it should fail before launch with a named reason.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## What

`headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage` (the route behind the OpenCode `ai-research`
tool and Pulse triage reviews) runs OpenCode pure (`OPENCODE_PURE=1`). Pure mode cannot load
the plugin that implements Anthropic OAuth. Model selection still picks Anthropic OAuth
candidates for this role, so the run is refused after launch by the trust-boundary check in
`headless-runtime-invoke.sh` (`_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`, exit 86). The
`standard` and `thinking` tiers are therefore always unusable for `ai-research` on installs
where Anthropic auth is OAuth, even when another configured candidate in that tier is
natively authenticated.

Make selection for the public-triage role treat "Anthropic OAuth under pure public triage"
as a structural exclusion, the same way `chatgpt_oauth_unsupported` excludes ChatGPT OAuth
models. Selection should fall through to the next natively authenticated candidate. If none
remains, it should fail before launch with a named reason.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- In an interactive OpenCode session, `ai-research` with `model=thinking` and then
  `model=standard` both returned: "The isolated OpenCode runtime cannot authenticate the
  Anthropic OAuth provider for the <tier> tier. Pure public triage does not load the
  provider-auth plugin; select a provider with native authentication." The tool has no
  provider parameter, so that advice cannot be acted on. The session fell back to a staged
  `research-only` Task subagent, which cost extra calls and a manual file-staging step.
- `headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role triage --tier <t>` on the same install:
  simple=`openai/gpt-6-luna`, standard=`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`,
  thinking=`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.
- `get_configured_models standard` lists `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` then
  `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (API key, native auth). Standard-tier triage could
  succeed but never reaches that candidate. `thinking` has only the Anthropic candidate.
- `opencode auth list` shows Anthropic as `oauth`.
- Related closed work: GH#38423 (fixed the research-staging error message only),
  GH#37205/#37207 (auto provider selection), t19061/GH#38620 (fix-the-fixer auth cooldown
  for the same refusal).

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`, give selection the public-triage context.
   Public triage means `role == triage` and not `--private-workload` (see
   `_headless_private_workload_enabled` and the role checks in `headless-runtime-run.sh`
   `_select_cmd_run_model`). Thread `role` through `choose_model` → `_choose_model_auto` →
   `_first_healthy_configured_model` → `get_configured_models`, or set one scoped variable
   for the duration of selection. Do not read the role from an inherited environment
   variable a child could set.
2. In that context, skip a candidate whose provider is `anthropic` when the credential that
   `copy_scoped_opencode_auth` would copy is OAuth (the same `.anthropic.type == "oauth"`
   test used in `_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`). Keep that invoke-time check
   unchanged as defence-in-depth (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).
3. Add the same structural reason to `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons` (for example
   `public_triage_oauth_unsupported`), so `tier_selection_unavailable_line` names it when
   no candidate remains. Update the reason list in `headless-runtime-helper.sh` help text
   (near "chatgpt_oauth_unsupported (structural)").
4. Reference pattern: the ChatGPT OAuth denylist handling in `get_configured_models`
   (`_headless_chatgpt_oauth_unsupported_ids` / `_headless_model_id_denied`) and in
   `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons`.
5. Optional: when the tier has no triage-capable candidate, have
   `.opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts` `runtimeFailure` say which tiers are usable
   instead of "select a provider with native authentication".

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh
- .opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts

## Acceptance

- With Anthropic auth of type OAuth, `select --role triage --tier standard` returns the
  next natively authenticated standard candidate (for example an `opencode-go/*` model),
  not `anthropic/*`.
- With no remaining candidate (for example `thinking` with only Anthropic OAuth), selection
  fails before launch with exit 75/1 and a `tier_selection_unavailable` line naming
  `public_triage_oauth_unsupported`. No OpenCode process is spawned.
- `--role worker` and `--role pulse` selection is unchanged: Anthropic OAuth stays
  selectable there.
- `--private-workload` behaviour is unchanged: it already requires an explicit `--model`.
- The invoke-time trust-boundary refusal in `headless-runtime-invoke.sh` remains.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- Live, read-only: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role triage --tier standard`
  and the same for `--role worker`. Compare before and after.
- If `.opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts` changes: `bun run typecheck`.

title: Add Brevo MCP guide and safe OpenCode setup (focused servers + send/delete deny rules)
body:
## Goal

Add a reusable Brevo (ex-Sendinblue) MCP guide and setup helper so email-campaign work can connect to Brevo safely without re-deriving the config each time.

## Evidence

An interactive session had to work out by hand how to connect Brevo's official remote MCP to OpenCode v2. Nothing in `~/.aidevops/agents` mentions Brevo or Sendinblue (`rg -il "brevo|sendinblue"` returns nothing).

## Observed working pattern (OpenCode v2)

- Token: a Brevo API key created with "Create MCP server API key" switched on, stored as `aidevops secret set BREVO_MCP_KEY`. It is then written to a 600-permission token file in a per-user config directory, the same token-file pattern the existing Magento/Matomo remote MCP entries use. Command: `aidevops secret BREVO_MCP_KEY -- bash -c 'printf %s "$BREVO_MCP_KEY" | install -m 600 /dev/stdin <token-file>'`.
- Servers: one `type: remote` entry per focused endpoint, `https://mcp.brevo.com/v1/<module>/mcp`, with header `Authorization: Bearer {file:<token-file>}`, `oauth: false`. The modules needed for newsletters are `brevo_email_campaign_management`, `brevo_campaign_analytics`, `brevo_lists`, `brevo_segments` and `brevo_senders`. The full `brevo` endpoint exposes about 193 tools, too many to use well.
- Guardrails via the `permissions` ruleset, with action `<server>_<tool>`:
  - Deny `send_email_campaign_now`, `delete_email_campaign`, `update_campaign_status` and `email_export_recipients`.
  - Deny the list mutations (`create_list`, `update_list`, `delete_list`, `add_contact_to_list`, `remove_contact_from_list`) and the sender mutations.
  - Set `ask` on `create_email_campaign` and `update_email_campaign`, because both accept `scheduledAt`, which can schedule a real send.
  - Denied tools disappear from the Code Mode catalogue. The config hot-reloads without a restart.

## Files to modify

- New: `.agents/services/email/brevo.md` (or the nearest existing email-services directory; confirm the path with `git ls-files '.agents/services/*'`).
- Add a Brevo row to `reference/domain-index.md` and to the email-campaign workflow (`scripts/commands/email-campaign.md` or its workflow file).
- Optional: an `mcp-setup` helper that adds the entries and permissions idempotently with jq and backs up the config first.

## Verification

- `tools/list` against each endpoint succeeds with the Bearer header.
- After the config change, the Code Mode `search({namespace:"brevo_campaigns"})` result shows no denied tools.
- A read-only `get_lists` call returns the account's lists.

title: routines: launchd jobs lack the terminal's TCC grants; document one-shot launchd probe and interpreter-path permission attribution
body:
## Observed

A macOS launchd routine (a project-owned weekday digest job, `ProgramArguments` = `/bin/bash <script>`) passed its terminal dry run, including a dry run under `env -i` to mimic launchd's environment. Its first real launchd run then failed: `sqlite3.connect("file:~/Library/Mail/V10/MailData/Envelope Index?mode=ro", uri=True)` raised `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file`. The terminal session holds Full Disk Access; the launchd job does not. `env -i` strips environment variables but keeps the terminal's TCC (privacy) attribution, so it cannot reproduce this class of failure.

Second finding: the first Apple Event to Mail from the launchd job (`osascript` spawned by Homebrew Python) produced a consent prompt, and the user TCC database recorded the grant against the Homebrew Cellar binary path (`.../Cellar/python@3.15/3.15.2/.../bin/python3.15` → `com.apple.mail`), not against `/bin/bash`. A Homebrew Python upgrade changes that path, so the grant silently stops applying and the prompt reappears.

## Proposal

Document both points in the routine guidance, so `/routine` designs and dry runs catch them before install:

1. Before installing a launchd routine that touches TCC-protected data (`~/Library/Mail`, Messages, Safari, Photos, Calendar or Contacts stores) or sends Apple Events, verify with a one-shot launchd probe: a temporary plist with `RunAtLoad=true` and the same `ProgramArguments[0]`, running a read-only subset and writing results to a temp file; then `launchctl bootout` it. A terminal or `env -i` dry run is not evidence.
2. Prefer per-app Automation (Apple Events) over Full Disk Access on `/bin/bash` or `/bin/zsh`, because a shell grant extends to every script that shell runs.
3. Note that Automation and Full Disk Access grants for non-bundled interpreters are keyed to the resolved binary path; interpreter upgrades (Homebrew Python or Node) re-prompt.

## Files

- `.agents/reference/routines.md`: add a short "macOS launchd and privacy permissions" subsection near the platform-unit (launchd/systemd) material (around lines 280-300).
- `.agents/workflows/local-permissions-check.md`: one line cross-referencing it under the Full Disk Access and Automation bullets (lines 30-34).
- Optional, if the `/routine` command has a dry-run checklist (`.agents/scripts/commands/routine.md`): add the probe step.

## Verification

- `rg -n "launchd probe|one-shot" .agents/reference/routines.md` finds the new guidance.
- Markdown lint per repository policy; the always-loaded size ratchet is unaffected (reference files only).

title: t19390: feat(runtime-verify): exact-head OpenCode plugin probe helper so plugin PRs carry runtime-verified evidence without waiting for an interactive verifier
body:
## Task


Add `.agents/scripts/plugin-runtime-probe-helper.sh`. It runs real headless `opencode run` sessions that
load exactly one copy of the aidevops plugin: either from a given worktree (the PR head) or the
deployed copy (the baseline). It prints a compact, secret-free report so the authoring worker can
pass `--testing-level runtime-verified` to `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` for plugin changes,
instead of `runtime-pending`.

Today a High/Critical plugin PR opens as `runtime-pending` under `hold-for-review`. Only a live
interactive session can lift that hold (`pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`: "High/Critical
runtime verification remains interactive"). Workers record runtime-pending because "the running
session cannot reload its plugin; no new isolated runtime harness was introduced" (PR #40263 body).
This helper is that harness.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## What

Add `.agents/scripts/plugin-runtime-probe-helper.sh`. It runs real headless `opencode run` sessions that
load exactly one copy of the aidevops plugin: either from a given worktree (the PR head) or the
deployed copy (the baseline). It prints a compact, secret-free report so the authoring worker can
pass `--testing-level runtime-verified` to `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` for plugin changes,
instead of `runtime-pending`.

Today a High/Critical plugin PR opens as `runtime-pending` under `hold-for-review`. Only a live
interactive session can lift that hold (`pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`: "High/Critical
runtime verification remains interactive"). Workers record runtime-pending because "the running
session cannot reload its plugin; no new isolated runtime harness was introduced" (PR #40263 body).
This helper is that harness.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- PR #40263 (permission broker, High) waited about 14 hours, CLEAN and green, for an interactive
  verifier. An interactive session built the probe below ad hoc. Each mode then took about
  3 minutes, and the evidence lifted the hold through `verify-runtime`.
- 17 PRs opened as runtime-pending in the 14 days to 2026-11-25. Plugin changes are a recurring
  class: #40263, #40274 and #40328. The interactive verification of #40328 took 4h 12m.
- Pitfall found while building the probe: an `OPENCODE_CONFIG` override does not replace the
  global plugin. OpenCode 1.19.6 concatenated both `file://…/index.mjs` entries, so two brokers and
  two command policies ran, and every permission event was captured twice. The probe must replace
  the plugin entry in an isolated config home.

## How

Mechanics that were proven in the ad hoc probe (macOS, OpenCode 1.19.6):

1. Make a private run directory (`umask 077`) under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/`.
2. Config home: create `cfg/opencode/` and symlink these entries from
   `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode`: `agent command tool skills themes node_modules
   package.json bun.lock AGENTS.md tui.json`. Do not link `plugins/`. Write
   `cfg/opencode/opencode.json` as `jq --arg p "$plugin_url" '.plugin = [$p]'` over the global
   config. Symlink `cfg/aidevops` to `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/aidevops`. Export
   `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<run>/cfg`, and unset `OPENCODE_CONFIG`.
3. Data home: create `data/opencode/`. Copy `auth.json` from the current
   `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/opencode/` with mode 600; inside a worker, that is the
   worker's own isolated copy. Export `XDG_DATA_HOME=<run>/data`.
4. Inert worker identity: set `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` and `WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH=<worktree>`, an
   inert `WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER` and a probe `WORKER_SESSION_KEY`. Unset `WORKER_REPO_SLUG` and
   `DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG`. Redirect `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BLOCKER_LOG_FILE` and
   `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_REQUEST_FILE` into the run directory. Nothing then reaches the shared
   blocker log, pulse or GitHub.
5. Run `opencode debug config` and print only caller-selected jq paths, for example
   `.plugin` and `.permission.external_directory | keys`. Delete the full output: it carries
   provider and MCP settings.
6. Probes: read a TSV file (`<id>\t<step>|<step>…`). Run each probe in a fresh `opencode run
   --format json --model <model> "<prompt>" </dev/null` session. A rejected permission ends the
   OpenCode turn, so put each expected-denied probe in its own session. For each probe, print the
   tool, status, input (command or filePath, truncated) and the first 100 characters of the output
   or error. Then print the broker events from the redirected blocker log: event, permission, tool
   and grantable.
7. Clean up on every exit path (trap): the auth copy, the copied `opencode.json` and any resolved
   config. Keep only the report and the probe event files in the 700 directory.
8. Flags: `--worktree PATH` (head mode; the plugin is `PATH/.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`),
   `--baseline` (deployed plugin), `--probes FILE`, `--model` (default: the normal worker model)
   and `--out DIR`. Exit non-zero only on harness failure. Probe outcomes are data for the caller.

Docs: add a one-line pointer in `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`, in the Runtime Testing
paragraph that mentions GH#39558. Plugin changes are exercised at the exact head with this helper,
and baseline vs head outcomes go into `--testing`. Add the same pointer to step 4 of
`.agents/scripts/commands/decisions.md` for interactive verifiers.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/plugin-runtime-probe-helper.sh
- .agents/workflows/full-loop.md
- .agents/scripts/commands/decisions.md

## Acceptance

- `plugin-runtime-probe-helper.sh --worktree <head> --probes <file>` and `--baseline` show
  different outcomes for a plugin permission change. Reference case, from the PR #40263 head
  against the deployed v3.39.282 plugin: `read /dev/null` was rejected with one
  `permission_request_captured` event on the baseline and allowed with none on the head. Reads of a
  home-root file and of an unrelated `~/Git` repository file were rejected on both.
- `opencode debug config` in head mode lists exactly one plugin entry, the worktree path.
- The shared `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` gets no new lines from a probe run.
  No auth or config copy remains after success, failure or interrupt.
- ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 compatible; every function has an explicit return.

## Verification

- Run the helper twice (head and `--baseline`) with a two-probe TSV: one allowed read inside the
  worktree and one denied home-root read. Compare the reports.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/plugin-runtime-probe-helper.sh`.
- `rg -c . ~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` before and after a run: unchanged.

</details>

<details>

title: gh_create_pr: fall back to REST on GraphQL 5xx create failures, not only on low rate-limit headroom
body:
## Observed (25 Nov 2026, interactive session, private project repo)

`gh_create_pr` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`) failed 4 times in about 4 minutes with GitHub GraphQL server errors on the create mutation:

- `HTTP 502: 502 Bad Gateway (https://api.github.com/graphql)`
- `GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query on ...` (twice)
- `HTTP 504: 504 Gateway Timeout (https://api.github.com/graphql)`

Over the same period, GraphQL reads (`gh pr list`) and REST calls worked. `gh api rate_limit` showed GraphQL at 5000/5000, and githubstatus.com reported "All Systems Operational". After each failure, `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` returned `[]` (no PR was created).

The REST fallback at line ~1431 runs only when `_rest_should_fallback_write` is true, and that is true only for low GraphQL headroom (`_rest_should_fallback`, `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` ~345). So a GraphQL 5xx with full headroom leaves no path except the test override `_GH_SHOULD_FALLBACK_OVERRIDE=1`. With that override, `_rest_pr_create` created the PR at once.

Two side notes from the REST path:

1. The PR was created as a draft (`_gh_create_pr_should_default_draft`), so it needed a separate `gh pr ready`.
2. `_rest_pr_create` printed `created PR #N but could not verify requested labels after bounded retries`, but `GET /issues/N/labels` showed `origin:interactive` already applied. The label postcondition may be checking through GraphQL (which was failing) or too early.

## Proposal

- In `gh_create_pr`, also allow the REST create fallback when the GraphQL failure is a transient server error (HTTP 502/503/504 or "Something went wrong while executing your query"). Before falling back, confirm through REST that no PR exists for the same head and base (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>&state=all`). GitHub also refuses a second open PR for the same head and base (422), which adds protection against duplicates.
- Make `_rest_pr_create_label_postcondition` verify labels through REST (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/labels`) so that a GraphQL outage doesn't report a false label failure.

## Reproducer

Conditions: api.github.com/graphql returns 5xx for the create mutation (or `gh pr create` is stubbed to exit 1 with that message), and `gh api rate_limit` shows GraphQL remaining at 5000.

**Symptom command:** `source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh; gh_create_pr --repo OWNER/REPO --base main --head BRANCH --title T --body-file F`

**Actual output:**

```text
pull request create failed: HTTP 502: 502 Bad Gateway (https://api.github.com/graphql)
pull request create failed: GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query on 2026-11-25T15:46:33Z. Please include `BD6A:337272:71DE2FC:164BB147:6B0702D6` when reporting this issue.
pull request create failed: HTTP 504: 504 Gateway Timeout (https://api.github.com/graphql)
```

No PR is created, and REST is never tried. **Expected:** one REST create, after confirming that no PR exists for the head.

**Workaround output** (same command with `_GH_SHOULD_FALLBACK_OVERRIDE=1`):

```text
[INFO] gh-wrapper: GraphQL exhausted, falling back to REST for pr create
[aidevops] _rest_pr_create: created PR #N but could not verify requested labels after bounded retries; not retrying creation
```

The PR was created as a draft, and `GET /issues/N/labels` showed `origin:interactive` was already applied.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`

`gh_create_pr` is at about lines 1409-1439; the fallback functions are `_rest_should_fallback_write`, `_rest_pr_create` and `_rest_pr_create_label_postcondition`.

## Verification

- Unit test: stub `gh pr create` to exit 1 with "HTTP 502: 502 Bad Gateway (https://api.github.com/graphql)", with GraphQL remaining at 5000 and the REST pulls list empty. Expect one `_rest_pr_create` call and the PR URL returned.
- Same stub, but the REST pulls list already has an open PR for the head. Expect no create call and the existing URL returned.
- Label postcondition: with GraphQL calls failing and REST labels returning the origin label, expect success.

title: t19391: fix(pulse-merge): held runtime-pending CI gate lets absent downstream require...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19391` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-25 | **Started:** 2026-11-25
**Tags:** `bug` `pulse` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(pulse-merge): held runtime-pending CI gate lets absent downstream required contexts mask a terminal failure

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the runtime-pending held-PR CI gate (`_pmrp_head_ci_ready` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`) report a terminal-red head when a required check failed terminally and no required check is still active, even if other required contexts are absent from the head's check-run rollup. Today any absent required context makes the whole head "pending", so a held runtime-pending PR whose failing job stops downstream matrix jobs is never routed to CI repair and never surfaces an ATTENTION line.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 on a managed WordPress plugin repository (PR held `hold-for-review` with recorded scope `runtime-pending` since 2026-11-24T09:12Z, ~34 hours):

- `full-loop-helper.sh runtime-pending-notice <PR> <repo>` returns a liftable notice (risk Critical, level runtime-pending).
- The default-branch ruleset requires `Lint (PHP 7.4)`, `Release build, preflight and Plugin Check`, `Smoke test (WordPress 6.2, PHP 7.4)` and `Smoke test (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3)`.
- On the exact head, `Lint (PHP 7.4)` is `completed/failure`; the release and smoke jobs depend on it, so they are `skipped` under the unexpanded matrix name (`Smoke test (WordPress ${{ matrix.wp }}, ...)`) and the two required smoke contexts never appear in the rollup.
- `_pmrp_head_ci_ready` evaluates "any required context is null → pending" before looking for failures, so it returns 1 (silent defer) every pass. `pulse.log` has only `skipping PR #N ... PR is draft or has hold-for-review` lines for the PR: no CI-repair route (t19244), no notice, no ATTENTION.

The normal merge-pass path already treats this head as red: `_check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` ignores absent contexts and counts terminal failures, and `pulse-merge-process.sh` only waits for absent/active contexts when no terminal failure exists. The held path's comment claims its states match those helpers, but the precedence differs.

## How

In `_pmrp_head_ci_ready`, keep the single exact-head rollup read and classify in this order:

1. Any required context present with an empty conclusion or an active status (`queued|pending|in_progress|waiting|requested`) → `pending` (unchanged: never route repair while a required check is running; covers same-SHA re-runs).
2. Else any required context whose latest run concluded `failure|cancelled|timed_out` → `red:<names>` (absent contexts no longer mask it; they are downstream jobs that cannot start).
3. Else any required context absent → `pending` (not yet created).
4. Else → `green`.

Update the function comment to state the precedence. No other behaviour changes.

## Acceptance

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`: add a case where one required context failed and another is absent from the rollup; it must log `deferred: required checks failing (<name>)` and route one CI repair. Existing cases (all pending, failure beside an active check, red, green, re-run turns red) keep their expectations.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean on both files.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`

title: t19392: fix(pulse-merge): resync PRs whose GitHub head desynced from the branch ref instead of skipping them as mergeable=UNKNOWN forever
body:
## Task


When the Pulse merge pass sees a same-repository PR whose `mergeable` stays UNKNOWN after its retry, check whether GitHub's PR head (`headRefOid`) has fallen behind the head branch ref. If the branch ref holds a different SHA, the PR is desynchronized: GitHub never processed the latest push, so mergeability is never computed and the PR is skipped every pass. Resynchronize it with the update-branch endpoint bound to the branch-ref SHA, at most once per (PR, branch SHA), and log a distinct reason. If resync is not allowed or fails, log an ATTENTION line naming both SHAs.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When the Pulse merge pass sees a same-repository PR whose `mergeable` stays UNKNOWN after its retry, check whether GitHub's PR head (`headRefOid`) has fallen behind the head branch ref. If the branch ref holds a different SHA, the PR is desynchronized: GitHub never processed the latest push, so mergeability is never computed and the PR is skipped every pass. Resynchronize it with the update-branch endpoint bound to the branch-ref SHA, at most once per (PR, branch SHA), and log a distinct reason. If resync is not allowed or fails, log an ATTENTION line naming both SHAs.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 on marcusquinn/aidevops PR #40371 (worker PR for #40366):

- `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/pulls/40371` → `head.sha=cf15197…`, `mergeable=null`, `mergeable_state=unknown`, `updated_at=2026-11-25T15:11:15Z`.
- `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/auto-20261125-145036-gh40366` → `1569a09…`, a worker fix commit (parent `cf15197`) pushed at 15:46Z. `refs/pull/40371/head` still pointed at `cf15197`.
- For ~4 hours `pulse.log` repeated `Merge pass: skipping PR #40371 in marcusquinn/aidevops — mergeable=UNKNOWN (was UNKNOWN, still not MERGEABLE after retry)` (`_resolve_pr_mergeable_status`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:544`). Meanwhile #40393 stayed deferred by `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#40366 …)` because #40366 could not close.
- `PUT repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/pulls/40371/update-branch` with `expected_head_sha=cf15197…` (the PR head) returned HTTP 422 "expected head sha didn't match current head ref". With `expected_head_sha=1569a09…` (the branch ref) it succeeded; within 20 s the PR head was `9810e7b…` and `mergeable=true`.

This is a GitHub-side sync failure, not a code problem; the pulse currently has no route out of it, so a finished worker PR waits for a human to notice.

## How

1. In `_resolve_pr_mergeable_status` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`), on the "still not MERGEABLE after retry" UNKNOWN branch, call a new helper (for example `_pmp_resync_desynced_pr_head`) before returning 1. Pass what it needs from the caller `_pmp_stage_review_and_gates` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (around line 1377): `pr_head_ref_oid`, `pr_labels`, and the head ref name (the merge-pass PR list already requests `headRefName`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:327`). Keep the existing three-argument calls working (new arguments optional; absent → old behaviour).
2. The helper reads the branch ref with one call: `gh api repos/<slug>/git/ref/heads/<headRefName> --jq .object.sha` (URL-encode `/` in the ref name per GitHub's API). Skip cross-repository PRs and any read failure (fail closed: log and return).
3. If the branch SHA equals the PR head: no desync; return as today.
4. If they differ and the PR labels allow worker routing (`_feedback_route_labels_allow_worker_route "$labels" 1`, the same `#aidevops:trust-boundary` gate the runtime-pending CI repair uses in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh`), call `_pmp_update_branch_rest "$pr" "$slug" "$branch_sha"` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-rest-state.sh:461`). Record `<branch_sha>` in a per-PR state file (pattern: `_pmrs_missing_checks_state_file`) so the same desync is attempted once. Log `Merge pass: PR #N in slug — PR head <12> desynced from branch ref <12>; update-branch resync rc=<rc>`.
5. Otherwise (not worker-routable, already attempted for this branch SHA, or resync failed) log `[pulse-merge] ATTENTION: PR #N in slug head <12> is desynced from branch ref <12> (GitHub did not process the latest push); push to the branch or close/reopen the PR to resync`.
6. Add the new log fingerprint to `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` next to `pw-merge-skip-unknown-retry` (line ~103) so diagnosis names the cause.

Do not close/reopen PRs automatically: close events trigger issue/label automation.

## Acceptance

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` (it already exercises `_resolve_pr_mergeable_status` with stubbed `gh_pr_view`): (a) UNKNOWN + branch SHA differs + worker labels → one `_pmp_update_branch_rest` call with the branch SHA, function still returns 1 this pass; (b) a second call for the same branch SHA makes no new update-branch call and logs ATTENTION; (c) branch SHA equal to PR head → no update-branch call; (d) interactive/external labels → ATTENTION only; (e) three-argument call → unchanged behaviour.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean on changed files.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh`

title: t19393: fix(dispatch-footprint): scope status:in-review footprints to the linked open PR's changed files instead of the whole brief
body:
## Task


In the dispatch footprint check, an in-flight issue labelled `status:in-review` that has an open linked PR should reserve the files that PR actually changes, not every path its brief declares. Today the brief's `EDIT:`/`NEW:`/`Files Scope` paths stay reserved until the issue closes, so a broad investigation brief whose PR touched one file defers unrelated candidates for hours.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

In the dispatch footprint check, an in-flight issue labelled `status:in-review` that has an open linked PR should reserve the files that PR actually changes, not every path its brief declares. Today the brief's `EDIT:`/`NEW:`/`Files Scope` paths stay reserved until the issue closes, so a broad investigation brief whose PR touched one file defers unrelated candidates for hours.

## Why

`pulse.log` on 2026-11-25:

- `Dispatch deferred for #40393 in marcusquinn/aidevops: FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#40366 files=.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh)`. #40366's consolidated brief lists ten scripts; its open PR #40371 changes only `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh` and a new test.
- `Dispatch deferred for #129 in wpallstars/seoproanalytics: FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#131 files=README.md)` (also #128 and #146, 17 deferrals). #131's open PR #145 does not change `README.md`.
- Across the log, 170 footprint deferrals; 47 distinct candidate/blocker pairs. Several blockers are `status:in-review` with an open PR.

The linked PR is the best evidence of the real conflict surface once implementation exists. A deferral against a file the PR never touched costs a dispatch slot per cycle and delays the candidate until the blocker merges.

## How

In `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`, around line 988):

1. Extend the per-rebuild open-PR memo already used by `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence` (the `gh pr list --repo "$repo_slug" --state open --json number,headRefName,body --limit 100` read, lines ~944-955) to also request `files` so one read serves both uses. Keep the existing failure semantics (failed read → `[]`, reused for the whole rebuild).
2. Emit a status:in-review flag in the existing single jq TSV pass (lines ~1013-1019; add a column like the `status:claimed` one).
3. For an in-review issue, find open PRs linked by the same rule as evidence 2 (branch name `gh<N>` boundary or a closing keyword `#<N>` in the body). If at least one linked PR returns a non-empty file list, reserve the union of those PRs' file paths instead of `_footprint_extract_paths "$body"`. Otherwise (no linked PR, empty file list, failed read, or 100-file truncation where `files` length == 100) keep the brief paths, so uncertainty still reserves the declared scope.
4. Log one `[footprint-coordinator] event=footprint_pr_scoped issue=#N repo=<slug> pr=#P files=<count>` line per narrowed issue via `_footprint_coordinator_log`.
5. Leave `status:in-progress`, `status:queued` and `status:claimed` behaviour unchanged: the worker may still be editing outside its PR's current diff.

## Acceptance

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: add cases with a stubbed `gh` where (a) an in-review blocker whose brief declares `a.sh` and `b.sh` but whose linked PR changes only `a.sh` no longer blocks a candidate declaring `b.sh` and still blocks one declaring `a.sh`; (b) an in-review blocker without a linked PR keeps its brief paths; (c) a failed PR read keeps brief paths; (d) an in-progress blocker with a linked PR keeps brief paths.
- Existing footprint tests pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`; ShellCheck clean on changed files.
- Keep the open-PR read count at one per rebuild (GH#38055).

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`

title: t19394: perf(pre-commit): run the diff-scoped pipe early-exit check locally so workers stop discovering it in CI after opening the PR
body:
## Task


Run the existing diff-scoped `pipe-early-exit-check.sh` from the shell pre-commit hook (`.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`) on the modified shell files, judging only lines added since `HEAD`. Workers and interactive sessions then see an early-exit pipe reader (`writer | grep -q`, `| grep -m1`, `| head -n N` under pipefail) before pushing, instead of after the PR's CI run.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Run the existing diff-scoped `pipe-early-exit-check.sh` from the shell pre-commit hook (`.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`) on the modified shell files, judging only lines added since `HEAD`. Workers and interactive sessions then see an early-exit pipe reader (`writer | grep -q`, `| grep -m1`, `| head -n N` under pipefail) before pushing, instead of after the PR's CI run.

## Why

The check runs only in CI (`.github/workflows/pipe-early-exit-check.yml`, and the pulse-merge suite job in `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`). Merged marcusquinn/aidevops PRs since 2026-11-20 (GraphQL search, commits after PR creation, classified by headline):

- worker PRs: 138 post-creation commits across 43 PRs; 18 are pipe early-exit repairs ("avoid early-exit pipe readers", "restore here-string greps to satisfy pipe-early-exit gate", "avoid grep SIGPIPE in ratchet assertions"), 10 complexity and 6 lint/style.
- interactive PRs: 26 post-creation commits across 11 PRs; 1 pipe early-exit repair.
- Only 19 of 52 recent worker PRs merged with no post-creation commit, against 22 of 28 interactive PRs. Worker PR create-to-merge median 43 min vs 16 min interactive, while last-commit-to-merge is similar (18 vs 16 min): the gap is post-PR iteration.

Each CI-only finding costs a full CI cycle and a worker continuation. The checker is local, fast, network-free and diff-scoped, so it fits the hook's existing "fast — no network calls" validators.

## How

1. Add `validate_pipe_early_exit` to `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` next to `validate_gh_api_slurp_filter` / `validate_bash32_parse` (pattern: same print_info header, return the violation count). Resolve the checker beside the hook (`$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/pipe-early-exit-check.sh`); if it is missing or not readable, print a warning and return 0.
2. Call `bash pipe-early-exit-check.sh --scan-files --diff-base HEAD <files>`; when `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` fails (initial commit), skip with an info line. Exit 1 → print its output and count 1 violation; exit 2 → warning only (usage error must not block commits).
3. Call it from the shell-file block after `validate_bash32_parse` (around line 1577).

## Acceptance

- In a temporary Git repository, a staged change adding `printf '%s' "$x" | grep -q foo` inside a `set -euo pipefail` script makes the hook return non-zero and print the checker's file:line; the here-string form `grep -q foo <<<"$x"` passes; a pre-existing violation on an unchanged line does not block.
- Add those cases to a new or existing pre-commit hook test (pattern: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-hook-warning-decoupling.sh`); `bash` the test and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pipe-early-exit-check.sh` pass; ShellCheck clean.

title: aidevops update uninstalls user-installed Homebrew beads/bd on every run, breaking repos that use Beads independently
body:
## What

Since PR #38530 (GH#38522), `cleanup_retired_beads()` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh` runs `brew uninstall` for `bd`, `bv`, `beads` and `beads_viewer` on every setup/update run. It cannot tell a formula that aidevops once installed from one the user installed for projects that use Beads on their own. On a machine whose project repos have `.beads/` databases and an `AGENTS.md` that mandates `bd`, the CLI disappears after each aidevops update, and reinstalling it from Homebrew is undone by the next run.

## Evidence (one macOS host, reporter is an aidevops user, not a maintainer)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log`, 2026-11-15 about 22:42 UTC, the first update after #38530 merged (22:28 UTC):
  - `Removed retired Homebrew formula bd`
  - `Removed retired Homebrew formula bv`
  - `Removed retired Homebrew formula beads_viewer`
- 2026-11-25: the CLI was reinstalled from homebrew/core (`beads` 1.3.4). The next setup run (script-drift re-deploy at v3.39.282, between 19:13 and 19:17 UTC) logged `Removed retired Homebrew formula beads`. `command -v bd` is empty again.
- Deployed `migrations.sh` at v3.39.282:
  - the comment above `cleanup_retired_beads()` says "Only remove aidevops-deployed files. Never uninstall user binaries, delete project databases, or alter independently managed Git hook sections."
  - the function body then calls `_retire_brew_formula` for `bd bv beads beads_viewer`, and `_retire_brew_formula()` runs `brew uninstall "$formula"` whenever `brew list --formula "$formula"` succeeds. There is no ownership check and no opt-out.
- Before #38530 this was advice only: `Beads integration retired; optional manual uninstall: ... (check your original installer first).`

## Impact

- Repos that use Beads independently of aidevops lose their issue-tracker CLI. Agent sessions in those repos fail with `command not found: bd`, so task notes and `bd dolt push` cannot be completed.
- `brew install beads` is the install method the Beads README recommends, so the obvious repair is silently reverted on the next update.
- Project Beads databases and exports are not touched; only the binary is removed.

## Expected

Retiring the aidevops Beads integration should not uninstall a Beads CLI the user installed themselves. Any of these would fix it:

## Task


`headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage` (the route behind the OpenCode `ai-research`
tool and Pulse triage reviews) runs OpenCode pure (`OPENCODE_PURE=1`). Pure mode cannot load
the plugin that implements Anthropic OAuth. Model selection still picks Anthropic OAuth
candidates for this role, so the run is refused after launch by the trust-boundary check in
`headless-runtime-invoke.sh` (`_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`, exit 86). The
`standard` and `thinking` tiers are therefore always unusable for `ai-research` on installs
where Anthropic auth is OAuth, even when another configured candidate in that tier is
natively authenticated.

Make selection for the public-triage role treat "Anthropic OAuth under pure public triage"
as a structural exclusion, the same way `chatgpt_oauth_unsupported` excludes ChatGPT OAuth
models. Selection should fall through to the next natively authenticated candidate. If none
remains, it should fail before launch with a named reason.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## What

`headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage` (the route behind the OpenCode `ai-research`
tool and Pulse triage reviews) runs OpenCode pure (`OPENCODE_PURE=1`). Pure mode cannot load
the plugin that implements Anthropic OAuth. Model selection still picks Anthropic OAuth
candidates for this role, so the run is refused after launch by the trust-boundary check in
`headless-runtime-invoke.sh` (`_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`, exit 86). The
`standard` and `thinking` tiers are therefore always unusable for `ai-research` on installs
where Anthropic auth is OAuth, even when another configured candidate in that tier is
natively authenticated.

Make selection for the public-triage role treat "Anthropic OAuth under pure public triage"
as a structural exclusion, the same way `chatgpt_oauth_unsupported` excludes ChatGPT OAuth
models. Selection should fall through to the next natively authenticated candidate. If none
remains, it should fail before launch with a named reason.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- In an interactive OpenCode session, `ai-research` with `model=thinking` and then
  `model=standard` both returned: "The isolated OpenCode runtime cannot authenticate the
  Anthropic OAuth provider for the <tier> tier. Pure public triage does not load the
  provider-auth plugin; select a provider with native authentication." The tool has no
  provider parameter, so that advice cannot be acted on. The session fell back to a staged
  `research-only` Task subagent, which cost extra calls and a manual file-staging step.
- `headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role triage --tier <t>` on the same install:
  simple=`openai/gpt-6-luna`, standard=`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`,
  thinking=`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.
- `get_configured_models standard` lists `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` then
  `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (API key, native auth). Standard-tier triage could
  succeed but never reaches that candidate. `thinking` has only the Anthropic candidate.
- `opencode auth list` shows Anthropic as `oauth`.
- Related closed work: GH#38423 (fixed the research-staging error message only),
  GH#37205/#37207 (auto provider selection), t19061/GH#38620 (fix-the-fixer auth cooldown
  for the same refusal).

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`, give selection the public-triage context.
   Public triage means `role == triage` and not `--private-workload` (see
   `_headless_private_workload_enabled` and the role checks in `headless-runtime-run.sh`
   `_select_cmd_run_model`). Thread `role` through `choose_model` → `_choose_model_auto` →
   `_first_healthy_configured_model` → `get_configured_models`, or set one scoped variable
   for the duration of selection. Do not read the role from an inherited environment
   variable a child could set.
2. In that context, skip a candidate whose provider is `anthropic` when the credential that
   `copy_scoped_opencode_auth` would copy is OAuth (the same `.anthropic.type == "oauth"`
   test used in `_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`). Keep that invoke-time check
   unchanged as defence-in-depth (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).
3. Add the same structural reason to `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons` (for example
   `public_triage_oauth_unsupported`), so `tier_selection_unavailable_line` names it when
   no candidate remains. Update the reason list in `headless-runtime-helper.sh` help text
   (near "chatgpt_oauth_unsupported (structural)").
4. Reference pattern: the ChatGPT OAuth denylist handling in `get_configured_models`
   (`_headless_chatgpt_oauth_unsupported_ids` / `_headless_model_id_denied`) and in
   `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons`.
5. Optional: when the tier has no triage-capable candidate, have
   `.opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts` `runtimeFailure` say which tiers are usable
   instead of "select a provider with native authentication".

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh
- .opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts

## Acceptance

- With Anthropic auth of type OAuth, `select --role triage --tier standard` returns the
  next natively authenticated standard candidate (for example an `opencode-go/*` model),
  not `anthropic/*`.
- With no remaining candidate (for example `thinking` with only Anthropic OAuth), selection
  fails before launch with exit 75/1 and a `tier_selection_unavailable` line naming
  `public_triage_oauth_unsupported`. No OpenCode process is spawned.
- `--role worker` and `--role pulse` selection is unchanged: Anthropic OAuth stays
  selectable there.
- `--private-workload` behaviour is unchanged: it already requires an explicit `--model`.
- The invoke-time trust-boundary refusal in `headless-runtime-invoke.sh` remains.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- Live, read-only: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role triage --tier standard`

- If `.opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts` changes: `bun run typecheck`.

title: fix(opencode-db): read-only lookup helpers checkpoint-on-close under exclusive lock — 11+ min lock convoy on global opencode.db
body:
## What

Several Python helpers that only **read** the OpenCode DB open it read-write with a plain `sqlite3.connect(path)`. Interactive TUIs use isolated project DBs, so these helpers are often the **only** connection to the global `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. When such a helper exits, SQLite closes the last connection and runs a full WAL checkpoint under an **exclusive lock** (`sqlite3WalClose → sqlite3WalCheckpoint`). On a large DB under I/O load that lock lasted more than 11 minutes. Every other reader and writer meanwhile got `database is locked (5)`, and the next helper repeated the cycle, producing a lock convoy.

## Evidence (2026-11-25, macOS, global opencode.db = 85 GiB, WAL 21 MB, disk I/O shared with Backblaze initial scan + Time Machine)

- `lsof` on `opencode.db`: the **only** holder was `Python worker_lifecycle_resolve_session.py` (parent `worker-watchdog.sh --check`). It had been running 10–11 minutes using 0.43 s of CPU.
- `sample <pid>`: 885/885 samples in `_Py_Finalize → connection_clear → sqlite3_finalize → sqlite3LeaveMutexAndCloseZombie → sqlite3BtreeClose → sqlite3PagerClose → sqlite3WalClose → sqlite3WalCheckpoint → pwrite/unixRead`.
- 22 `sqlite3 -cmd .timeout 15000` children of OpenCode processes were queued, one of them for 17 h. `sqlite3 -readonly ... "PRAGMA ..."` returned `Error: in prepare, database is locked (5)` repeatedly, even with `.timeout 15000`.
- When the first holder exited, the next one, `session_tail_query.py`, immediately took over as sole holder.

## Root cause

A read-write connection that is the last one open checkpoints on close (SQLite default). A read-only connection (`file:...?mode=ro`, `uri=True`) never checkpoints, so it cannot take that exclusive lock. Other helpers in the same directory already use `?mode=ro` correctly, for example `report_token_efficiency.py:108`, `session-miner/extract.py:74` and `gh_transport_status.py:65`.

## Fix

Open these lookups read-only with a busy timeout:

```python
conn = sqlite3.connect(Path(db).resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=5)
```

Keep the existing `busy_timeout` and close the connection explicitly with `contextlib.closing`. Do not add writes.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker_lifecycle_resolve_session.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker_lifecycle_count_messages.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/session_tail_query.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/report_token_observability.py`

Before editing `report_token_observability.py`, confirm it never writes. Callers live in `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common*.sh`; check that none rely on these scripts creating the DB file. With `mode=ro`, a missing DB raises an error instead of creating an empty file; keep the existing missing-DB behaviour (print empty / exit 0) where callers expect it.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `sqlite3 -readonly -cmd ".timeout 15000" "file:$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db?mode=ro" "SELECT count(*) FROM session;"` (run while `lsof` shows a `worker_lifecycle_resolve_session.py` or `session_tail_query.py` holder)

**Actual output:** `Error: in prepare, database is locked (5)`. The holder's `sample` stack is in `sqlite3WalClose → sqlite3WalCheckpoint → pwrite`.

**Expected:** read-only lookups never block other readers.

Synthetic repro:

1. Create a WAL DB, write about 1,000 pages so the WAL is non-empty, and close nothing else.
2. Run `DB_PATH=<db> TITLE=x python3 worker_lifecycle_resolve_session.py` and watch it with `sample`/`py-spy`. On exit it checkpoints; while it does, a concurrent `sqlite3 -readonly <db> 'select 1'` gets `database is locked`.
3. With the `?mode=ro` URI, the WAL is left untouched on exit (`ls -l <db>-wal` size unchanged) and concurrent readers are never blocked.

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile` passes for all four files. Run any existing tests that import them (`rg -l 'worker_lifecycle_|session_tail_query|report_token_observability' .agents/scripts/tests`).
- With the reproducer, the WAL size is unchanged after each script exits.

## Related

#40302 (archive DB compaction) and the tiered-storage issue filed alongside this one.
