title: consolidated: public-triage model selection must skip Anthropic OAuth candidates it cannot authenticate
body:
_Supersedes #40393 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

`headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage` (the route behind the OpenCode `ai-research` tool and Pulse triage reviews) runs OpenCode pure (`OPENCODE_PURE=1`). Pure mode cannot load the plugin that implements Anthropic OAuth. Model selection still picks Anthropic OAuth candidates for this role, so the run is refused after launch by the trust-boundary check in `headless-runtime-invoke.sh` (`_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`, exit 86). The `standard` and `thinking` tiers are therefore always unusable for `ai-research` on installs where Anthropic auth is OAuth, even when another configured candidate in that tier is natively authenticated.

Make selection for the public-triage role treat "Anthropic OAuth under pure public triage" as a structural exclusion, the same way `chatgpt_oauth_unsupported` excludes ChatGPT OAuth models. Selection should fall through to the next natively authenticated candidate. If none remains, it should fail before launch with a named reason.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-25)

- In an interactive OpenCode session, `ai-research` with `model=thinking` and then `model=standard` both returned: "The isolated OpenCode runtime cannot authenticate the Anthropic OAuth provider for the <tier> tier. Pure public triage does not load the provider-auth plugin; select a provider with native authentication." The tool has no provider parameter, so that advice cannot be acted on. The session fell back to a staged `research-only` Task subagent, which cost extra calls and a manual file-staging step.
- `headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role triage --tier <t>` on the same install: simple=`openai/gpt-6-luna`, standard=`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, thinking=`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.
- `get_configured_models standard` lists `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` then `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (API key, native auth). Standard-tier triage could succeed but never reaches that candidate. `thinking` has only the Anthropic candidate.
- `opencode auth list` shows Anthropic as `oauth`.
- Related closed work: GH#38423 (fixed the research-staging error message only), GH#37205/#37207 (auto provider selection), t19061/GH#38620 (fix-the-fixer auth cooldown for the same refusal).

## How

Symbols below were verified on default branch commit `a28ddd56ff04` (line numbers in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`: `_headless_chatgpt_oauth_unsupported_ids` 94, `_headless_model_id_denied` 112, `get_configured_models` 130, `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons` 199, `tier_selection_unavailable_line` 244, `_first_healthy_configured_model` 405, `_choose_model_auto` 510, `choose_model` 561).

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`, give selection the public-triage context. Public triage means `role == triage` and not `--private-workload` (see `_headless_private_workload_enabled` in `headless-runtime-launch.sh:53` and the role check in `headless-runtime-run.sh:211`; `_select_cmd_run_model` at `headless-runtime-run.sh:162` already passes `$role` as the first argument of `choose_model`, so `headless-runtime-run.sh` needs no change). Thread `role` through `choose_model` → `_choose_model_auto` → `_first_healthy_configured_model` → `get_configured_models`, or set one scoped variable for the duration of selection. Do not read the role from an inherited environment variable a child could set.
2. In that context, skip a candidate whose provider is `anthropic` when the credential that `copy_scoped_opencode_auth` would copy is OAuth (the same `.anthropic.type == "oauth"` test used in `_invoke_opencode_copy_isolated_auth`, `headless-runtime-invoke.sh:94`). Keep that invoke-time check unchanged as defence-in-depth (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).
3. Add the same structural reason to `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons` (for example `public_triage_oauth_unsupported`), so `tier_selection_unavailable_line` names it when no candidate remains. Update the reason list in `headless-runtime-helper.sh` help text (near "chatgpt_oauth_unsupported (structural)", currently line 1270).
4. Reference pattern: the ChatGPT OAuth denylist handling in `get_configured_models` (`_headless_chatgpt_oauth_unsupported_ids` / `_headless_model_id_denied`) and in `tier_candidate_exclusion_reasons`.
5. Optional: when the tier has no triage-capable candidate, have `.opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts` `runtimeFailure` (line 111) say which tiers are usable instead of "select a provider with native authentication".

### Hazards and compatibility

- Selection is shared by worker, pulse and triage roles; the exclusion must apply only to public triage (`role == triage`, not `--private-workload`).
- The role must come from the selection call arguments, never an inherited environment variable.
- The invoke-time refusal (exit 86) stays; the new exclusion is an earlier, additional guard.
- A tier with only an Anthropic OAuth candidate (for example `thinking`) must fail before launch, with no OpenCode process spawned.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh
- EDIT: .opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With Anthropic auth of type OAuth, `select --role triage --tier standard` returns the next natively authenticated standard candidate (for example an `opencode-go/*` model), not `anthropic/*`.
- [ ] With no remaining candidate (for example `thinking` with only Anthropic OAuth), selection fails before launch with exit 75/1 and a `tier_selection_unavailable` line naming `public_triage_oauth_unsupported`. No OpenCode process is spawned.
- [ ] `--role worker` and `--role pulse` selection is unchanged: Anthropic OAuth stays selectable there.
- [ ] `--private-workload` behaviour is unchanged: it already requires an explicit `--model`.
- [ ] The invoke-time trust-boundary refusal in `headless-runtime-invoke.sh` remains.
- [ ] The `headless-runtime-helper.sh` help text lists `public_triage_oauth_unsupported (structural)` beside `chatgpt_oauth_unsupported`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- Live, read-only: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role triage --tier standard` and the same for `--role worker`. Compare before and after.
- If `.opencode/lib/ai-research-runtime.ts` changes: `bun run typecheck`.

## Context & Decisions

- Original problem statement, evidence, approach, scope and acceptance criteria: @alex-solovyev (parent #40393, interactive session).
- Fix-the-fixer classification (t3077, automated comment by @alex-solovyev's account): the issue touches the worker dispatch system (`headless-runtime-helper.sh`, `select`/`run --role triage`, which also serves Pulse triage reviews). Workers run with `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE=1`, `WORKER_STALL_TIMEOUT=180` and `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PREFLIGHT_SENTINEL=1`. Remove the `fix-the-fixer` label if this is wrong.
- Self-hosting tier override (t2819, automated): the pre-dispatch detector replaced the parent's lower workload-tier label with `tier:thinking` because `headless-runtime-helper.sh` appears in the body. That is automation, not a maintainer choice, so no `tier:*` label is copied here; the detector reapplies it if it matches. Bypass: `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1`.
- No scope changes, rejected ideas or superseded decisions appear in the parent thread. This spec adds only verified line references and the observation that `headless-runtime-run.sh` already passes `role` into `choose_model`.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev

title: fix(opencode-db-archive): global opencode.db archive pass never completes — 254 consecutive 60s deferrals, 84 GiB active DB
body:
## What

The hourly archive pass has **never** completed on the global DB `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Each run hits the 60 s per-DB budget and defers. Old sessions are therefore never moved out, and the active DB has grown to 85 GiB with **zero** free pages.

## Evidence (2026-11-25, macOS)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log`: **254** `Archive inventory outcome: db=…/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db rc=2` lines, preceded by `Archive deferred/partial: per-DB time budget exhausted (60s)`, and **0** `rc=0` lines over the log's whole history (first entry at line 41228).
- Active DB: `PRAGMA page_count` = 22,002,065 (4 KiB pages ≈ 84 GiB), `freelist_count` = 0. Nothing is being deleted from it.
- Sessions: 10,836 total (oldest 2026-09-30). **4,364 not updated for 30+ days**, above the documented `DEFAULT_INTERACTIVE_RETENTION_DAYS=30` / `DEFAULT_WORKER_RETENTION_DAYS=7` (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:66-67`).
- No TUI holds the global DB (interactive sessions use isolated project DBs). Contention comes from helper lookups instead; see #40415 for the lock convoy that can consume the whole 60 s budget.

## Likely causes (confirm before fixing)

1. Each 60 s pass may spend its budget on candidate scanning or integrity checks over an 85 GiB file before archiving the first batch. Check whether any committed batch happens in a typical pass (add per-batch progress logging).
2. Lock waits behind helper checkpoints (#40415) eat the budget.
3. There is no persisted resume cursor, so each pass may rescan from the start.

## Fix direction

- Log `archived N sessions / M rows` per committed batch so progress or no progress is visible.
- Select candidates oldest-first using an indexed predicate (`session.time_updated`) with a small `LIMIT`. Commit each batch before any heavyweight check, and persist a cursor.
- When a DB has been deferred K consecutive times (e.g. 6), raise its per-DB budget for that pass or schedule a dedicated catch-up run. Never loop silently forever; emit one warning via the existing notice path.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -c 'db=.*/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db rc=2' ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log; rg -c 'db=.*/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db rc=0' ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log`

**Actual output:** `254` and no match (0). Meanwhile `SELECT count(*) FROM session WHERE time_updated < (strftime('%s','now')-30*86400)*1000` returns 4364.

**Expected:** on a host with eligible sessions, successive passes reduce that count until it reaches zero.

## Verification

- On a fixture DB with many eligible sessions, repeated `archive --max-duration-seconds 60` passes each commit at least one batch and the eligible count falls monotonically.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` is clean.

## Related

#40415 (lock convoy), #40302 (archive compaction), and the tiered segmented-storage issue that depends on this.

title: feat(opencode-db): tiered session storage — small hot DB + monthly sealed immutable archive segments so backups copy long-term history once
body:
## Goal (owner direction)

> "we should be somehow splicing the database so that long-term storage doesn't change, and only short-term data fills each session/day/week"

Split OpenCode session storage so long-term history goes into **sealed, immutable files**. Only a small, recent working set should change day to day. Backups (Time Machine, Backblaze) would then copy each sealed file once instead of re-copying tens of GB every hour. VACUUM and lock windows also stay short because the hot file stays small.

## Current state (evidence, 2026-11-25, macOS)

| File | Size | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (hot) | 84 GiB, 0 free pages | constantly; included in Time Machine |
| `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-archive.db` | 18.4 GiB after manual VACUUM (was 29.7 GiB, 38% free) | every archive pass |
| per-project `opencode-archive.db` | up to 24 GiB, 89% free before manual VACUUM (#40302) | every archive pass |

- `tmutil isexcluded` returns `[Included]` for the global `opencode.db` and `opencode-archive.db`. The owner wants to keep backing them up, so the fix must reduce churn, not exclude the files.
- The hot DB holds 4,364 sessions idle for 30+ days because the archiver never completes on it (#40418).
- A single ever-growing archive file means every archive batch or event expiry rewrites pages in one large file, which Time Machine then copies again in full.

## Design

1. **Hot tier**: `opencode.db`, unchanged location (OpenCode owns it). Holds only sessions inside retention (7 d worker / 30 d interactive). Depends on #40418 actually draining it. Target steady state: a few GiB.
2. **Warm segment**: `opencode-archive-YYYY-MM.db`, beside the existing archive. This is the only archive file written in a given month. Archive batches go into the segment for the **current** month, the month the session was archived.
3. **Sealing**: once a segment's month has ended plus a grace period (default 7 days, configurable), run `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` → `VACUUM` → `quick_check`. Record `{segment, sessions, bytes, sha256, sealed_at}` in a small manifest, then `chmod 0444` the file. A sealed segment is never written again. This replaces #40302's periodic archive VACUUM with a one-time VACUUM at seal.
4. **Index**: a small `opencode-archive-index.db` (or JSON manifest) maps `session_id → segment`. It is the only archive-side file that changes after sealing, and it stays tiny.
5. **Restore without mutation**: `opencode-db-archive-restore.sh` / `opencode-session-restart-helper.sh` copy a session from its sealed segment back into the hot DB and mark it restored in the **index**, never in the sealed segment. When the session ages out again, it is re-archived into the current warm segment and the index is updated, so the newest copy wins.
6. **Expiry of archived events** (`--events-only`) applies only to the warm segment. Sealed segments are final, so expire before sealing.
7. **One-time migration**: split the existing `opencode-archive.db` (global and per-project) by archive time, or by `session.time_updated` when that's unavailable, into monthly segments, then seal every completed month. Keep the original file until each segment's `quick_check` and its row counts match the source. Then move the original to the trash path the storage-lifecycle helpers use, never `rm -rf`.
8. **Readers**: everything that reads `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_DB` must resolve through the index or iterate segments: session lookup, the maintenance report, storage inventory, session attachments, profile README data and session time. Open read-only (`?mode=ro`, see #40415).

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-retention.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-schema.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-inventory-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-sessions.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-report.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-window.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/session-attachments-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/session_time_db.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-store-policies.md`

Discover the complete reader list with `rg -n 'OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_DB|opencode-archive.db' .agents/scripts`.

## Phasing (one PR each; `For #<this>` until the last)

1. Index plus segment resolution in all readers, with the single legacy archive treated as one unsealed segment. No behaviour change.
2. Writer switch: new archive batches go to the current monthly segment. Add sealing and the manifest.
3. Migration of the existing archives, plus updated docs in `storage-lifecycle-store-policies.md`.

## Verification

- Fixture with sessions archived across 3 months: after phase 2, the two completed months are sealed (`0444`, manifest sha256 matches) and only the current segment's mtime changes across further archive passes.
- Restoring a session from a sealed segment leaves the segment's sha256 unchanged and puts the session in the hot DB. Re-archiving lands it in the current segment, and lookups return the newest copy.
- Migration: row counts per table across all segments equal the original archive, and every segment passes `quick_check`.
- The existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` and `test-opencode-session-lookup-helper.sh` pass; `shellcheck` is clean.
- Real host: after a week, `tmutil` reports only the hot DB, the current segment and the index as changed files under `~/.local/share/opencode/`.

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=remaining-scope -->
## Remaining scope after merged phases (brief owner reconciliation, 2026-11-26)

Already merged. Do not redo these:

- #40474: phase 1, readers resolve segments (`opencode-db-archive-segments-lib.sh`, maintenance report/sessions, storage inventory, session attachments, profile README data, `session_time_db.py`)
- #40475: phase 2, monthly writer, sealing and manifest (`opencode-db-archive-seal-lib.sh`)
- #40478: phase 3, legacy migration and `storage-lifecycle-store-policies.md` docs (`opencode-db-archive-migrate-lib.sh`)
- #40480: archive index with restored marks (`opencode-db-archive-index-lib.sh`, restore path)

One gap remains, and it is the final deliverable:

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh` `_restore_archived_worker_session()` (around line 593) returns 1 when the legacy `opencode-archive.db` is missing: `[[ -f "${shared_db%/*}/opencode-archive.db" ]] || return 1`. Phase 3 migration moves that legacy file to trash, so after migration, archived worker sessions held only in monthly segments are never restored before `--session <id> --continue`. Fix: gate on "any archive exists" through the existing segment/index resolution (`opencode-db-archive-segments-lib.sh` / `opencode-db-archive-index-lib.sh`). Keep passing the legacy path as `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_DB` so `opencode-db-archive.sh restore` resolves through the index, as `opencode-session-restart-helper.sh` already does.
- In the same PR, re-run `rg -n 'opencode-archive\.db' .agents/scripts` and fix any other existence check that still requires the legacy file. Leave plain path pass-through to `opencode-db-archive.sh` unchanged, because that helper resolves segments itself.

Verification: a fixture with no legacy `opencode-archive.db` and a session in `opencode-archive-YYYY-MM.db` plus the index. `_restore_archived_worker_session` must restore the session into the hot DB, and the sealed segment's sha256 must stay unchanged. Also run `test-opencode-db-archive.sh`, `test-opencode-db-archive-seal.sh` and the headless-runtime database tests, and keep `shellcheck` clean.

This is the last code item, so its PR may use `Resolves #40419`. The "Real host: after a week" `tmutil` check is a post-merge observation, not worker scope.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
## Depends on / related

- #40418 (hot DB must actually drain; do this first)
- #40415 (read-only lookups; avoids lock convoys)
- #40302 (archive VACUUM; superseded by seal-time VACUUM once phase 2 lands)

title: t19395: fix(headless-runtime): seed worker DB from a cached schema template when the shared OpenCode DB is locked
body:
## Task


When a worker's fresh isolated OpenCode DB cannot be initialised because the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is lock-held, seed it from a cached schema template instead of failing the launch. After every successful live initialisation, snapshot the new data-empty worker DB (schema, `user_version`, migration ledgers; no session data) as that template.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a worker's fresh isolated OpenCode DB cannot be initialised because the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is lock-held, seed it from a cached schema template instead of failing the launch. After every successful live initialisation, snapshot the new data-empty worker DB (schema, `user_version`, migration ledgers; no session data) as that template.

## Why

Worker launches die before the model starts with exit 86 (`Worker database could not initialise from the shared OpenCode schema`, result `local_error`, `prelaunch_abort ... stage=post_attempt_observers_start cause=worker_runtime_not_invoked`):

- `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`: 58 exit-86 attempts from 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-25 (17 on 2026-11-25). Each costs ~62 s, a dispatch slot and a re-dispatch cycle.
- Worker log `pulse-awardsapp-awardsapp-35717.log` (2026-11-25T20:06-20:07Z): `db_schema_init_retry attempt=1/5 ... 5/5 step=read_shared_schema detail=Error: database is locked`, then the error and exit 86. The retry budget from GH#39417 (5 attempts, 2+4+8+16 s sleeps, 5 s busy timeout each) recovered only once across 12 logged episodes: lock episodes outlast it.
- The shared DB is 91.6 GB (WAL mode). A worker needs only its schema and migration ledgers, which change only when OpenCode migrates.

A template captured in one initialisation is self-consistent (schema and ledger rows together), so OpenCode on worker start applies any newer migrations to it. `_merge_worker_db` still requires `_opencode_db_graph_schema_matches` before merging back, so a mismatch is retained for recovery rather than merged.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`: add a template path helper (`AIDEVOPS_WORKER_DB_TEMPLATE`, default `$HOME/.aidevops/cache/opencode-worker-db-template.db`), a store helper (sqlite `.backup` to a per-PID temp file with umask 077, then `mv`), and a seed helper (copy, then require `PRAGMA quick_check` = ok and at least one non-empty migration ledger).
2. In `_initialize_worker_db_from_shared_schema`: on success, store the template (best effort). On a failed attempt whose SQLite detail says `locked` or `busy`, seed from the template immediately and log `[lifecycle] db_schema_init_from_template`; without a valid template keep the existing bounded retries.
3. Continuation seeding (`_seed_worker_db_session_context`) needs live session rows, so it keeps failing closed to a fresh session as today.

## Acceptance

- A test in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh` (pattern: `test_fresh_worker_db_initializes_shared_schema_before_session_merge`): a successful init writes the template; with the shared DB write-locked by a held `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`, a later init succeeds from the template without sleeping through the retries, and the worker DB carries the ledger rows; with no template, the locked init still fails after the bounded retries.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-harness.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh`

title: t19396: email-sieve-helper: one hardened ManageSieve client with generic copy-to/copy-to-remove (Purelymail wraps it)
body:
## Task


One hardened ManageSieve client (RFC 5804) for every Sieve server, with keep-and-copy available to any mailbox:

- `email-sieve-helper.sh copy-to --server HOST --user ADDR --target ADDR [--secret NAME] [--script NAME] [--port N] [--dry-run]`
- `email-sieve-helper.sh copy-to-remove --server HOST --user ADDR [--secret NAME] [--script NAME] [--port N] --yes`
- The existing `list-scripts`, `show-script`, `deploy` and `delete-script` commands use the same client.
- `purelymail-helper.sh sieve-list|copy-to|copy-to-remove` keep their CLI and output unchanged, but delegate to `email-sieve-helper.sh` with `--server mailserver.purelymail.com`.

## Done when

- [ ] Only one ManageSieve client remains, and `email-sieve-helper.sh` has no embedded Python client.
- [ ] `email-sieve-helper.sh copy-to --dry-run` prints the Roundcube-format keep-and-copy script without connecting.
- [ ] Regression: `purelymail-helper.sh copy-to` keeps its positional CLI and dry-run output.
- [ ] Regression: the client refuses to run with no host configured.
- [ ] `tests/test-email-sieve-helper.sh` passes, and ShellCheck reports zero violations on both helpers.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/purelymail_sieve.py` → `git mv` to `.agents/scripts/managesieve_client.py`. Host is read from `SIEVE_HOST`, then legacy `PURELYMAIL_SIEVE_HOST`; port from `SIEVE_PORT`, then `PURELYMAIL_SIEVE_PORT`, default 4190. With no host set, exit 2 with a usage error; drop the hard-coded Purelymail default from the client. Keep the `PASSWORD_VAR USER OP ARGS` argv contract and the `list/get/install/remove` ops. Update module docstrings, which say "Purelymail". Keep the parked-name constant and the pre-TLS capability tolerance, which is harmless on RFC-compliant servers.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/email-sieve-helper.sh`: delete the embedded heredoc client and its temp-file writing. Route `list-scripts`, `show-script`, `deploy` (= `install`) and `delete-script` (= `get` then `remove NAME CURRENT`) through `managesieve_client.py` inside `secret-helper.sh NAME -- ...` injection. The secret name comes from `--secret` (default `SIEVE_PASSWORD`, so `aidevops secret set SIEVE_PASSWORD` keeps working). If `SIEVE_PASSWORD` is already in the environment, existing behaviour is kept: call the client directly with that variable name. Add `copy-to` and `copy-to-remove` by moving `_pm_sieve_copy_script`, `_pm_sieve_same`, `_pm_sieve_copy_target`, `cmd_copy_to` and `cmd_copy_to_remove` from `purelymail-helper.sh`, renamed with a `_sieve_` prefix. `--script` defaults to `roundcube`, matching Roundcube's own script name so the filter stays editable in webmail.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/purelymail-helper.sh` (Sieve block, about lines 162-172 and 876-1040): replace with thin wrappers that call `email-sieve-helper.sh <cmd> --server "${PURELYMAIL_SIEVE_HOST:-mailserver.purelymail.com}" --user ADDR --secret NAME ...`. Positional arguments, messages, `--dry-run` and `--yes` stay exactly as today. Remove `_pm_inner_sieve` and the `__sieve` internal command.

- `EDIT: .agents/services/email/purelymail.md` section "Keep and copy (Sieve filter)": note that it wraps `email-sieve-helper.sh copy-to`.
- `EDIT: .agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`: add a short "Mail filters (Sieve)" note. ManageSieve is at `my.<domain>:4190`; authenticate with the mailbox address and a Cloudron app password (`mail` scope). Cloudron mailboxes also have native `forwards`/`skipInbox` settings in the dashboard; prefer those when no Sieve logic is needed.
- `EDIT: tests/test-email-sieve-helper.sh`: update assertions that depend on the embedded client or the `SIEVE_PASSWORD`-only flow. Add no new harness.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `purelymail-helper.sh` (`_pm_sieve`, `cmd_sieve_list`, `cmd_copy_to`, `cmd_copy_to_remove`) and `email-sieve-helper.sh` (`deploy_sieve` and the list/show/delete functions). Check other callers with `rg -n "purelymail_sieve|email-sieve-managesieve|MANAGESIEVE_PYTHON_HELPER" .agents tests`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** ManageSieve `PUTSCRIPT`, `SETACTIVE`, `RENAMESCRIPT` and `DELETESCRIPT`, only inside `managesieve_client.py`.

- Never put the password in argv or output. Keep the `secret-helper.sh NAME -- cmd` injection pattern; the client reads the variable by name.

## Task Brief

## What

One hardened ManageSieve client (RFC 5804) for every Sieve server, with keep-and-copy available to any mailbox:

- `email-sieve-helper.sh copy-to --server HOST --user ADDR --target ADDR [--secret NAME] [--script NAME] [--port N] [--dry-run]`
- `email-sieve-helper.sh copy-to-remove --server HOST --user ADDR [--secret NAME] [--script NAME] [--port N] --yes`
- The existing `list-scripts`, `show-script`, `deploy` and `delete-script` commands use the same client.
- `purelymail-helper.sh sieve-list|copy-to|copy-to-remove` keep their CLI and output unchanged, but delegate to `email-sieve-helper.sh` with `--server mailserver.purelymail.com`.

## Why

There are now two ManageSieve clients:

1. `.agents/scripts/purelymail_sieve.py` (GH#40230, PR #40262, v3.39.280) handles a pre-TLS capability re-send, synchronises after TLS with `NOOP`, keeps passwords out of argv and removes scripts safely (rename aside, verify, then delete).
2. A simpler Python client embedded as a heredoc in `.agents/scripts/email-sieve-helper.sh` (around lines 600-850, written to a temp file at runtime). It only checks the greeting for `STARTTLS` and has none of the hardening above.

Keep-and-copy is also useful on non-Purelymail servers. **Live evidence (2026-11-25):** on a Cloudron 10.1.6 mail server (Dovecot Pigeonhole, `my.<cloudron-domain>:4190`, auth with a Cloudron app password, `mail` scope), the released `purelymail-helper.sh` with `PURELYMAIL_SIEVE_HOST` pointed at the server passed this sequence:

- `sieve-list`: no scripts
- `copy-to`: script read back and active
- a test message was kept in the mailbox and a copy delivered to the target (IMAP search: 1 match in each mailbox)
- `copy-to-remove`: succeeded, including `RENAMESCRIPT`
- `sieve-list`: no scripts
- a second message was kept but not copied (0 matches in the target)

Only the host differs, so the right fix is one generic client, not a second provider helper.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** the design is decided below (file rename, environment variables, delegation direction, secret handling), but the worker must restructure two existing helpers and keep their CLIs and tests passing. That needs judgement about local refactoring, not new decisions.

## Context & Decisions

- Why not IMAP/SMTP? Re-sending from a client needs an always-on poller and breaks SPF/DMARC alignment. A server-side Sieve `redirect :copy` avoids both.
- Purelymail live write-path verification is requested from the original reporter on GH#40230. Cloudron/Dovecot verification is recorded above.
- Follow-up from GH#40230.

- `.agents/scripts/purelymail_sieve.py:192-256`: ops and the `OPS` table.
- `.agents/scripts/purelymail-helper.sh:876-1040`: copy-to logic to move.

## What

title: t19397: fix(terminal-blocker): checkpoint triage can classify live lock contention as resource_contended
body:
## Task


Let the released-checkpoint LLM triage (`_terminal_blocker_triage_unknown`) return `resource_contended`. Today its prompt and its `jq` allowlist omit that class, so a worker report that describes live lock contention without a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=` line can only become `unknown` or `runner_capability_unmet`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Let the released-checkpoint LLM triage (`_terminal_blocker_triage_unknown`) return `resource_contended`. Today its prompt and its `jq` allowlist omit that class, so a worker report that describes live lock contention without a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=` line can only become `unknown` or `runner_capability_unmet`.

## Why

- t19285 (GH#39887) added `resource_contended` to the worker contract (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:203-210`), the reason allowlist, the recovery text and the per-issue dispatch backoff (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-backoff-helper.sh:240-274`). It did not add the class to the triage fallback (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:495` prompt and `:510` `jq` filter).
- Local evidence (`~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl`, 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-25): 59 `terminal_blocker_captured` events describe a shared sign-in lock held by another live session. 9 were `resource_contended`; 38 were `runner_capability_unmet` and 10 `unknown`. Most of the misclassification stopped once the product repo's briefs started naming the explicit line, but undeclared reports still go to triage: 3 of 9 lock-contention captures since then were `unknown`.
- Wrong class cost: `unknown` is held by `_hrff_blocked_exit_holds` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:541-547`); `runner_capability_unmet` arms the worker-observation capability cooldown (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`, `_dispatch_capability_cooldown_from_observation`). `resource_contended` instead returns the issue to `status:available` after a 10-60 minute per-issue backoff, with no person involved.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `_terminal_blocker_triage_unknown`, add `resource_contended` to the prompt's reason list, with one sentence: it means a shared lock, lease or serialized resource held by another live session that did not free within the helper's bounded wait; a lock held on this runner awaiting operator reconciliation stays `runner_capability_unmet`.
2. Add `resource_contended` to the `pending_only == false` alternation in the `jq` decision filter on the next lines.
3. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `test_unknown_triage`, add `resource_contended` to the reason loop so the parser maps it to `known:resource_contended`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- A triage response `{"reason":"resource_contended","owner":"","pending_only":false}` yields `AIDEVOPS_TERMINAL_BLOCKER_TRIAGE=known:resource_contended`, and `terminal_blocker_capture_output` then fingerprints the capture as `resource_contended`.
- `resource_contended` with `pending_only:true` is still rejected (no `pending_work`).
- Existing triage classes behave unchanged.

title: opencode-db maintain: 3x-free-space VACUUM gate defers forever on a bloated DB; add VACUUM INTO fallback
body:
## Problem

`aidevops opencode-db maintain` can never reclaim a bloated OpenCode database on a
disk that is not large enough to hold three copies of it. It defers every run,
forever, and reports success ("deferred") while free pages keep growing.

Observed on this machine today:

```
$ aidevops opencode-db report
  DB size:       8.52 GB
  Pages:         2234249 (page_size=4096B)
  Free pages:    1695283 (75.88% of total)
  Last maintenance run:
    timestamp: 2026-11-25T04:37:15Z
    outcome:   deferred
    bytes_reclaimed: 0
```

Disk free: 19 GiB. Required by the current gate: `db_kb * 3` ≈ 27.4 GiB, so
`_maintain_vacuum_capacity` returns `insufficient-capacity` on every scheduled run
and VACUUM is skipped with 0 bytes reclaimed. The DB is 76% dead pages, which is
the reported cause of slow session loads and UI stalls.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-maintain.sh:80-103` —
`_maintain_vacuum_capacity()` hard-requires `VACUUM_FREE_SPACE_MULTIPLIER` (3,
defined at `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh:148`) times the DB
size. The comment justifies it: VACUUM may need one DB-sized temp copy plus one
DB-sized WAL, plus a safety margin.

That is correct for in-place `VACUUM`, which writes its temp copy next to the file.
It is not correct for `VACUUM INTO`, which writes only the compacted result.

## Proposed change

When the 3x gate fails, attempt a fallback before deferring:

1. Compute `expected_kb` from live data, not file size:
   `(page_count - freelist_count) * page_size`, plus WAL, plus a safety margin.
2. Require only `expected_kb * 2` free (compacted copy + margin).
3. If satisfied: `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, `VACUUM INTO <tmp>`,
   `PRAGMA quick_check` on the result, compare row counts for
   `session`/`session_v2`/`message`/`part` against the source, `mv` the source to
   `<db>.pre-vacuum-<ts>`, `mv` the temp into place, remove stale `-wal`/`-shm`.
4. Report `bytes_reclaimed` from the swap, and keep the previous DB until the next
   successful run (or an explicit `--prune-backups`).
5. If even the fallback cannot fit, keep deferring, but log the individual numbers
   (`expected_kb`, `available_kb`) so the operator sees why.

Keep the existing in-place VACUUM path when 3x free space is available — it is
cheaper than moving a multi-GB file.

## Verification

- Unit: synthetic SQLite DB with >50% freelist and a mocked
  `aidevops_disk_capacity_snapshot` below 3x but above the fallback threshold →
  expect `vacuum_ran=true`, compacted file, equal row counts, `outcome=success`.
- Unit: mocked capacity below the fallback threshold → expect `deferred` with both
  numbers logged.
- Integration: on a real 8.5 GB/76%-free DB with 19 GiB free, `maintain` shrinks the
  file and preserves `session_v2`, `message`, and `part` counts.

## Scope

- Target files: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-maintain.sh`,
  `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh` (constant/docs),
  `tests/` for the helper.
- Related but separate: stale lock directories under
  `~/.local/state/opencode/locks/` (44 present, every recorded PID dead, oldest
  Oct 26) are written by OpenCode core, not by this framework, so they are not part
  of this change.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: t19399: fix(watchdog): let the elapsed cap wait for an in-flight tool's declared timeout
body:
## Task


The worker activity watchdog kills workers at the elapsed cap while a bounded tool call is still in flight. Make the elapsed cap wait for the newest tool started in this attempt to reach its own declared OpenCode timeout, bounded to 30 minutes plus a 60-second grace. The remaining confirmed-stall chain (CI wait, DB update, network, CPU, else stall kill) is unchanged, so a silent hung tool is still killed. The 3h sandbox timeout remains the absolute backstop.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The worker activity watchdog kills workers at the elapsed cap while a bounded tool call is still in flight. Make the elapsed cap wait for the newest tool started in this attempt to reach its own declared OpenCode timeout, bounded to 30 minutes plus a 60-second grace. The remaining confirmed-stall chain (CI wait, DB update, network, CPU, else stall kill) is unchanged, so a silent hung tool is still killed. The 3h sandbox timeout remains the absolute backstop.

## Why (evidence)

Local metrics `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`, last 48h: `watchdog_stall_killed` = 26 runs / 1090 worker-minutes, the largest pure-loss result class. Since t19336 (GH#40157) deployed, every cap kill in `pulse-dispatch.log` is `hard_kill_cap_active` with `cap_liveness=network_active` at 49-77 min elapsed.

For 8 of the 9 cap kills since 11-24T23:00Z, the killed session's newest tool part in the OpenCode DB was a `bash` part with `state.status = running` and a declared `state.input.timeout`:

- 5 lock-wrapped staging QA checks in a private managed repo, timeout 1800000 ms
- 2 staging data-publication scripts in the same repo
- 1 `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait ... --timeout 1200`, timeout 1300000 ms

Example: one worker had finished publication, started its final staging QA check at 11:50:35Z with a 30-minute tool timeout, and was killed at 12:01:35Z (elapsed 4589s). Every affected issue later succeeded on redispatch, so each kill cost about 50 minutes of model time plus a repeated publication/QA step.

Root cause: GH#39197/GH#40157 count only *streamed* part updates as DB progress. Tools that print nothing until completion (lock waits, `| tail`, CI waits) leave `part.time_updated` stale, so the cap treats a live bounded tool as a stall.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh`:
  - New `_watchdog_inflight_tool_deadline`: read the isolated worker DB (`WORKER_DB`) for running tool parts whose `state.time.start` is at or after `_MONITOR_START_EPOCH` and whose `state.input.timeout` is a positive integer. Return the latest bounded deadline `start + min(timeout, WORKER_STALL_INFLIGHT_TOOL_MAX_SECONDS) + 60`. Fail open (no deferral) when there is no DB, no sqlite3, an old schema, or invalid values.
  - In `_monitor_enforce_hard_kill`, after the GH#40157 DB extension, return 0 while `now < deadline`. Log one `[lifecycle] worker_cap_deferred_inflight_tool` event per tool part.
  - `_parse_args`: validate `WORKER_STALL_INFLIGHT_TOOL_MAX_SECONDS` (default 1800; 0 disables; invalid falls back to 1800).

title: t19400: fix(opencode-db-archive): scan recent pulse logs in one pass so archive fits its per-DB budget
body:
## Task


`get_active_worker_sessions` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` forks a `_file_mtime_epoch` subshell plus `stat` for every retained `pulse-*.log` on each call. Pulse keeps 48 h of worker logs (720+ files on a busy host), so each call costs about 1,450 forks before any SQLite work. It runs inside the per-DB archive deadline, once or more per DB (worker-event filter, retention, archive selection). Replace the per-file loop with one `find -mmin -60` plus one batched `grep`, keeping the exact output: sorted unique UUIDs from pulse logs modified in the last hour.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Pulse keeps 48 h of worker logs (720+ files on a busy host), so each call costs about 1,450 forks before any SQLite work. Replace the per-file loop with one `find -mmin -60` plus one batched `grep`, keeping the exact output: sorted unique UUIDs from pulse logs modified in the last hour.

body:
## Task


Add a maintainer-only runtime-verification waiver to the interactive merge path, modelled on the existing review-bot-gate override (GH#36901):

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <REPO> --waive-runtime-verification="<reason, 20+ chars>"`

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-25, interactive maintainer session
- **Evidence:** PR #40194 (GH#40135). The maintainer explicitly waived live runtime verification. The OpenAI org had no credits, and the feature was built to the published API documentation. No supported route recorded that decision:
  - `full-loop-helper.sh merge` refused with `runtime verification is pending (runtime-pending)`.
  - A direct `gh pr merge` is correctly blocked by command policy (`github.pr-merge-direct`).
  - The PR finally merged only after the PR body's `Risk level` was hand-edited from Critical to Medium with `self-assessed` verification. That works, but it leaves no dedicated audit record, and it encourages risk relabelling as a bypass.

## What

Add a maintainer-only runtime-verification waiver to the interactive merge path, modelled on the existing review-bot-gate override (GH#36901):

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <REPO> --waive-runtime-verification="<reason, 20+ chars>"`

## Why

A maintainer can legitimately accept the risk of skipping a live test, for example when there is no paid account or test hardware, or when the change is documentation-driven. Today the only way through is to change the declared risk level. That misstates the PR, and the decision is never recorded as a waiver.

## Tier

tier:standard. Narrow change that follows an existing in-file pattern.

## How (Approach)

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
  - Parse `--waive-runtime-verification=REASON` next to `--override-review-bot-gate=*` (around line 1416).
  - Add `_merge_prepare_runtime_waiver`, `_merge_verify_runtime_waiver_approval` and `_merge_record_runtime_waiver`, copying `_merge_prepare_rbg_override` / `_merge_verify_rbg_override_approval` / `_merge_record_rbg_override` (lines 1656-1730).
  - Requirements:
    - interactive-only;
    - reason of at least 20 characters;
    - cryptographic maintainer approval of the PR (same verdict check as the RBG override);
    - after the merge, post a PR comment and add an `audit-log-helper.sh log security.event` entry recording the PR, head SHA, merge SHA and reason.
- Where `_runtime_testing_merge_refusal` is called (around line 1836), skip only the `runtime-pending` and High/Critical-without-`runtime-verified` refusals when a verified waiver is active. Keep the malformed-metadata and ambiguous-section refusals.

- Docs: one line in `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` or `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md` next to the `verify-runtime` guidance. Pointer only; do not add to always-loaded AGENTS.md.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An interactive merge with `--waive-runtime-verification="..."` and a verified maintainer approval merges a Critical, `runtime-pending` PR without editing its body.
- [ ] Headless sessions, short reasons, or a missing/invalid approval are refused before any merge transport.

title: fix(terminal-blocker): external_trigger hold still flaps status:blocked <-> status:available across runners after #40092
body:
## What

Follow-up to #40068 / PR #40092. The same `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency` <-> `status:available` label flap recurs on runners at v3.39.277+ (after the #40092 fix shipped).

Observed on one private managed-repo issue (number withheld; held by an `external_trigger_pending` terminal-blocker observation with a `Recheck after:` date; its only native `blocked_by` issue is closed/completed):

- 2026-11-25: 22 `status:blocked` re-applications and 22 releases from two other runners, cadence 10-90 minutes, no dispatch, no claim, no new comments after a single `terminal-blocker-rearmed ... reason=revision_changed` receipt at 01:14Z.
- Release shape: one edit removing `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency` and adding `status:available` (same second). Re-block shape: add `needs-dependency`, remove `status:available`, add `status:blocked` over 2-4 s (separate edits) — identical to #40068.
- The flap continued after the dated hold expired (re-blocks at 21:32Z and 23:19Z; recheck_after was 21:11Z).
- On this runner, `pulse.log` shows the re-block side at least once: `TRIGGER_REVISIT repo=<private> issue=<N> label=status:blocked` (16:32Z), and dispatch dedup blocking with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_DATED_HOLD` then `brief_scope_hold signal=brief_scope_status_blocked` (benign). This runner's own `rearm` pass logs `rearm_decision ... observed_rev=a04f… current_rev=a04f… reason=unchanged`, while the other runner's public receipt reported `observed_rev=a04f… current_rev=aeae… reason=revision_changed` for the same body.
- Comparison: other blocked issues in the same repo had 1-2 block events that day; the flap is specific to the external-trigger hold whose native blocker is closed.

## Why it matters

GitHub API spend on multiple runners (~66 label writes/day for one issue) for zero progress; label churn changes owner digests and resurfaces recovery-queue entries.

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=reproducer -->
## Reproducer

Unconfirmed investigation; the live reproducer is observational:

1. An `auto-dispatch` issue whose worker ended `BLOCKED` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON` mapped to `external_trigger_pending`, so the observation comment carries `Recheck after: <ISO>` and the issue gets `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency`.
2. Its only native `blocked_by` issue is closed/completed.
3. Two or more runners (v3.39.277+) run pulse against the repo.
4. `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>/timeline --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.event=="labeled" or .event=="unlabeled") | [.created_at,.actor.login,.event,.label.name] | @tsv'` shows repeated release/re-block pairs with no new comments.

Local fixture path: extend `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh` with two revision computations for the same body/comments under the two code paths named below and assert equal revisions.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
## Hypotheses (verify before changing code)

1. Revision digest instability across runners/versions: the rearm pass on one runner computes a different `current_rev` for an unchanged body, so it keeps treating the hold as re-armed by a revision change and releases it; the rearm receipt is deduplicated by key, so repeat releases are silent.
2. Release by `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` (`_der_try_unblock`) because the only native blocker is closed, with `_der_comments_after_dependency_conversion` still dropping the observation on some path #40092 did not cover (e.g. the `CLAIM_RELEASED ... terminal-blocker-observation` comment).
3. Re-block by `terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit` / dated-hold projection or `pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh` blocked-companion repair (`:273`).

## Files to inspect / likely modify

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh` (rearm receipt and `revision_changed` decision, ~`:244`, `:419`)
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (`rearm_decision`, ~`:928`; revision computation)
- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` (`_der_comments_after_dependency_conversion` ~`:493-540`, `_der_try_unblock`)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh` (`:273`)
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-reopen.sh` (`terminal_blocker_dated_hold_active`)
- Exact writer pair is not yet identified: the unblock/re-block edits are not in `gh-audit.log` (only `_hrff_project_blocked_exit` writes are). Adding audit coverage for those writers is in scope if needed to identify them.

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=files-scope -->
### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-reopen.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
## Acceptance

- For an `external_trigger_pending` hold with a closed native blocker and an unchanged body, every runner computes the same revision and no mechanical path releases it before its `Recheck after:` date or a trusted retry/brief revision.
- After the recheck date passes, exactly one path owns the release (or the supervisor re-records the hold) and no other path re-blocks it in a loop.
- Regression coverage in the existing `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit*.sh` / `tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh` suites, matching the PR #40092 pattern.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh`
- Live: the affected issue's timeline shows no further `status:blocked` <-> `status:available` flips for 24h after deployment on all runners.

title: aidevops_sessions ask does not wake idle OpenCode TUI sessions (silent failure)
body:
## Observed

From a Buzz-bridged OpenCode session, `aidevops_sessions` `action=ask` was sent to two idle OpenCode TUI sessions on the same machine and repo. The tool reported each recipient as idle and said the question would wake it (well under the 6 wakes/hour cap).

After ~35 minutes neither session had replied. Both were still listed as idle with last activity unchanged (~2h earlier), and the sender's inbox showed no replies. The wake was never delivered or never started a turn, and the sender got no error.

## Expected

`ask` wakes the idle session and starts a turn, or returns an explicit delivery/wake failure so the caller can fall back.

## Impact

Cross-session coordination from remote (Buzz) sessions stalls silently; the remote user cannot get a status update.

## Suggested investigation

- Idle-wake path in the opencode-aidevops sessions relay for `kind: tui` sessions.
- Add a wake acknowledgement/receipt and surface failure in the `ask` result and in `show`/`inbox`.

## Verification

`ask` an idle TUI session with `wait_seconds`; confirm it becomes busy and replies, or that the sender receives an explicit wake-failed status.

title: OAuth MCP servers: terminal login never reaches aidevops-launched OpenCode sessions, and connect only reports status unknown
body:
## What

For OAuth-based remote MCP servers (seen with `sentry`), a user cannot get from "not logged in" to "connected" by following anything aidevops prints or documents:

1. `aidevops_mcp connect sentry` waits 30 seconds and fails with `MCP connect failed for sentry: MCP did not become ready (last status: unknown)`. Nothing says a login is needed.
2. The obvious repair, `opencode mcp auth sentry` in a normal terminal, succeeds but has no effect on the session. aidevops launches OpenCode with a per-project `XDG_DATA_HOME`, so the session reads `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/mcp-auth.json` while the terminal login writes `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json`.
3. `services/monitoring/sentry.md` still documents the retired local `@sentry/mcp-server` plus `SENTRY_YOURNAME` token setup, although the registry entry is now remote OAuth.
4. `mcp-diagnose.sh sentry` prints `Command not found: sentry` and `Try: npm install -g sentry`, which is wrong for a remote server.

## Evidence (one macOS host, aidevops 3.39.282 to 3.39.284, OpenCode 1.19.x, reporter is a user, not a maintainer)

- Registry: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs` has `name: "sentry"`, `type: "remote"`, `url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"`, with the comment "migrate away from legacy local+token config".
- Three separate connect attempts over nine days (two from the `sentry` agent, each with one retry) all returned `MCP did not become ready (last status: unknown)`.
- At the same time `opencode mcp auth list`, run from the session shell, showed `sentry  not authenticated`. Seven other remote servers showed the same state.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs`: `MCP_STATUS_VALUES` is `connected, connecting, disabled, error, failed`; anything else becomes `unknown`, and `waitForConnection()` polls until the 30-second deadline. The status OpenCode reports for a server that needs a login is therefore probably collapsed to `unknown` (not confirmed against the OpenCode API).
- After the user ran `opencode mcp auth sentry` in a normal terminal and approved in the browser:
  - `XDG_DATA_HOME=~/.local/share opencode mcp auth list` showed `sentry  authenticated`;
  - the same command in the session environment still showed `sentry  not authenticated`, and connect failed as before.
  - Session `XDG_DATA_HOME` was `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/<project-shard>`.
- After the user ran `XDG_DATA_HOME="<session data dir>" opencode mcp auth sentry`, the session showed `sentry  authenticated` and the `sentry` agent connected and called `sentry_whoami` successfully, without restarting the TUI.
- `rg 'mcp-auth|mcp auth'` over `.agents` (excluding tests) at `10d42d11c` matches only `scripts/opencode-runtime-switch-helper.sh`. No doc or helper tells the user how to log in for an isolated session store.

## Impact

Any OAuth MCP server (Sentry, Cloudflare, PostHog, Context7, Socket and others in the registry) is unusable in aidevops-launched OpenCode sessions until the user discovers the `XDG_DATA_HOME` detail on their own. In this case a Sentry investigation ran on user screenshots for nine days because the failure looked like a broken server rather than a missing login.

## Expected

Maintainer's choice; any of these would close the gap:

1. When activation fails and the server is an OAuth remote that is not authenticated, say so and print the exact login command for the current session store.
2. Provide one supported login path that targets the session's store (a helper or `aidevops` subcommand), or share MCP OAuth credentials across per-project stores.
3. Update `services/monitoring/sentry.md` to the OAuth flow and make `mcp-diagnose.sh` handle remote servers.

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs` — `MCP_STATUS_VALUES`, `waitForConnection()`, the user-visible failure message.
- EDIT: `.agents/services/monitoring/sentry.md` — setup and troubleshooting sections.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh` — remote-server branch.
- Where per-project `XDG_DATA_HOME` is set and whether credentials should be shared: path not known to the reporter.

## Verification

- In an aidevops-launched OpenCode session with no Sentry login, `aidevops_mcp connect sentry` from the `sentry` agent fails fast with a message that names the missing login and the command to run.
- After following only that message, connect succeeds and `sentry_whoami` returns.
- `mcp-diagnose.sh sentry` no longer suggests `npm install -g sentry`.

## Dispatch Hold

Reporter is an external user; choosing between a clearer message, a supported login path and shared credentials is a maintainer decision
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

They are the SQLite candidate/commit_gap cases, the per-DB preflight/batch deadline cases, and the GH#38590 in-flight-marker / halved-retry / oversized-deferral cases, roughly lines 1268-1420. Do this by not paying for a real `lsof` holder scan inside their 10 s budgets.

## Why

At load average ~110 on 16 cores, the same 7 cases fail on every run (PR #40450 evidence, 2026-11-26): 82 passed, 7 failed, both before and after sandboxing the pulse-log directory. The cause is measured. `opencode_db_holder_count` (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh:73-89`) runs `lsof -t <db>`, which scans every process and costs 1.4-2.7 s per call on that host. The archive runs at least three holder checks (`opencode-db-archive.sh:225`, the idle gate at `:275/:291`, and VACUUM at `:416`). Event expiry alone took 4-7 s on a 164 KB fixture, so the first copy never commits inside the 10 s budget. The cascaded checks then fail ("copy/delete gap archive copy mismatch", "in-flight marker missing", "oversized deferral mismatch"). Workers and verifiers that touch the archive helper run this suite locally (it is not in CI). False failures cost them time and invite "pre-existing failure" reasoning that hides real regressions. #40436's runtime verification depends on this suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` reports 0 failed, run twice, on a host with load average above 2x the core count (check with `sysctl -n vm.loadavg` and `sysctl -n hw.ncpu`, and record both in the PR).
2. `rg -n "OPENCODE_DB_HOLDER_COMMAND" .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` shows the dedicated holder-veto cases still using `$mock_holder` / `$mock_active_only`.
3. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` is clean.

## Context

Found while verifying t19400 / GH#40443 (PR #40450), which fixed the production causes of archive deferrals. Load at the time came mostly from desktop apps, not pulse workers.

## Task

## What

title: report-token-use misses sessions in per-project interactive OpenCode DBs (opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db)
body:
## Problem

`report-token-use-helper.sh report` reads one OpenCode database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, or the
single path in `AIDEVOPS_REPORT_TOKEN_USE_OPENCODE_DB`. Interactive sessions launched by aidevops keep their own
per-project database under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/<project-key>/opencode/opencode.db`
(plus `opencode-archive.db`). Those sessions are missing from the report, even when `--session <id>` names them:
the command returns `"sessions": []` with no warning.

Observed 2026-11-26 (aidevops 3.39.277, OpenCode 1.19.6): a 3-day interactive project session (7,670 requests,
122 subagent sessions, about $428 API-equivalent in `llm_requests`) and four earlier sessions of the same project
in another per-project DB were invisible to `report --session` and `report --since 30d --limit 5000`. Only headless
workers (global DB) appeared. Setting `AIDEVOPS_REPORT_TOKEN_USE_OPENCODE_DB` to each per-project DB in turn found
them, one DB per run.

The default `--runtime auto` also picked the Claude metrics path for an OpenCode session id and returned nothing.

## Expected

- `report` and `data` read every OpenCode DB: the global one, each `opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db`
  and its `opencode-archive.db`, deduplicating session ids.
- `--session <id>` searches all of them and says which DB it used; when nothing matches it prints
  "session not found in N databases" instead of an empty report.
- `--runtime auto` tries OpenCode when the id starts with `ses_`.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/report-token-use-helper.py`: `DEFAULT_OPENCODE_DB`, `_opencode_reports()` (around line 458),
  `_read_sessions()`, `_children_by_root()`; runtime selection for `auto`.
- `.agents/scripts/commands/report-token-use.md`: document the DB discovery.

## Verification

1. `report-token-use-helper.sh report --session <an interactive OpenCode session id> --json` returns one row with
   `child_session_count` > 0, without the environment override.
2. `report --since 7d --runtime opencode` row count equals the global DB rows plus the per-project DB rows in the
   window (no duplicates when the same id exists in a DB and its archive).
3. Existing tests for the helper pass.

title: t19404: feat(claim-task-id): warn when an auto-dispatch issue is filed in a pulse-off...
body:
## Task


`claim-task-id.sh` prints a non-blocking warning (stderr) when it is asked to create an `auto-dispatch` issue in a repository whose `repos.json` entry on this host has `pulse != true`, or which has no entry. The warning names the two ways out: implement it in the current session, or enable pulse for the repo.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `auto-dispatch pulse disabled repo stall` → 0 relevant hits — no prior lesson
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch `claim-task-id.sh` pulse handling in last 48h (`prework-discovery-helper.sh`)
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — complete function supplied, but the warning text and placement are a small judgement call
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — single-function change, brief carries the full code

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-26
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Autonomy baseline for the maintainer's "how far from efficient, reliable, autonomous" question. Of 36 `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` issues idle 7+ days across the maintainer's managed scope, 35 sat in repos whose local `repos.json` entry has `pulse: false` (30) or no entry (5), across 19 repos. Only 1 was in a pulse-on repo.

## What

`claim-task-id.sh` prints a non-blocking warning (stderr) when it is asked to create an `auto-dispatch` issue in a repository whose `repos.json` entry on this host has `pulse != true`, or which has no entry. The warning names the two ways out: implement it in the current session, or enable pulse for the repo.

## Why

An `auto-dispatch` label says "a worker will do this", but pulse never scans a pulse-off repo, so the issue waits silently until a person notices. The onboarding audit (`repo-onboarding-audit-lib.sh:70-86`) already writes a "Pulse off" advisory later, and `setup-debt-helper.sh` folds it into one generic toast line ("N repos have incomplete aidevops setup"). That arrives after the creating session has gone and does not say that work is waiting. The creating session has the most context and can usually implement the task on the spot.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** complete function and call site supplied; the worker only verifies placement, message wording and the existing claim tests.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — add `_warn_pulse_off_auto_dispatch` directly after `_warn_dispatch_path_auto_dispatch` (ends near line 1913), and call it in `_main_preclaim_discovery` right after the existing `_warn_dispatch_path_auto_dispatch` call (near line 1984).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** only `_main_preclaim_discovery` in `claim-task-id.sh`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none — read-only lookup of `repos.json`, output to stderr via `log_warn` (`shared-constants.sh:1079`, writes to stderr).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-stdout-isolation.sh` (stdout must stay machine-readable), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-auto-dispatch-no-assign.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** reads `${REPOS_FILE:-$HOME/.config/aidevops/repos.json}` (same default as `aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh:248`); no schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copy under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` refreshes on `setup.sh`; nothing generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A — advisory only; existing stalled issues are handled by the maintainer decision, not by this change.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the function and call; `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_OFF_CHECK=1` disables it without a revert.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the function after `_warn_dispatch_path_auto_dispatch`:

```bash
#
_warn_pulse_off_auto_dispatch() {
	[[ "${AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_OFF_CHECK:-}" == "1" ]] && return 0
	[[ ",${TASK_LABELS}," == *",auto-dispatch,"* ]] || return 0
	[[ "$NO_ISSUE" == "false" ]] || return 0
	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
	local repos_file="${REPOS_FILE:-$HOME/.config/aidevops/repos.json}"
	[[ -f "$repos_file" ]] || return 0
	local slug="" state=""
	slug=$(_extract_github_slug "$REPO_PATH" "$REMOTE_NAME")
	[[ -n "$slug" ]] || return 0
	state=$(jq -r --arg s "$slug" '
		[.initialized_repos[]? | select(((.slug // "") | ascii_downcase) == ($s | ascii_downcase))][0]
		| if . == null then "not registered" elif .pulse == true then "on" else "off" end' \
		"$repos_file" 2>/dev/null) || return 0
	[[ -z "$state" || "$state" == "on" ]] && return 0
	log_warn "Pulse is ${state} for ${slug} on this host: unless another runner pulses it, no worker will pick up this auto-dispatch issue."
	log_warn "  Implement it now: interactive-start-helper.sh --issue <N> --repo ${slug} --task \"...\" --auto-dispatch"
	log_warn "  Or enable dispatch for the repo: aidevops repos pulse on ${slug}"
	return 0
}
```

2. In `_main_preclaim_discovery`, directly after `_warn_dispatch_path_auto_dispatch`, add:

```bash
	# Pulse-off repos never dispatch auto-dispatch issues; say so while the
	# creating session can still implement the task itself.
	_warn_pulse_off_auto_dispatch
```

3. Run `shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`, then the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** read-only `jq` over `repos.json`; a concurrent registry write can at worst yield a skipped warning (`|| return 0`).
- **Migration/rollback:** none; revert or set `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_OFF_CHECK=1`.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older `repos.json` without `initialized_repos` yields `null` → "not registered" only when the slug is absent; `[]?` keeps jq from failing.
- **Idempotency/retry:** stateless, prints once per claim.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** every failure path returns 0 before printing; stdout is untouched (all output via `log_warn` to stderr), preserving the `task_id=`/`ref=` stdout contract.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-stdout-isolation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-auto-dispatch-no-assign.sh
```

Production path, no issue created and no shell redirects (they are blocked in worker shells): with the Write tool, create `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse-off-repos.json` containing `{"initialized_repos":[{"slug":"marcusquinn/aidevops","pulse":false}]}`, then run from the worktree:

```bash
env REPOS_FILE="$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse-off-repos.json" .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh --dry-run --title "pulse-off advisory check" --description "x" --labels auto-dispatch
env REPOS_FILE="$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse-off-repos.json" AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_OFF_CHECK=1 .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh --dry-run --title "pulse-off advisory check" --description "x" --labels auto-dispatch
```

The first output must contain `no worker will pick up this auto-dispatch issue`; the second must not. Both must still print the `task_id=` dry-run line.

- **Surface mapping:** shellcheck → function syntax; stdout-isolation test → stdout contract; dry-run pair → positive warning and opt-out.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Claiming an `auto-dispatch` task in a repo whose local `repos.json` entry has `pulse: false` (or no entry) prints the three-line warning on stderr and still completes the claim.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "_warn_pulse_off_auto_dispatch"
    path: ".agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh"
  ```

- [ ] stdout stays machine-readable: `test-claim-task-id-stdout-isolation.sh` passes, and no warning appears for pulse-on repos, non-`auto-dispatch` labels, `--no-issue`, or `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_OFF_CHECK=1`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-stdout-isolation.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` is clean.

## Context & Decisions

- Warn, never block: `repos.json` is per host, and another runner may pulse the repo.
- Not changed here: whether pulse-off repos should dispatch at all. `pulse: false` / `maintenance: false` is an explicit maintainer setting, and overriding it is a maintainer decision.
- Non-goal: changing the onboarding advisory or the setup-debt toast text.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:1869` — `_warn_dispatch_path_auto_dispatch`, the sibling advisory pattern to follow.
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:1972` — `_main_preclaim_discovery`, the call site.
- `.agents/scripts/repo-onboarding-audit-lib.sh:70-86` — the later, host-wide "Pulse off" advisory this complements.
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh:248` — `REPOS_FILE` default.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

title: t19405: feat(metrics): read-only autonomy outcome report — interactive share, worker waste, lead time, queue health
body:
## Task


A read-only command, `autonomy-report-helper.sh report [--weeks N] [--json]`, that prints, for the maintainer's managed scope:

1. **Weekly, split into framework repo and each other owner:** merged PRs by origin (`origin:worker` / `origin:interactive` / unlabeled), **interactive share** = interactive / (worker + interactive), worker **waste** = closed-unmerged worker PRs / (worker merged + worker closed-unmerged).
2. **Lead time for the latest week:** issue-created → PR-merged and PR-opened → merged, p50/p90 hours, per origin (sample ≤100 PRs per row via `closingIssuesReferences`).
3. **Queue health now:** `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` count; the subset not updated for 7+ days, split by local pulse state (on / off / not registered); `status:blocked` count and the subset not updated for 14+ days; `hold-for-review` PRs; `needs-maintainer-review` items.
4. **Targets line:** each metric beside an initial target (constants at the top of the Python file): interactive share < 15%, waste < 5%, worker issue→merge p90 < 24h, idle-7d available in pulse-on repos = 0, blocked-stale-14d = 0.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `autonomy convergence metrics weekly throughput` → 0 relevant hits — no prior lesson
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs for an autonomy/outcome report (`prework-discovery-helper.sh`); `autonomy-*` matches no tracked file
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — new read-only files modelled on an existing helper pair; reference implementation supplied inline
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — reference script is inline below

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-26
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** The maintainer asked how far aidevops is from running efficiently, reliably and autonomously, and when framework optimisation stops being a large share of the work. No existing command answers that: `pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh` measures local pulse mechanics (spawns, slot occupancy, ceremony seconds), and `aidevops metrics` measures repo code metrics. The answer needed an ad-hoc GitHub search script; this task makes it a reusable command.

## What

A read-only command, `autonomy-report-helper.sh report [--weeks N] [--json]`, that prints, for the maintainer's managed scope:

1. **Weekly, split into framework repo and each other owner:** merged PRs by origin (`origin:worker` / `origin:interactive` / unlabeled), **interactive share** = interactive / (worker + interactive), worker **waste** = closed-unmerged worker PRs / (worker merged + worker closed-unmerged).
2. **Lead time for the latest week:** issue-created → PR-merged and PR-opened → merged, p50/p90 hours, per origin (sample ≤100 PRs per row via `closingIssuesReferences`).
3. **Queue health now:** `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` count; the subset not updated for 7+ days, split by local pulse state (on / off / not registered); `status:blocked` count and the subset not updated for 14+ days; `hold-for-review` PRs; `needs-maintainer-review` items.
4. **Targets line:** each metric beside an initial target (constants at the top of the Python file): interactive share < 15%, waste < 5%, worker issue→merge p90 < 24h, idle-7d available in pulse-on repos = 0, blocked-stale-14d = 0.

## Why

Baseline from the ad-hoc version (2026-11-26; owner names omitted):

- Framework repo, 8 weeks: merged PRs grew from 370 to 715 per week; interactive share stayed at 35–48% (44% last week); worker waste 0–3%.
- Non-framework owners last week: interactive share ranged from 3% (one bulk-pipeline owner, ~4,450 worker merges) to 49% and 80% in the others.
- Lead time last week (hours, p50/p90): framework worker issue→merge 0.9/10.6, interactive 1.1/3.3; product worker 3.1/47.6.
- Queue: 36 available issues idle 7+ days, 35 of them in repos whose pulse is off or not registered; 275 blocked, only 3 not updated for 14+ days.

Raw merged-PR counts mislead (bulk pipelines dominate them). The interactive share, waste, tail lead time and stale queue are the signals that show whether the maintainer is still the bottleneck. A repeatable report lets each week's improvement work be judged against them, and shows when framework work can drop to maintenance.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** read-only new files following a verified two-file pattern; the worker chooses scope derivation details and output formatting.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/autonomy-report-helper.sh` — thin wrapper, model exactly on `.agents/scripts/pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh` (27 lines: `set -euo pipefail`, source `shared-constants.sh`, `main` dispatching `report` / `help` to `python3 -B`).
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/autonomy_report.py` — the report; model argument handling and `--json` on `.agents/scripts/pulse_throughput_report.py` (`argparse`, one JSON object, `null` for unavailable values).
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/observability.md` — add a short `### 6. Autonomy outcomes (GitHub)` subsection after `### 5. Session output-efficiency evidence` (line 343) with the command, the metric definitions in one sentence each, and the targets.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** none yet (manual command); a later routine may call it.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none — GitHub GraphQL `search` reads only; no files written.
- **Existing verification/tests:** none encode this behaviour; verify by running the command (below).
- **Schemas/config:** reads `${REPOS_FILE:-$HOME/.config/aidevops/repos.json}` `initialized_repos[]` (`slug`, `pulse`, `local_only`, `role`, `maintenance`); no schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` by `setup.sh`; nothing generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** delete the two new files and the doc subsection.

### Implementation Steps

1. Scope: from `repos.json`, take entries with `local_only != true`, `role` absent or `"maintainer"`, and a `slug` containing `/`. Group owners. The framework repo (`marcusquinn/aidevops`, overridable with `--framework-repo`) is its own row; every other owner gets a row with qualifier `user:<owner>` or `org:<owner>`. Find out which one GitHub needs by querying `repositoryOwner(login:) { __typename }` once per owner. Exclude the framework repo from its owner's row with `-repo:<framework>`. Never print private paths; owner/repo slugs go to stdout only (local report).
2. Batch searches with GraphQL aliases, `search(type: ISSUE, query: $q, first: 0) { issueCount }`, at most ~40 aliases per request. On any GraphQL error print the error and exit 1; never print a partial table as if complete.
3. Reference implementation of the queries and formulas (ad-hoc version; replace the hard-coded scope with step 1):

```python
METRICS_PER_WEEK = {  # r = "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD"
    "worker":       "{scope} is:pr is:merged label:origin:worker merged:{r}",
    "interactive":  "{scope} is:pr is:merged label:origin:interactive merged:{r}",
    "all":          "{scope} is:pr is:merged merged:{r}",
    "worker_waste": "{scope} is:pr is:closed is:unmerged label:origin:worker closed:{r}",
}
LEAD_Q = """query($q:String!){search(type:ISSUE, query:$q, first:100){nodes{... on PullRequest{
  createdAt mergedAt closingIssuesReferences(first:1){nodes{createdAt}}}}}}"""
QUEUE = {
    "available":        "{scope} is:issue is:open label:auto-dispatch label:status:available",
    "available_idle_7d":"{scope} is:issue is:open label:auto-dispatch label:status:available updated:<{d7}",
    "blocked":          "{scope} is:issue is:open label:status:blocked",
    "blocked_stale_14d":"{scope} is:issue is:open label:status:blocked updated:<{d14}",
    "hold_for_review":  "{scope} is:pr is:open label:hold-for-review",
    "needs_maintainer_review": "{scope} is:open label:needs-maintainer-review",
}
```

4. GitHub search does not support parenthesised `OR` across `label:` qualifiers in this API: query each status label separately and sum, never `(label:a OR label:b)`.
5. Text output: one table per section plus the targets line; `--json`: one object with `window`, `rows`, `lead_times`, `queue`, `targets`, `notes` (note that counts are point-in-time GitHub search totals, and that search totals above 1,000 are exact counts but node samples cap at 100).

### Hazards and Compatibility
