title: t19420: refactor(pulse): remove shared-lock refill workarounds after the split dispat...
body:
## Task


Remove the code that existed only because dispatch and maintenance shared the Pulse instance lock, including the shared-lock refill path itself. After this change every dispatch round takes the dispatch lock and there is no `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT` switch.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

<!-- aidevops:not-before at=2026-11-30T00:00:00Z reason=48h_soak_after_dispatch_lock_default -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `dispatch lock split canary duplicate dispatch claim loss t19322` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs touch the target files; the latest relevant commits are t19364 (`a9a3fbf360`) and t19350 (`d7bb8595a9`), both merged
- [x] File refs verified: 14 refs checked at `6efb3484e5`, all present
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — removing guards from the self-hosting dispatch path (`pulse-wrapper.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) needs a judgement, item by item, about which guards are only shared-lock workarounds
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — depends on the soak result

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-27
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer session)
- **Parent task:** t19322 / GH#40108 (Phase 3)
- **Blocked by:** blocked-by: t19418 (GH#40535, dispatch-lock default) and blocked-by: t19419 (GH#40536, supervisor lane), plus the `not-before` gate above for the 48 h soak
- **Conversation context:** The maintainer approved filing Phase 3 now, gated so it starts only after the split dispatch lock has been the default for 48 h and the supervisor lane has landed.

## What

Remove the code that existed only because dispatch and maintenance shared the Pulse instance lock, including the shared-lock refill path itself. After this change every dispatch round takes the dispatch lock and there is no `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT` switch.

## Why

GH#40108 measured that the shared lock caused 76% of worker-exit refills to end `lock_busy`. Seven layers were added around it (GH#35349, GH#36603, GH#38162, GH#38210, GH#38696, t19015, t19064 and others). With the split lock as the default, those layers are dead or redundant, and every future Pulse change still has to reason about both modes.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** each removal must be checked against the soak evidence and the remaining split-mode callers. Some guards (cycle-final drain, cycle-entry wake) may still carry split-mode duties after t19350.

## PR Conventions

Final phase of GH#40108: the PR may close the parent only if the parent's remaining acceptance is met. Otherwise use a closing keyword for this issue and `For #40108` for the parent.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:393-447` — `_pulse_event_refill_split_lock`, `_pulse_event_refill_try_lock`, `_pulse_event_refill_release_lock`, `_pulse_event_refill_wait_for_instance_lock`: keep only the dispatch-lock branch and rename the wait helper.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:523-592` — the GH#35349 admission budget (`_pulse_event_refill_apply_budget`, `_pulse_event_refill_budget_spent`, `_PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_ADMIT_DEADLINE`): unused in split mode (line 881 skips it). Delete it and the `drain_budget_exhausted` branches at lines 766-773 and 794-797.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:637-697,840-849,884-888` — the failed-drain cooldown (`_pulse_event_refill_cooldown_file`, `_record_cooldown`, `_clear_cooldown`, `_cooldown_remaining`, and the `split_lock=0` branches): already skipped in split mode. Delete it.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:699-714` — `_pulse_event_refill_run_routines_if_busy`: keep only if a refill-only run still needs to run routines while a cycle holds the instance lock. Decide from logs.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1746-1762` — `_pulse_drain_cycle_final_refill`: decide whether the cycle-final drain is still needed now that worker-exit refills dispatch at any time.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1438-1530` — `_pulse_cycle_entry_gates` cycle-entry drain call (line 1522) and `_pulse_event_refill_cycle_entry` (`pulse-event-refill.sh:716-736`): keep the t19350 wake if the soak data shows it still fills slots during preflight.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1183-1280` — `maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse` (line 1202, GH#38696 supervisor-phase active refill), its `active_refill` gate and the t19324 comment at line 1268. After GH#40536 lands, the cycle tail no longer hosts a long supervisor, so this wake may be dead.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:975,1049-1050` — the `last_active_refill_epoch` caller of that function.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1672-1673` — t19324 split comment on the post-release fill.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh:423-510` — remove `pulse_dispatch_lock_split_enabled`, the mode file and `pulse_dispatch_lock_publish_mode`. Remove the call at `pulse-wrapper.sh:1068`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh` — delete cases for removed behaviour (shared-lock refill, cooldown, admission budget). Keep the split-mode cases.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** find with `rg -n "_pulse_event_refill_split_lock|pulse_dispatch_lock_split_enabled|_pulse_event_refill_apply_budget|_pulse_event_refill_budget_spent|_cooldown_remaining|_record_cooldown|maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse|cycle_final_refill|dispatch-mode" .agents/scripts`. Also `pulse_throughput_events.py` parses `[pulse-event-refill]` actions (`lock_busy`, `failed_drain_cooldown`, `drain_budget_exhausted`). Removed actions simply stop appearing, so the report needs no change.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `${trigger_file}.failed-cooldown` and `${LOCKDIR}.dispatch-mode` files. After removal nothing writes them; leftover files must be harmless.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-event-refill.sh`, `test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` (the active-refill case near line 931), `test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh` (routines-while-busy), plus the lock tests named in GH#40535.
- **Schemas/config:** env knobs to remove: `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT`, `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_MAX_SECONDS`, `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_FAILED_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`, plus any active-refill knobs read by `maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse`. Search `.agents/` docs with `rg -n` for each.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh` only.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Stale marker files are ignored.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. There is no runtime switch after this change, which is why the soak gate exists.

### Implementation Steps

1. Precondition: confirm the dispatch-lock default has been deployed for at least 48 h. Compare the GH#40535 merge time with `rg -n "activated bundle" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`. Run `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh report --since <merge+1h> --until <now> --json` and record `slot_occupancy`, `slot_occupancy_census`, `ceremony_concurrency.idle_share` and the refill outcomes in a comment here. If the window is shorter than 48 h, record that and stop.
2. For each item in Files to Modify, show from the soak logs whether the path ran (for example `rg -c "action=drain_budget_exhausted|failed_drain_cooldown" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` should be 0 since the default). Remove paths that did not run. Keep any that did, and explain why in the PR.
3. Remove the code and tests, run the verification, and commit WIP.
4. After deploy, rerun the Phase 0 report over 6 h and post it on GH#40108.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** every dispatch round must still take the dispatch lock. Removing the shared-lock branch must not leave a path that dispatches with no lock at all.
- **Migration/rollback:** no runtime opt-out remains after this PR. Rollback is a revert plus deploy.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** during a deploy drain an old bundle may still run shared-lock refills. Those take the instance lock, which new cycles still respect, so mixing versions is safe for one drain.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged. The trigger file still coalesces exits.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a refill that dies still leaves the trigger. Stale dispatch-lock owners are still reclaimed by the dead-PID and heartbeat checks in `pulse-instance-lock.sh`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-singleton-lock.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lock-force-reclaim.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** shellcheck covers every edited script. The event-refill test covers the remaining refill path. Min-concurrency covers the active-refill wake. First-wave and max-parallel cover cycle dispatch rounds. Merge-routine-standalone covers the routines-while-busy pass. The lock tests cover the instance and dispatch lock invariants.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the Pulse dispatch tests above.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: remove shared-lock refill workarounds`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Positive: the PR has a net negative line count in `.agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh`, and every listed test passes.
- [ ] Negative: no Pulse occupancy regression. Over 6 h after deploy, `slot_occupancy_census.mean` and the ceremony idle share are no worse than the 48 h soak values recorded in step 1, in a window where rounds start with at least 20 candidates.
- [ ] Negative: the shared-lock refill path is gone.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT"
    path: ".agents/scripts"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] No issue has two live local workers in the 6 h after deploy. Check: same-issue spawns without an exit between, using the method in the GH#40108 2026-11-27 comment.

## Context & Decisions

- Phase 3 was planned to be filed after 48 h as the default. The maintainer chose to file it now with a time gate and dependency edges instead, so it is not forgotten.
- Not chosen: keeping the opt-out permanently. Two lock modes double the reasoning cost for every Pulse change.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:393-892` — refill lock choice, budget, cooldown, drain and the refill-only entry.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1438-1530,1746-1762` — cycle-entry and cycle-final drains.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1202` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:1049` — supervisor-phase active refill (GH#38696) and its caller.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh:423-510` — split flag and mode file.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** GH#40535 (t19418) and GH#40536 (t19419); `not-before` 2026-11-30T00:00Z.
- **Blocks:** closing GH#40108.

</details>

body:
## Task


A candidate that was refused for a durable ownership reason (`dedup_active_claim_durable_launch`, `dedup_pr_evidence`, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`) is skipped by the existing cross-cycle negative cache in later rounds, until something that could change the decision changes. Today the same issues are re-evaluated through the full dedup ceremony round after round.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `dispatch lock split canary duplicate dispatch claim loss t19322` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs touch `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` or `pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`
- [x] File refs verified: 7 refs checked at `6efb3484e5`, all present
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — the work is diagnosing why an existing cross-cycle cache almost never hits, then changing ownership-gate caching on the self-hosting dispatch path without weakening any gate
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the root cause is not yet known

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-27
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer session)
- **Related:** GH#40108 (Pulse dispatch throughput). Filed separately, not as a phase: it reduces the cost of rejecting candidates rather than changing lock or supervisor structure.
- **Conversation context:** With the split dispatch lock, the remaining throughput cost is candidates that are fully evaluated and then refused. The maintainer approved a separate task to reject them earlier, without bypassing any safety gate.

## What

A candidate that was refused for a durable ownership reason (`dedup_active_claim_durable_launch`, `dedup_pr_evidence`, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`) is skipped by the existing cross-cycle negative cache in later rounds, until something that could change the decision changes. Today the same issues are re-evaluated through the full dedup ceremony round after round.

## Why

Evidence from one macOS runner (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` from 2026-11-24T05:02Z, `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` from 2026-11-26T18:00Z to 2026-11-27T01:30Z):

| Refusal reason | Refusals | Distinct issues | Most for one issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch` | 639 | 436 | 15 |
| `dedup_pr_evidence` | 522 | 300 | 26 |
| `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` | 146 | 68 | 20 |

- The negative cache is recorded for all three reasons (`_dispatch_negative_cache_record`, `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:511-575`), yet `cross-cycle ownership block` appears only 15 times in the same log (`_dispatch_prefilter_owned_candidate`, `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:780-799`).
- `negative_cache_record_skipped reason=boundary detail=assigned` appears 120 times. That path (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:533-540`) declines to record draft-checkpoint hints for assigned issues.
- In the 7.5 h stage window: 1,513 candidate evaluations, 155 worker launches. 422 evaluations reached `dedup.dedup_check` and were then refused, costing 10,611 s of cumulative stage time (median 18.4 s, p90 45.5 s each).

Each refused evaluation also spends GitHub API calls and holds the dispatch lock while slots are free.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** the cause of the cache misses is unknown. Likely candidates: the reader invalidates on issue `updatedAt` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:773-775`), which claim comments and label edits bump; the TTL; or the owner gate at `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:527-532`. Any fix touches ownership decisions on the dispatch path.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue and `Ref #40108`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:480-800` — negative-cache record, reader, revision refresh and the owned-candidate prefilter.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:480-560` — dedup gate order, only if the diagnosis shows a cheap local gate runs after an expensive remote one.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh` — only where a refusal site does not call `_dispatch_negative_cache_record` (find with `rg -n "DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=(dedup_active_claim_durable_launch|dedup_pr_evidence|worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked)" .agents/scripts`).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` or `test-pulse-dispatch-negative-cache-material.sh` — extend the existing cases for the changed invalidation rule.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` is read at `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:783,1792` and `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:1314`. Find writers with `rg -n "_dispatch_negative_cache_record " .agents/scripts`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** files under `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-negative-cache/<owner>--<repo>--<issue>` and their `.skip` markers.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-negative-cache-material.sh`, `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` (negative-cache cases near line 1839).
- **Schemas/config:** record format is a 9-field TSV line written at `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:563`. A format change must keep old records readable or make them miss safely.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh` only.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Old records expire by TTL.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. Wrong cache hits only delay dispatch, and records expire.

### Implementation Steps

1. Diagnose before changing anything. For a sample of issues refused more than 5 times for one reason, log why the cache did not hit: no record written, record expired, or revision mismatch with a failed refresh. Use the existing log lines plus a temporary local probe, not new production logging, unless the cause stays hidden.
2. Fix the cause. Acceptable directions: key invalidation on material that can change the decision (assignees, status labels, linked PR head, claim owner liveness) rather than on raw `updatedAt`; record the assigned draft-checkpoint case with the owner as the boundary; move a cheap local refusal ahead of the remote reads.
3. Keep every gate. A cache hit must only skip a candidate the full ceremony would also refuse. Never skip the claim, footprint-overlap or final-ownership checks for a candidate that proceeds to launch.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** records are written by parallel dispatch children; keep the temp-file plus `mv` write.
- **Migration/rollback:** records in the old format must miss, never hit wrongly.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an old bundle reading a new-format record must treat it as a miss.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a stale hit delays a dispatchable issue by at most one TTL. State that bound in the PR.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a failed write leaves the current behaviour (full evaluation).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-negative-cache-material.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** shellcheck covers edited scripts. The failure-reasons and cache-material tests cover record and read rules. Stale-PR continuation covers the draft-checkpoint reasons. Max-parallel covers the cache inside a dispatch round.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: negative cache hit rate`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-negative-cache-material.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The diagnosis is posted on this issue: for each of the three reasons, which of "not written", "expired" or "revision mismatch" explains the misses, with counts.
- [ ] Positive: over 6 h after deploy, `rg -c "cross-cycle ownership block" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (new lines only) is at least half of the repeated refusals for the three reasons in the same window.
- [ ] Negative: no rise in `CLAIM_LOST`, no issue with two live local workers, and no issue held past its blocker clearing for longer than the stated TTL bound.
- [ ] Every listed test passes.

## Context & Decisions

- Not chosen: removing or reordering safety gates (claim consensus, footprint overlap, final ownership fence). The aim is to stop repeating a refusal already proven, not to admit more candidates.
- Repository names in the evidence are omitted; reproduce with the commands above on any runner.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:511-575` — negative-cache record.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:760-799` — reader revision check and owned-candidate prefilter.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:503-519` — footprint overlap gate (must stay).

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none.
- **Blocks:** none.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #32557 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #32557

**Parent issue:** #32557 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #32557 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#32557 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 32557 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Tier (t19356):** copy the parent's `tier:*` label only when a maintainer set it. If the parent's tier was raised by a `Cascade Tier Escalation` comment, use the tier from before that escalation. Escalation is evidence about the parent's failed run, not about the consolidated spec, so the successor must earn `tier:thinking` through its own repeated failures.

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #32557, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 32557 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 32557 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 32557 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 32557 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/32557" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #32557 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #32557.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

title: agent-sources: registry lost after update; sync suffixes same-source command symlinks instead of repointing
body:
## Observed

`agent-sources-helper.sh sync` reported "No agent sources configured" although a private agent source had been registered and deployed earlier. Its `custom/<source>/` folder and two OpenCode command symlinks still existed, and they pointed at an older runtime bundle (3.39.285; current 3.39.288). After `agent-sources-helper.sh add <repo>`, `sync` saw those symlinks as collisions. It deployed `/<command>-<source>` duplicates instead of replacing the stale links that the same source owned.

## Expected

- The source registry survives `aidevops update` (or is rebuilt from existing `custom/<source>/` deployments).
- `sync` recognises command symlinks that point into `agents/custom/<same source>/` in any runtime bundle as its own, and repoints them rather than adding a suffix.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/agent-sources-helper.sh`: the `sync` collision check and registry storage.
- The update/setup path that rewrites runtime bundles. Path unknown: search `setup.sh` and `runtime-bundles` handling.

## Verification

Register a source and sync, then run `aidevops update` and `sync` again. Expect no "No agent sources configured" message and no `-<source>` suffixed commands. Then delete the registry entry, re-add it and sync. Expect existing same-source symlinks to be repointed, not duplicated.

## Workaround used

Moved the suffixed symlinks over the stale originals in `~/.config/opencode/command/`, then re-synced. The second sync was clean.

body:
_Supersedes #32557 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

<!-- aidevops:generator=large-file-simplification-gate cited_file=.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh threshold=2000 -->

## What

Simplify `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` — currently over 2000 lines (2481 lines on `main` at consolidation time). Break it into smaller, focused modules so the original path is a thin orchestrator below 2000 lines, without changing dispatch behaviour.

## Why

Issue #32532 is blocked by the large-file gate. Workers dispatched against this file spend most of their context budget reading it, leaving insufficient capacity for implementation.

The file was already split once: per @vladimirdulov's completion summary on #32557, PR #32574 split the original 2796-line library into three focused files (round coordinator and state kept in `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`; helper groups moved to `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` and `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`). Later dispatch features (for example t19330, t19324, t19301, t19300, GH#39765) grew the orchestrator back above the threshold, so #32557 was reopened. This is a second split pass, not a re-do of PR #32574.

Current line counts on `main` (measured with `wc -l` at consolidation time — re-measure before editing):

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: 2481
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`: 1931
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`: 2039 (also over the 2000-line threshold)

Because both existing sibling modules are already near or over the threshold, code moved out of the orchestrator must not be added to them; extract into a new named module instead.

## How

- Extract cohesive function groups into separate files.
- Keep a thin orchestrator in the original file that sources the extracted modules.
- Verify: `wc -l .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` should be below 2000.

Suggested extraction (verify the line ranges against the current file first):

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:140-887` — the dispatch negative-cache and verified-block group (`_dispatch_negative_cache_path` through `_dispatch_record_and_cache_block`, including `_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint`, `_dispatch_checkpoint_pr_head`, `_dispatch_checkpoint_decimal`, `_dispatch_draft_hint_boundary`, `_dispatch_negative_cache_ops_only`, `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` and `_dispatch_cache_confirmed_block`). Move it to the new `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-negative-cache.sh`. That is about 750 lines, which takes the orchestrator to about 1730.

title: t19422: fix(audit-log): stale-lock reclaim acts on a newer holder's lock, wedging or overlapping concurrent writers
body:
## Task


`audit-log-helper.sh`'s mkdir lock loses mutual exclusion or wedges under concurrent writers. `test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` is red (rc `1,1`) in Shell Suite Main Health, and the failure reproduces locally on macOS.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`audit-log-helper.sh`'s mkdir lock loses mutual exclusion or wedges under concurrent writers. `test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` is red (rc `1,1`) in Shell Suite Main Health, and the failure reproduces locally on macOS.

## Evidence

**Hosted runner** ([run 45924328273](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/45924328273), `suite-health` artifact, branch `bugfix/gh40029-residual-suite-health` merged with current `main`). In the 40-writer block, two writers held the lock together:

```
[AUDIT ERROR] Refusing to release audit log lock owned by another process
FAIL: parallel writer process 2479044 failed unexpectedly
PASS: all concurrent writers appended exactly once
FAIL: concurrent sequence numbers are duplicated or non-monotonic
[AUDIT ERROR] Entry 26: Chain broken — prev_hash mismatch
```

The same mode recurs in the rotation block (entry 10). The suite passed in runs 45823247563 and 45918823438, so it is intermittent.

**Local** (macOS): 6 rounds × 4 parallel `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` gave 1/24 failures in a second mode, a wedged lock:

```
[AUDIT ERROR] Could not remove audit log lock directory: .../audit.jsonl.lock.d
[AUDIT ERROR] Could not acquire audit log lock after 30s   (x many)
FAIL: expected 40 concurrent entries, found 3
```

## Confirmed mechanism (local mode)

See `.agents/scripts/audit-log-helper.sh`, `_audit_reclaim_stale_lock` and `_audit_remove_lock_dir`.

1. Writer B fails `mkdir lock.d` and reads holder Z's owner record.
2. Z releases normally and exits. A new holder A creates `lock.d`.
3. B runs `kill -0 Z`, which fails, so B judges the lock stale. B then creates `lock.d/.reclaim` inside **A's** live lock. Its re-verify (from #40427) later aborts correctly.
4. A's release runs `rm owner` → `rmdir .reclaim` (before B's mkdir) → `rmdir lock.d`, which fails because B's `.reclaim` exists. A reports "Could not remove" and fails.
5. B's re-verify sees no owner (≠ Z) and removes `.reclaim`. That leaves an empty, ownerless, fresh `lock.d`. Every writer then waits out `AUDIT_LOCK_ORPHAN_AGE_SECONDS` (default 60s) and times out.

So the stale judgement is made against a *previous* holder's identity but acts (`mkdir .reclaim`) on whatever lock now exists at that path. The release path also is not robust to a concurrent election directory.

**Hosted-runner overlap mode:** not yet explained. Someone deleted a live holder's `owner` file, and two writers appended concurrently. Candidates to check: the TOCTOU between the reclaimer's re-verify and `_audit_remove_lock_dir`'s `rm -f owner`, and the A/B interleaving above when A's `rmdir .reclaim` runs *after* B's mkdir.

## How (suggested)

- Make reclaim act only on the lock instance it judged. For example, bind the decision to the lock directory's identity (`dev:ino` plus owner record) and re-check both after electing. Or reclaim by atomically renaming `lock.d` to a unique tombstone after verification, then deleting the tombstone, so no step mutates a lock a new holder created.
- Make holder release tolerate a concurrent `.reclaim`: remove its owner, then rename its own lock dir away atomically instead of `rmdir`.
- Keep Bash 3.2 compatibility and the existing dead-owner and ownerless reclaim behaviour the suite asserts.
- Functions to change: `_audit_reclaim_stale_lock`, `_audit_remove_lock_dir`, `_audit_release_current_lock`, `_audit_acquire_lock`. The existing suite provides the coverage, so no new test infrastructure is needed.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/audit-log-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-audit-log-concurrency.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Concurrent writers never overlap: no duplicate or non-monotonic sequence numbers, and `verify` reports an intact hash chain under parallel load.
- [ ] No reclaim mutates a lock created after the stale judgement, so no writer sees "Could not remove audit log lock directory" followed by acquisition timeouts.
- [ ] Regression guard: dead-owner and ownerless-orphan reclaim still succeed, as `test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` already asserts.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/audit-log-helper.sh`
- 24+ parallel runs locally with zero failures: `for i in $(seq 1 6); do for j in 1 2 3 4; do bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-audit-log-concurrency.sh >/dev/null 2>"$TMPDIR/a-$i-$j.err" & done; wait; done`, then `rg -l FAIL "$TMPDIR" -g 'a-*.err'` prints nothing
- `gh workflow run shell-suite-main-health.yml --ref <branch>`: `test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` passes

Found while closing #40529 (Ref #40029).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #40538 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #40538

**Parent issue:** #40538 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t19421: perf(pulse): make the cross-cycle negative cache hit so repeatedly refused ca...
**Parent labels:** `enhancement,status:available,auto-dispatch,pulse,tier:thinking,origin:interactive,framework,consolidation-in-progress,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #40538 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#40538 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 40538 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Tier (t19356):** copy the parent's `tier:*` label only when a maintainer set it. If the parent's tier was raised by a `Cascade Tier Escalation` comment, use the tier from before that escalation. Escalation is evidence about the parent's failed run, not about the consolidated spec, so the successor must earn `tier:thinking` through its own repeated failures.

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #40538, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 40538 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 40538 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 40538 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 40538 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/40538" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #40538 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #40538.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Task


A candidate that was refused for a durable ownership reason (`dedup_active_claim_durable_launch`, `dedup_pr_evidence`, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`) is skipped by the existing cross-cycle negative cache in later rounds, until something that could change the decision changes. Today the same issues are re-evaluated through the full dedup ceremony round after round.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `dispatch lock split canary duplicate dispatch claim loss t19322` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs touch `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` or `pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`
- [x] File refs verified: 7 refs checked at `6efb3484e5`, all present
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — the work is diagnosing why an existing cross-cycle cache almost never hits, then changing ownership-gate caching on the self-hosting dispatch path without weakening any gate
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the root cause is not yet known

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-27
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer session)
- **Related:** GH#40108 (Pulse dispatch throughput). Filed separately, not as a phase: it reduces the cost of rejecting candidates rather than changing lock or supervisor structure.
- **Conversation context:** With the split dispatch lock, the remaining throughput cost is candidates that are fully evaluated and then refused. The maintainer approved a separate task to reject them earlier, without bypassing any safety gate.

## What

A candidate that was refused for a durable ownership reason (`dedup_active_claim_durable_launch`, `dedup_pr_evidence`, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`) is skipped by the existing cross-cycle negative cache in later rounds, until something that could change the decision changes. Today the same issues are re-evaluated through the full dedup ceremony round after round.

## Why

Evidence from one macOS runner (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` from 2026-11-24T05:02Z, `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` from 2026-11-26T18:00Z to 2026-11-27T01:30Z):

| Refusal reason | Refusals | Distinct issues | Most for one issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch` | 639 | 436 | 15 |
| `dedup_pr_evidence` | 522 | 300 | 26 |
| `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` | 146 | 68 | 20 |

- The negative cache is recorded for all three reasons (`_dispatch_negative_cache_record`, `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:511-575`), yet `cross-cycle ownership block` appears only 15 times in the same log (`_dispatch_prefilter_owned_candidate`, `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:780-799`).
- `negative_cache_record_skipped reason=boundary detail=assigned` appears 120 times. That path (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:533-540`) declines to record draft-checkpoint hints for assigned issues.
- In the 7.5 h stage window: 1,513 candidate evaluations, 155 worker launches. 422 evaluations reached `dedup.dedup_check` and were then refused, costing 10,611 s of cumulative stage time (median 18.4 s, p90 45.5 s each).

Each refused evaluation also spends GitHub API calls and holds the dispatch lock while slots are free.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** the cause of the cache misses is unknown. Likely candidates: the reader invalidates on issue `updatedAt` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:773-775`), which claim comments and label edits bump; the TTL; or the owner gate at `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:527-532`. Any fix touches ownership decisions on the dispatch path.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue and `Ref #40108`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:480-800` — negative-cache record, reader, revision refresh and the owned-candidate prefilter.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:480-560` — dedup gate order, only if the diagnosis shows a cheap local gate runs after an expensive remote one.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh` — only where a refusal site does not call `_dispatch_negative_cache_record` (find with `rg -n "DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=(dedup_active_claim_durable_launch|dedup_pr_evidence|worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked)" .agents/scripts`).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` or `test-pulse-dispatch-negative-cache-material.sh` — extend the existing cases for the changed invalidation rule.

### Complete Write Surface

title: planning-commit-helper: silent publication failure when local HEAD is behind earlier direct planning publications
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh "<message>"` fails with no diagnostic when the caller's checkout HEAD is behind the remote default branch, the remote has already changed `TODO.md`, and the caller's working copy adds lines next to one of those remote changes. The 3-way merge in `planning-publisher.sh` conflicts and returns 1. All the user sees is:

```
[plan] Planning file publication failed; see the publication output above for remote, PR and worktree state
```

There is no "publication output above" to look at.

## Observed (2026-11-27, aidevops v3.39.285, OpenCode 1.19.6)

1. A linked worktree on a planning chore branch had HEAD = merge commit X.
2. Two direct planning publications landed on main after X (a t59/t60 completion tick, then a TODO backfill). Both came from this worktree through the helper, which does not move local HEAD.
3. `claim-task-id.sh` appended two new task lines right after the ticked t60 line.
4. `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: add ..."` then failed twice with only the line above. Base = X's TODO.md, ours = the working copy (t60 tick + new lines), theirs = main (t60 tick). The hunks overlap and differ, so `git merge-file` conflicts.
5. Workaround: `git reset -q origin/main` (mixed, so the working tree is kept) in the linked worktree, then rerun. That published cleanly.

## Expected

- On a merge conflict, print the conflicting path and the cause, and suggest the fix: "local HEAD is N planning commits behind origin/<default>; fast-forward or mixed-reset to origin/<default> and retry".
- Better: when HEAD is an ancestor of the remote default branch and the only differences between them are planning files, use the remote tip's blob as the merge base for those files. The caller's own earlier publications from this checkout are then not re-merged against a stale base.

## Where

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`: `_planning_publish_resolve*`/merge-file paths around lines 410-430 and 535-560 (the `merge_rc` checks return 1 silently).
- `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` around line 666 (the generic error message).

## Verification

Reproduce in a scratch repo: publish a TODO change via the helper from a linked worktree without moving HEAD, then add a line adjacent to the published change and publish again. Expect either a clean publish or an actionable error naming the stale base.

title: process-guard never reaps pre-#40209 deadlocked bounded-operation supervisors (orphaned, past budget, bundle deleted), pinning worktrees
body:
## What

`process-guard-helper.sh` exempts every `bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` process from runtime limits as `MANAGED` ("runtime delegated to bounded-operation-supervisor lifecycle controls"). Supervisors that hit the GH#40205 Node 26 `process.exit()` deadlock before the #40209 fix stay alive forever: parent PID 1, no children, past the 86400 s maximum budget, running from a runtime-bundle directory that has since been deleted. Their lifecycle controls no longer exist, so nothing reaps them.

Impact: the worktree lifecycle registry correctly refuses to retire any worktree a live process uses as its working directory (`retirement-refused ... detail=live-process-reference`). One such orphan blocked removal of a merged worktree for more than 24 h; `worktree-helper.sh clean` reported only "removal guard refused path".

## Evidence (2026-11-27)

- Three orphans from a 3.39.277 bundle built before #40209 merged: elapsed 2 d 4 h, 1 d 20 h and 1 d 0 h; parent PID 1; `pgrep -P` empty; bundle directory missing. The working directories were a merged project worktree, a framework bugfix worktree and the canonical framework checkout.
- SIGTERM had no effect, matching the #40205 symptom. SIGKILL worked, and `worktree-helper.sh remove <path>` then retired the worktree.
- Current-bundle supervisors (3.39.288) all have live parents.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/process-guard-helper.sh` `_runtime_management_owner` / runtime classification (around lines 487-544): return `MANAGED` for a bounded-operation supervisor only when it still has a live owner. Treat it as a reapable orphan when all of these hold: PPID 1, no child processes, age greater than the 86400 s budget ceiling plus kill grace, and either the script path no longer exists or the bundle version is older than the deployed one. Send SIGKILL directly, because SIGTERM cannot run its handler in the deadlock state; log the reap.
- Optionally, make the `worktree-helper.sh clean` skip message name the blocking PID and command, not just "removal guard refused path".

## Acceptance

- An orphaned, childless supervisor that is past the budget ceiling and whose bundle is missing gets reaped by the process-guard pass. Supervisors with a live parent, or within budget, are never touched.
- Covered by a case in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-process-guard-managed-workers.sh` (existing harness), using a fake supervisor command line.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-process-guard-managed-workers.sh`; ShellCheck clean on `process-guard-helper.sh`.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

## Task


Explain and fix the intermittent `test_decision_policy_races` failure in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh` (sourced by `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`). It occurs only on the hosted GitHub runner in `Shell Suite Main Health`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Explain and fix the intermittent `test_decision_policy_races` failure in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh` (sourced by `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`). It occurs only on the hosted GitHub runner in `Shell Suite Main Health`.

## Why

The concurrent-decision case starts two `_pcc_resolve_decision` calls on one fixture root (`decision-concurrent`). It expects one inference and two writes. On the runner it sometimes reports:

```
FAIL concurrent decision: rc=0,0 inferences=2 writes=4 [edit,edit,comment,comment,] refs=[refs_aidevops_checkpoint-decisions_123_findings_42-<head>-21,refs_aidevops_checkpoint-decisions_123_slots_1,]
```

Both callers passed `_pcc_decision_reserve` (`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh`, around line 171) and each ran inference, edit and publish. Yet only one findings ref and only `slots_1` exist. The fixture's fake `gh` creates refs with an atomic `mkdir`, so in principle a second reservation cannot succeed.

History: red (`1,1`) on runs 45924328273 and 45930194935. Flaky (`1,0`) on 45937493624. Pass on 45943811093. It never reproduced in `ubuntu:24.04` Docker, which covered:

- 18 isolated stress iterations and 18 full-suite runs under CPU load
- 8 runs with `~/.aidevops/agents` staged like the workflow
- 8 runs through `Popen(start_new_session=True)`, as `affected-tests-helper.sh` launches suites

The double inference could also come from the production reservation logic. That makes it worth explaining, not only silencing.

Dispatch note: this task waits for evidence, not for a decision. No current artifact contains the trace; the latest branch run passed. Add `auto-dispatch` once a health artifact shows `FAIL trace gh-ref:` lines.

## How

1. Read the next `Shell Suite Main Health` artifact in which this suite is not `pass`. PR #40533 makes `affected-tests-helper.sh` append rerun output, so the first attempt's FAIL lines survive. The test also prints `FAIL trace gh-ref:` lines: per-process `BASHPID`, `EPOCHREALTIME`, `root`, ref operation and rc for every fake ref call.
2. From the trace, decide between these mechanisms:
   - two successful `POST` findings creations, meaning the ref directory was removed or recreated between the calls

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` classified a version-bump PR (one JSON version field, TODO.md, a brief) as **Critical** runtime risk and refused PR body generation ("Critical runtime risk requires runtime-verified evidence"), only because the `--summary` text said "this session's t64 (#124) ...". - Reproduction: any commit-and-pr whose summary includes "session's" or "this session" with a non-runtime diff (e.g. a manifest version bump).

## How

- Keep the other critical categories (payments, auth, credentials, crypto, data deletion) unchanged.

- A commit-and-pr dry run whose summary says "this session's PRs" on a JSON-only diff classifies as low/medium risk; a diff touching session-management code still classifies as critical.

title: Worker sandbox: pass the host's npm global config and rootless Docker socket
body:
## Problem

On a NixOS host, npm's prefix for the system Node comes from `/etc/npmrc`
(`prefix = ${HOME}/.npm-global`). The Nix store is read-only, and this is NixOS's own
`programs.npm` module. npm finds that file only through `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG=/etc/npmrc`,
which login shells export from `/etc/profile`. The prefix cannot go into `~/.npmrc` instead:
nvm refuses a `prefix` there
([nvm.sh v0.41.0 L4354](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm/blob/v0.41.0/nvm.sh#L4354)), so
`nvm use` and `nvm install` exit 11, and `AIDEVOPS_NODE_INSTALL=nvm` then fails.

The worker sandbox drops that variable:

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:1307` starts from `env -i`, and `:54` keeps only
  `PATH HOME USER LANG TERM SHELL`.
- `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:897`) adds only the
  names and prefixes listed at `:958` and `:961`; everything else hits `*) continue` (`:962`).
- The plugin's `shell.env` hook (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/shell-env.mjs:216`, `:266`)
  copies only `WORKER_LINEAGE_ENV_VARS` and `OTEL_ENV_VARS`.

All line numbers are at commit `b40d678753d7dfe6d80196514875f6bb8d778a2b`.

Observed on the host (aidevops 3.39.289, a user without `~/.npmrc`):

```
$ npm config get prefix                                   # login shell
$HOME/.npm-global   (expanded)
$ sandbox-exec-helper.sh run npm config get prefix        # sandbox
/nix/store/<hash>-nodejs-slim-26.13.1
```

So inside a worker, `npm install -g`, `npm root -g` and `npm link` with the system Node point
at the read-only store. Interactive sessions are not affected, because they inherit the login
shell's environment.

`DOCKER_HOST` has the same problem. With rootless Docker it is
`unix:///run/user/<uid>/docker.sock`, and it is exported the same way. Without it, `docker` in a
worker connects to `/var/run/docker.sock`, where no daemon listens.

## Change requested

For the worker role only (the triage and model-replay roles and private workloads keep their
reviewed allowlists), pass through these exact names when they are set:

- `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG`
- `DOCKER_HOST`

Name them explicitly. Do not use an `NPM_CONFIG_*` wildcard: npm also reads credentials from
such variables (for example `NPM_CONFIG__AUTH`). Do not pass
`NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` either: nvm rejects that variable when it points outside `NVM_DIR`.

Both values are paths, not secrets. They are configuration the host owner sets on purpose.

### Where to change

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`: add an explicit
  `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG | DOCKER_HOST) ;;` case next to the `UV_TOOL_DIR | …` case (`:961`),
  with a short comment referencing this issue. The triage/model-replay branch and the private
  workload branch return earlier, so they stay unchanged.
- Test pattern: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-passthrough-otel.sh`, and the existing
  `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`

## Acceptance

1. The existing tests for `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` cover the new behaviour:
   - with `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG` and `DOCKER_HOST` set, the worker role includes both names;
   - the triage and model-replay roles and private workloads include neither;
   - `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` and `NPM_CONFIG__AUTH` are never included.
2. On a host where `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG` is set, a worker's `npm config get prefix` returns
   the prefix from that file, not the Node install directory.
3. nvm keeps working inside the worker: `nvm_die_on_prefix` checks the `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX`
   variable and the npmrc files (builtin, `${NVM_VERSION_DIR}/etc/npmrc`, `~/.npmrc`, project),
   not `NPM_CONFIG_GLOBALCONFIG`.

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-passthrough-otel.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh
```
