title: t19424: fix(worker-lifecycle): half-removed worktrees are retained forever instead of resumed, leaking disk to quota
body:
<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Problem

Two distinct half-states survive every cleanup pass indefinitely and leak disk
until the host hits its quota. Observed on a Linux pulse host (aidevops
v3.39.288, home soft quota 200G): the managed worktree base accumulated 5.2G of
mode-A residue over 15 days and 11.1G of mode-B residue in a single day.

### Mode A: content present, `.git` absent, unregistered

Ten directories held a complete tracked source tree (~390-520M each, `todo/`
plus `packages/` plus `apps/`, `node_modules` already deleted) with no `.git`
file. `git -C <dir> rev-parse --git-dir` returned `fatal: not a git repository`
and `git worktree list` did not mention them. Directory mtimes spanned
2026-11-12 to 2026-11-23.

Those exact paths appear ~388 times in `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log`,
emitted every 10-minute cycle as:

    {"errno":2,"ownership":"managed-by-current-cleanup",
     "path":"<worktree-base>/<repo>-feature-auto-<timestamp>-gh<issue>",
     "reason":"FileNotFoundError","status":"retained"}

Cleanup therefore saw each directory hundreds of times, claimed ownership of it,
and re-decided to keep it on every pass.

### Mode B: relocated into retire staging, never deleted

Three `.lifecycle-retire-<id>/tree` directories (11.1G total; ids `elwmao3l`,
`kf0zg0f2`, `spbyodoa`; created 2026-11-26 at 03:47, 06:17 and 11:42) were
intact worktrees: `.git` present, `node_modules` present, still listed by
`git worktree list`, `git status --porcelain` empty, and their branches
(`feature/auto-20261126-054211-gh35711`, `feature/auto-20261126-015249-gh36467`,
`feature/auto-20261126-030013-gh36059`) all present on `origin`. The relocation
step completed; the deletion step never did, for hours.

## Root cause

### Mode A

`process_item` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py:255`
classifies each item through a single if/elif chain:

- line 274: `elif not pending and not os.path.lexists(item["path"])` yields
  `already-absent`. The absence test is the **root path only**.
- line 280: `elif item["modern"]:` calls `take_over_managed`, which runs
  `require_managed_takeover(reconstructible, ...)` (line 248) and inspects the
  source through `reconstructible` in `legacy_inventory.py:44`.

A half-removed worktree satisfies neither branch correctly. Its root still
exists, so line 274 does not fire. It is `modern`, so line 280 fires, and the
source inspection stats the missing `.git` administration path and raises
`FileNotFoundError` (errno 2). That is an `OSError` subclass, so it is caught by
the broad handler at line 290:

    except (ValueError, OSError, sqlite3.Error, ObservationUnavailable,
            subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        outcome.update(retained_outcome(item, error))

`retained_outcome` in `legacy_options.py:77` then reports
`status="retained"` plus `failure_details(error)`
(`cleanup_failure.py:14`, which copies `reason=type(error).__name__` and
`errno`) plus `ownership="managed-by-current-cleanup"` for modern items.

The defect is the classification, not the guards. A **permanent structural
inconsistency is reported in the same shape as a transient guard refusal**, so
it is retried forever and never escalated. There is no third state between
"fully present" and "fully absent", and no code path treats a present tree with
absent Git administration as an interrupted removal to finish.

### Mode B

Retirement itself is already designed to resume. `_finish` in
`.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/retirement.py:257` re-derives its
position from observed state on every call (line 279 relocates only when the
private tree is absent and no `removing` event exists; line 281 removes when the
tree is present), so the staging container is not an unrecoverable state by
design.

What stops it is a guard that runs **before** the resume logic.
`_validate_owner_evidence` (line 241, called at line 268) requires the
admission row to be `closed` **and** every run row to satisfy
`row["admitted"] and row["state"] == "ended"`. A worker killed without
completing its run teardown leaves a run row that is not `ended`, so
`_validate_owner_evidence` raises `StoreConflict("retirement-owner-evidence-changed")`
on every subsequent pass and `_finish` never reaches line 281. The same stall
shape is produced by `require_idle_processes(target)` (line 221) when the
process census cannot read a same-user CWD, which matches the observed
`refused=6 skip_reasons=cwd-visibility-degraded:6` in
`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/logs/storage-hygiene.log`.

Because the admission row is only deleted at the very end (line 287-294), a
generation whose owner evidence can never be completed is both un-retireable and
un-forgettable.

## Correction to the requested framing

The request was "deletion must be atomic" plus "add a cleanup for directories
without `.git`". Both need correcting before implementation.

1. **Atomic recursive deletion is not available on POSIX.** `rename` is atomic;
   `rm -r` is not. Retirement already uses the strongest available construct
   (atomic `git worktree move` into a private container at
   `retirement.py:140,175`, then delete). Mode B proves that rename-to-staging
   plus a delete step still leaks when the resume path is gated by evidence that
   can never arrive. Adding more atomicity to the delete is not the fix.

2. **"Directories without `.git`" is the symptom, not the class.** The real
   invariant is: *every half-state must be classified as resumable work and
   driven to completion or to an explicit terminal refusal, and must never be
   reported as a retryable guard refusal.* A sweeper keyed on "no `.git`" would
   miss mode B entirely, since those directories do have `.git`.

The correct invariant is therefore: **removal is a resumable state machine whose
every intermediate state is recognised, and whose terminal refusals are
distinguishable from transient ones.**

## Why this recurs despite prior fixes

This exact failure family has been filed and closed at least nine times:
GH#36795, GH#36798, GH#37034, GH#37181, GH#37385, GH#37729, GH#37895, GH#38158
and GH#36851, plus GH#37326 (resume interrupted native removal) which is cited
in `interrupted_removal.py`. Each addressed one guard or one ordering; none
introduced a state that is unambiguously "half-removed", so a newly-discovered
half-state keeps landing in the generic `except OSError` path and is reported as
`retained`. Fix the classification, not the next individual guard.

## Proposed change

1. **Recognise the half-state explicitly.** In `process_item`
   (`legacy_cleanup.py:255`), before the `item["modern"]` branch at line 280,
   detect "root present, Git administration absent or unreadable" and route it
   to the interrupted-removal resume path rather than to the takeover guards.
   `interrupted_removal.py` and `legacy_resume.py` already carry the
   deletion-only evidence concepts needed; reuse `RECONSTRUCTIBLE_REMOVING`
   handling at line 270-273 rather than adding a parallel mechanism.

2. **Stop laundering structural errors as retryable.** In `retained_outcome`
   (`legacy_options.py:77`), separate a terminal classification failure from a
   transient guard refusal, so the emitted JSON carries a distinct status (for
   example `unclassified` or `needs-resume`) instead of `retained`. A path that
   produces the same `errno`/`reason` pair on N consecutive passes must escalate
   rather than loop; `cleanup_quarantine.py` already has backoff but grants no
   authority, so escalation must be a reported terminal state.

3. **Make retirement resume independent of unobtainable owner evidence.** In
   `retirement.py`, a generation whose private tree is already relocated and
   whose branch is present on the remote must be completable. Either evaluate
   `_validate_owner_evidence` (line 241) only on the pre-relocation path, or add
   an explicit bounded reconciliation for run rows that can never reach `ended`
   because their process is gone. Do not weaken the clean/pushed/idle guards and
   do not remove the `require_removable` deletion-only check (line 228).

4. **Sweep retire staging on its own cadence.** `legacy_discovery.py:39` already
   knows `_CONTAINERS = (".lifecycle-retire-", ".legacy-retire-")`. Ensure an
   unconditional idempotent pass enumerates those containers from the filesystem
   and either completes or terminally reports each one, independent of the
   generation that created it.

Constraints: preserve the dirty-content guards (`require_deletion_only`), the
owner claim checks (`require_managed_authority`, `require_idle_processes`), the
cwd-visibility refusals, and the preservation-name exclusions in
`legacy_options.py:62-66`. This issue is about completing or terminally
reporting half-states, never about deleting anything a guard currently protects.

## Target areas

- `legacy_cleanup.py` — `process_item` classification chain (line 255-293)
- `legacy_options.py` — `retained_outcome` (line 77-84)
- `cleanup_failure.py` — `failure_details` (line 14)
- `retirement.py` — `_finish` (line 257), `_validate_owner_evidence` (line 241), `_remove_private` (line 213)
- `legacy_discovery.py` — `_CONTAINERS` (line 39) and container enumeration
- `interrupted_removal.py` — `resume_first` reuse
- `test_reconstructible.py` — asserts `status == "retained"` at lines 65, 250, 469, 512, 575 and `ownership` at line 225; update for the new terminal status
- `test_retirement.py` — asserts an empty `.lifecycle-retire-*` glob at lines 750, 773
- `LEGACY-CLEANUP.md` — line 129 documents the `managed-by-current-cleanup` ownership contract
- `CLEANUP.md` — update the state-machine description

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_options.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_failure.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/retirement.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_discovery.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/interrupted_removal.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_runner.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`


Scope correction (GH#40569): `legacy_runner.run` is the only caller of the
legacy cleanup pass, so proposed change 4 (an unconditional retire-staging sweep
on its own cadence) is invoked there; adding it to `cleanup.cleanup_pass` would
duplicate the same journaled retirement under two writers. Evidence: 
`legacy_runner.py:42-56` iterates `process_item` and is reached by
`worker-legacy-cleanup.py` on the observed 10-minute cycle that emitted the
reported `retained` loop. Verification: the existing pass report plus
`tests/test_reconstructible.py` and `tests/test_retirement.py`.

## Verification

1. Regression test, mode A: build a managed worktree fixture, delete only its
   `.git` file, run a cleanup pass, and assert the outcome is a resume or a
   terminal classification, never `status="retained"` with
   `reason="FileNotFoundError"`. A second pass must not reproduce the same
   outcome unchanged.
2. Regression test, mode B: interrupt after `git worktree move` into
   `.lifecycle-retire-*` while leaving a run row not `ended`, then run a later
   pass and assert the container is gone and `git worktree list` no longer
   mentions it. `test_retirement.py:750,773` already encodes the end state.
3. Run the existing suites: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`,
   `test_retirement.py`, and the shell suites
   `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`,
   `test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-cleanup.sh`,
   `test-pulse-cleanup-preserves-dirty.sh` (the last must still pass unchanged —
   dirty content stays preserved).
4. Field check on a host with residue: a cleanup pass must reduce the count of
   managed worktree base entries that have no `.git` and the count of
   `.lifecycle-retire-*` containers, with each action reported in
   `cleanup_worktrees.log` under a non-`retained` status.

## Not in scope

Per-worktree disk cost (~2.2G of tracked content per worktree in the observed
repository, of which 1.4G is a single tracked data directory) is a separate
concern and should not be addressed here.

</details>

## Brief Workflow

title: worktree-helper remove fails closed on unrelated foreign-user process with unreadable CWD
body:
## Observed

On Linux, `worktree-helper.sh remove <branch>` refused retirement with `proc-observation-unavailable`, `cause=inspection-not-enabled`, `stage=cwd`, and a PID/TID identifying a root-owned `sudo -v` waiting for a password in another terminal. The process had been running for more than two days. `recovery unreadable-processes` incorrectly reported that no same-user unreadable CWDs existed and visibility was complete.

## Expected

- An unrelated foreign-user process should not block retirement when evidence proves it is foreign.
- At minimum, `recovery unreadable-processes` must list unreadable foreign-user PIDs too, with owner information, so the native census refusal can be diagnosed.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` remove and recovery paths
- Native worker-lifecycle census emitting `inspection-not-enabled`

## Implementation evidence and approach

The live default already skips native tasks when none of their four `Uid:` fields matches the caller (`legacy_proc.live_owned_proc_task`). Root ownership alone is not proof of foreign identity: a setuid-root helper can retain the caller's real UID. Keep all retirement and privilege safeguards unchanged. Implement the explicitly authorized diagnostic fallback: a read-only, unprivileged listing of unreadable CWDs across all visible processes and threads, including foreign UID entries, showing PID, TID, sanitized comm and four numeric UID fields. Do not infer global census completeness from an empty CWD listing; FD-only denials and enumeration failures remain possible. No sudo invocation, process control or permission changes.

Before editing: issue OPEN; no existing PR or pushed issue branch found; fetched origin/main and verified the diagnostic gap persists. Python 3.13 available; the local ShellCheck wrapper has no real binary, so CI supplies ShellCheck coverage.

Brief repaired: PR #40573 CI at a6e526fa44 reported one new `qlty:file-complexity` finding in `worktree_process_proc.py`. Keep the manual diagnostic separate from clearance providers by moving its functions into the adjacent `worktree_process_diagnostics.py` module. The existing provider imports the diagnostic entrypoint and name formatter; behavior and all safety boundaries stay unchanged. Collision discovery found no competing work on the new module; the issue remains assigned and in progress. Re-run focused fixture, process-census tests, Python compilation and CI regression checks.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_proc.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_diagnostics.py`
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle-maintenance.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

## Verification

Original reproduction: leave `sudo -v` at a password prompt in another terminal, create and remove a test worktree, then check that removal succeeds or names the foreign PID and owner and that recovery lists the PID. Do not create privileged processes in automated verification.

- Exercise `worktree-helper.sh recovery unreadable-processes` on Linux without invoking sudo.
- Run the existing recovery maintenance suite, extending its unreadable-CWD fixture to cover foreign UID and private thread CWDs.
- Run existing native retirement-process tests to ensure refusal safeguards remain intact.
- Run ShellCheck on changed shell files, Python compilation, and the repository affected-tests helper.

<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->

title: Interactive claim released on GitHub without audit comment; local stamp left stale with reused PID
body:
## Observed

An interactive claim on a managed private project issue was released on GitHub without any audit comment, about 62 minutes after it was taken. A worker on another runner then dispatched legitimately and merged a fix. The interactive user later started a new session believing the issue was still claimed, and only discovered the merged duplicate during pre-work dedup.

Timeline (UTC, from the issue timeline API; actor shown as a role, not a login):

| Time | Event | Actor |
|------|-------|-------|
| 05:57:26 | assigned, `status:available` | interactive user |
| 05:57:54 | `status:available` -> `status:claimed`; claim comment posted (`aidevops-interactive-claim/v1`) | interactive user |
| 06:59:40 | **unassigned** | interactive user's token |
| 06:59:42 | **`status:claimed` removed** | interactive user's token |
| 06:59:44 | **`status:available` added** | interactive user's token |
| 07:04:36 | `DISPATCH_CLAIM` by another runner | other runner |
| 08:02:00 | worker PR merged, issue closed | other runner |

No comment of any kind was posted for the 06:59 release: no `CLAIM_RELEASED`, unclaim, stale-recovery or reason marker.

Local state on the claiming host afterwards: the claim stamp still existed, and its PID had been reused by an unrelated `opencode` process started after the claim, so a PID-only liveness check would treat the dead claim as alive.

## Why this is a framework problem

1. **Silent release.** Whatever released the claim did not leave an audit comment. This breaks "Git is the audit trail".
2. **Stamp and GitHub state diverge.**
3. **PID reuse.** The stamp stores `pid` plus `owner_argv_hash` but no process start time.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` and `interactive-session-helper-scan.sh` (`scan-stale`, `release-if-dead`, `reap-dead-stamps`, `release`)
- `normalize_active_issue_assignments` and `_has_active_claim` in the pulse issue-reconcile path (`pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`)
- Any session-end or OpenCode plugin hook that releases interactive claims

## Expected

- Every automatic release of an interactive claim posts a short audit comment with the reason, for example `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=<dead-owner|stale|session-end> host=<host> stamp_pid=<n>`, and deletes or tombstones the local stamp in the same operation.
- Stamp liveness binds the PID to the process start time, so PID reuse cannot keep a dead claim alive or misattribute ownership.
- Optional: `interactive-session-helper.sh status` should report the GitHub-side truth, not just the stamp.

## Verification

- Reproduce: claim an issue interactively, end the session, and let the stale or dead-owner release path run. Confirm an audit comment appears and the stamp is removed.
- Unit test: a stamp whose PID belongs to a process started after `claimed_at` is classified as dead.
- `shellcheck` clean on touched scripts.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-stamp.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/reconcile-stuck-claims.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stamp-owner-start-time.sh`

title: gh-write-helper: pr comment warns 'approval verification errored' for normal NO_APPROVAL state
body:
## Problem

`gh-write-helper.sh pr comment` prints a misleading warning on every PR that simply has no signed approval:

```
[aidevops][gh-write-helper][WARN] approval verification errored (exit 1); posting without approval guard
```

The comment still posts correctly (the guard fails open), but the message reports a verification error when nothing went wrong. Operators then spend time investigating, or learn to ignore the warning, which hides real verification errors such as `API_ERROR` (exit 6).

## Evidence

Observed 2026-11-27 posting an evidence comment on an open PR in a private managed repo that had no signed approval.

Reproduced read-only:

```
approval-helper.sh verify pr <N> <owner/repo>
NO_APPROVAL      # exit 1
```

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh` `_pr_comment_guarded()` (around line 72) treats any non-zero exit as an error unless the last line is `STALE_APPROVAL` or `UNSIGNED`:

```bash
elif [[ "$rc" != 0 && "$last" != "STALE_APPROVAL" && "$last" != "UNSIGNED" ]]; then
    printf '...approval verification errored (exit %s); posting without approval guard\n' "$rc" >&2
```

`.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` (verify path, around line 1965) returns `NO_APPROVAL` with exit 1 when no approval marker comment exists. That expected, non-error outcome is missing from the allowlist. In addition, `approval-helper.sh` never emits `UNSIGNED` (`rg -n UNSIGNED .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` returns nothing), so that allowlist entry is dead or drifted from the helper's actual vocabulary.

## Suggested fix

Files:
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: in `_pr_comment_guarded()`, treat `NO_APPROVAL` as a known non-error state alongside `STALE_APPROVAL`. Review whether `UNSIGNED` should be replaced by the real state name the helper emits, or removed. Keep the warning for genuine errors (`API_ERROR`, unknown output, empty output).
- Existing tests for `gh-write-helper.sh` / the approval guard (locate with `rg -ln "_pr_comment_guarded|allow-approval-stale" .agents/scripts/tests`). Add or extend a case that stubs `AIDEVOPS_APPROVAL_HELPER` to print `NO_APPROVAL` with exit 1, and assert that no WARN line appears and the comment is still forwarded to `gh_pr_comment`.

Keep the fail-open behaviour and the `VERIFIED` block unchanged.

## Verification

- With a stubbed helper printing `NO_APPROVAL` (exit 1): no warning, and the comment is posted.
- With a stubbed helper printing `API_ERROR` (exit 6): the warning still appears.
- With a stubbed helper printing `VERIFIED` (exit 0): still blocked with return 2.
- ShellCheck is clean on `gh-write-helper.sh`.

title: Issue-ref TODO sync appends duplicate lines for issues whose TODO entries are still in an open PR
body:
## Observed

In a private project repo, an interactive PR added `TODO.md` lines for five new follow-up tasks (`ref:GH#...` to five open issues filed by the same session). While the PR was open, the scheduled "chore: sync GitHub issue refs to TODO.md" commit on `main` appended its own lines for the same five issues, because the issues were open and `main` had no TODO entries for them yet.

At merge, `full-loop-helper.sh merge` stopped with `prospective merge introduces duplicate TODO mappings`. A worker then had to merge `main` into the branch and delete the five sync-appended lines by hand before the merge could go through.

## Expected

The issue-ref sync should not append TODO lines for issues whose TODO entries already exist in an open PR's diff, for example issues linked from an open PR or referenced by its changed `TODO.md`. Alternatively, the merge guard could resolve exact duplicates itself, keeping the PR's fuller entry.

Candidate files: the issue-ref-to-TODO sync job (path not verified) and the `prospective-todo-guard` in `full-loop-helper.sh`.

## Verification

Open a PR that adds TODO lines for newly filed issues, then let the sync run on `main`. After the PR merges, `rg -n 'ref:GH#N' TODO.md` shows one line per issue, with no manual fix needed.

title: Pulse takeover merges idle origin:interactive PRs whose owner review is still pending
body:
## Observed

In a private project repo, an interactive session opened a ready (non-draft) `origin:interactive` PR for an owner-reviewed research task. The PR body said: "Please do not merge before reviewing: the proposed plans become usable only after written approval." The task brief also said the owner reviews at the end.

After the session had been idle 4 hours:

1. The pulse handover added `origin:worker-takeover` and posted a takeover comment, because a review-bot thread was still unresolved.
2. A worker fixed the four CodeRabbit threads. That part was fine.
3. About two hours later the pulse supervisor ran `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <slug> --squash` and merged the PR. The owner never reviewed or approved it, and the issue closed.

The interactive session only learned of the handover through a session-bus message, delivered at the owner's next turn, after the merge.

No harm resulted: the repository's own rules keep the proposed plans unusable until the owner approves them in writing. But the owner's review step was skipped, and the "do not merge" request in prose was not honoured.

## Expected

A takeover may resolve review threads, but it should not merge an interactive PR whose owner review is still pending. Possible fixes (paths not verified):

- The interactive full-loop applies a hold label (for example `hold-for-review` or `no-takeover`) when the brief or the PR body says the owner reviews before merge, and the takeover merge path refuses PRs that carry it.
- Or the takeover merge path checks the PR body for an explicit do-not-merge request and stops with a comment.
- Or the handover notice reaches the owning session (or the user) before the takeover acts, not after.

Candidate files: the pulse handover and takeover logic, `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, and `workflows/full-loop.md` (interactive PRs that need owner review).

## Verification

An `origin:interactive` PR that carries the hold signal and goes idle past the handover threshold gets its review threads fixed, but it is not merged until the hold is removed.

title: t19425: fix(locks): mkdir-as-mutex is not exclusive under uutils coreutils (Ubuntu 26.04) — two concurrent owners
body:
## Task


Make every `mkdir`-as-mutex lock exclusive on hosts where `mkdir` is uutils (rust-coreutils), the default on Ubuntu 26.04. Today two concurrent `mkdir <same path>` calls can both exit 0 there, so the lock admits two owners.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make every `mkdir`-as-mutex lock exclusive on hosts where `mkdir` is uutils (rust-coreutils), the default on Ubuntu 26.04. Today two concurrent `mkdir <same path>` calls can both exit 0 there, so the lock admits two owners.

## Why

GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` is now `ubuntu-26.04` (run 46000916604 set-up log: `Image: ubuntu-26.04`, version `20261116.202.1`). On that image `mkdir` resolves to `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/mkdir` (`mkdir (uutils coreutils) 0.10.0`). GNU coreutils remains installed as `gnumkdir` (package `gnu-coreutils`).

Reproduction in `docker run ubuntu:26.04`: two background `mkdir "$d"` calls on one fresh path, repeated 2000 times.

| tool | iterations where both exited 0 |
|------|-------------------------------|
| `mkdir` (uutils 0.10.0) | 885 / 2000 |
| `gnumkdir` (GNU) | 0 / 2000 |
| `ln -s` (uutils) | 0 / 2000 (not affected) |

On the same image `mv` and `cp` are GNU; `ln` and `sort` are uutils.

This explains every Linux-runner-only lock race in `Shell Suite Main Health`. None of them reproduced in `ubuntu:24.04` Docker, which has GNU `mkdir`:

- `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, `test_decision_policy_races`: the fixture's fake `gh` creates refs with `mkdir`. The run-46000916604 artifact shows two PIDs (1339657/1339658) both `POST`-ing the same findings ref 23 µs apart, both `rc=0`, and then both creating `slots/1` with `rc=0`. In the same run, `concurrent daily digest writers ...` failed through the same `mkdir` reservation (`test_unknown_daily_digest`).
- `test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` and `test-gh-quota-lock-race.sh` were regressions on main in run 46000916604. #40579 hardened their ownership protocol; whether they still rely on `mkdir` exclusivity is unknown.

Production impact: about 90 non-test scripts take `mkdir` locks, for example `pulse-instance-lock.sh`, `claim-task-id-counter.sh`, `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`, `cleanup-worktrees-lock.sh`, `canonical-recovery-lock.sh`, `audit-log-helper.sh` and `gh-quota-attribution-lib.sh`. List them with `rg -l -e 'if mkdir ' -e 'until mkdir ' -e 'while ! mkdir ' -e 'mkdir "[^"]*lock' .agents/scripts`. Any user or pulse host on Ubuntu 26.04 (or another uutils distro) can get duplicate lock owners. Which runner hosts run 26.04 is unknown. macOS and GNU hosts are unaffected.

## How

1. Add one shared exclusive-create primitive and use it everywhere. Recommended: in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`, detect uutils once (`mkdir --version` contains `uutils`). If `gnumkdir` is available, define a `mkdir` shell function that calls `command gnumkdir "$@"`. Otherwise define one that does an exclusive `mkdir(2)` per path: `python3 -c 'import os,sys; os.mkdir(sys.argv[1])'` for the non-`-p` lock form, and keeps `command mkdir` for `-p`. Keep it Bash 3.2-safe; never touch it on GNU or macOS.
2. Check which lock scripts do not source `shared-constants.sh`, and cover them through the same primitive. Do not hand-edit every call site if one sourced definition reaches them. These scripts cannot be listed in advance; enumerate them with the `rg` in Why and add them to the PR's file list.
3. Make the deterministic fixtures exclusive the same way: the fake `gh` ref creation in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh` (around line 69) and the digest label reservation (around line 554). The helper suite does not source `shared-constants.sh` directly, so confirm how the fixture obtains the primitive.
4. Optional: add a guard to `.agents/scripts/tests/` or Framework Validation that proves the primitive is exclusive under concurrency on the CI image (about 200 iterations, both-succeed count must be 0). It should be cheap and run on `ubuntu-latest`.
5. Document the platform trap in `.agents/reference/platform-support.md` (Linux section), one short paragraph with the table above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In `docker run ubuntu:26.04`, concurrent exclusive-create through the new primitive reports 0 double successes over 2000 iterations. Plain uutils `mkdir` remains reproducibly non-exclusive, as the negative control.
- [ ] `Shell Suite Main Health` on the branch: `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (incl. `test_decision_policy_races` and the daily-digest race), `test-audit-log-concurrency.sh` and `test-gh-quota-lock-race.sh` pass with no `flaky` classification.
- [ ] macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2: the full checkpoint helper suite and the audit/quota suites still pass; ShellCheck clean on changed files.
- [ ] No behaviour change on GNU or macOS `mkdir` (the shim is inactive there).

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh
- .agents/reference/platform-support.md

- `.agents/scripts/mkdir-exclusive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli-converge-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cpu-saturation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/issue-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/objective-reconciliation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shellcheck-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-lock.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-quota-attribution-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-runtime-pin.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-runtime-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-runtime.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mkdir-exclusive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-runtime-pin.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-runtime-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-audit-log-concurrency.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-quota-lock-race.sh`

Brief repaired: the source audit found standalone gh transport, canonical recovery, archive, saturation, setup and Pulse bootstrap lock paths that do not load shared constants before acquisition. These paths must source the same dependency-light primitive directly; the checkpoint fixture must load it explicitly. Verification: ShellCheck changed shell files; test-mkdir-exclusive.sh (2000 concurrent attempts on Ubuntu 26.04, including the plain-mkdir negative control); checkpoint continuation, audit concurrency and quota lock-race suites; affected-tests-helper.sh against origin/main. Native macOS verification remains required through the existing platform verification route.

Brief repaired: verification found the audit publication fixture and quota race suite define mkdir interceptors that call command mkdir, bypassing the compatibility function on uutils. Their interceptors must invoke the named shared primitive instead; verify both existing suites and the new concurrency guard. This is necessary fixture integration for the stated Ubuntu acceptance criteria, not a changed lock protocol.

Brief repaired: affected-suite comparison isolated one introduced failure: test-pulse-runtime-pin.sh stages the real pin helper into a minimal old-bundle fixture but omits its new mkdir-exclusive.sh sibling. Add that shipped dependency to the existing fixture copy list and rerun this suite. The other eleven red suites also fail on origin/main and remain out of scope.

Brief repaired: terminal Ubuntu advisory CI identifies five integration regressions. Restricted-PATH fixtures must resolve external tools with type -P rather than command -v now that mkdir may be a function; the routine fixture otherwise recursively invokes mkdir. The gh shim and deployment bundle fixtures must copy the new sibling library. Pin the selected GNU mkdir executable so later restricted PATHs cannot lose the detected implementation. Rerun these existing suites and affected CI; do not weaken any gate.

Supersedes #40562 (root cause found). Ref #40529, #40578, #40579.

title: t19426: fix(ci): suite-health logs drop a flaky suite's first attempt when the rerun fills the 80-line tail
body:
## Task


Keep a flaky suite's first-attempt failure evidence in the `Shell Suite Main Health` artifact when the passing rerun prints 80 or more lines.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Keep a flaky suite's first-attempt failure evidence in the `Shell Suite Main Health` artifact when the passing rerun prints 80 or more lines.

## Why

#40529 (PR #40533) made `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh` append rerun output after a `--- rerun attempt ---` marker. The log write-out then keeps the last `LOG_TAIL_LINES` (80) lines, plus up to 40 earlier lines that match `\bFAIL\b|\bnot ok\b|Traceback|\bERROR\b`.

For a long suite, the passing rerun fills the whole tail, which drops both the marker and the first attempt. If the first attempt printed no line that matches the pattern, nothing of it survives. Example: in run 45943811093, `test-headless-runtime-helper-state.sh` was `1,0 flaky`. Its artifact log is exactly 80 lines of the rerun, ending in `Failures: 0`. It has no marker and no first-attempt line, so the flake cannot be diagnosed. `Failures: 1` does not match the pattern either, because `\bFAIL\b` requires a word boundary after `FAIL`.

## How

1. EDIT `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh`, the log write-out loop near `head_lines, tail = lines[:-LOG_TAIL_LINES], lines[-LOG_TAIL_LINES:]` (around line 421). Split the scratch log on the `--- rerun attempt ---` marker lines. Write each attempt as its own section: early failure lines (if any), then that attempt's last `LOG_TAIL_LINES` lines. Keep the marker between sections. A single attempt keeps today's output exactly.
2. Optional: widen `early_failure_line` to also match a non-zero failure summary such as `Failures: [1-9]` or `[1-9][0-9]* failed`, without matching `0 failed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A synthetic flaky suite whose first attempt prints 30 lines ending in a non-pattern failure summary, and whose rerun prints 120 passing lines, yields a log that contains the first attempt's last lines, the marker, and the rerun tail.
- [ ] A single-attempt red suite's log is byte-identical to today's format.

title: fix(issue-sync): closure-reason labeler marks not-planned closes as duplicate from loose comment keywords
body:
## What

The closure-reason labeler applies a wrong specific label when an issue is closed as not planned. It searches the whole last comment for loose keywords, so a structured review that only mentions duplicates, or uses the phrase "already exists", gets the issue labelled `duplicate`.

## Why

Observed on #40581 (2026-11-27). The maintainer posted a Decline review ("works as designed") and closed the issue as not planned. Nine seconds later, `github-actions[bot]` added `duplicate`. The trigger was the review's table row "The requested outcome already exists". The issue is not a duplicate; the label was corrected to `not-planned` by hand.

The maintainer Decline flow (`.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md:354`) is: post the review, then close. The standard review template (`review-issue-pr.md:269-320`) always contains "Pre-existing duplicates" and "Not a pre-existing duplicate" rows. So any templated Decline review that is the last comment before close gets labelled `duplicate`. Labels must have one specific meaning; a wrong specific label is worse than the generic `not-planned`.

## Reproducer

1. On a `marcusquinn/aidevops` issue, post a comment whose body contains `already exists` (or the review-template row `| Pre-existing duplicates | None |`) but no duplicate claim.
2. Close the issue with reason "not planned".
3. Observed: the `Label Issue Closure Reason` job adds `duplicate`. Evidence on #40581: timeline `2026-11-27T16:18:38Z closed by marcusquinn`, then `2026-11-27T16:18:47Z labeled duplicate by github-actions[bot]`. The last comment is `7223004983`, which contains "The requested outcome already exists".
4. Expected: `not-planned`.

Root-cause line: `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml:1990` — `grep -qiE 'duplicate|dupe|already exists'` over the full comment body.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: one inline step in one workflow file, with a known pattern and local verification.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml:1985-1998` (job `label-closure-reason`, step "Apply closure reason label", `not_planned)` branch)

### Implementation Steps

1. Leave the existing early exits unchanged: issues already labelled `duplicate`/`wontfix` (`:1979-1984`), and the `status:done` skip (`:1969`). The automated dedup path labels `duplicate` *before* closing (`:804-805`), so it is unaffected.
2. Replace the keyword `grep -qiE` checks at `:1990-1998` with explicit closing-intent patterns only:
   - `duplicate`: `duplicate of #[0-9]+`, `closing as (a )?duplicate`, or the `<!-- issue-dedup:auto-closed -->` marker.
   - `already-fixed`: `already (fixed|resolved|implemented|addressed) (by|in) #[0-9]+`, or `closing as superseded` (the superseded template, `review-issue-pr.md:446`).
   - `wontfix`: `wontfix`, `won't fix`, `will not fix`. Drop bare `will not`.
   - Otherwise: `not-planned` (existing fallback).
3. A body that starts with `## Review: Recommendation: Decline` and has no explicit duplicate/superseded phrase must resolve to `not-planned`.
4. Keep the matching in Bash 3.2-compatible `grep -qiE` inside the existing step. Do not add new label names.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Closing as not planned, with the #40581 Decline review (comment `7223004983`) as the last comment, resolves to `not-planned`, not `duplicate`.
- [ ] A last comment containing "duplicate of #123" still resolves to `duplicate`.
- [ ] The superseded template text ("Closing as superseded.") resolves to `already-fixed`.
- [ ] A comment with only a "Pre-existing duplicates | None" table row resolves to `not-planned`.

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` (or the repo's configured workflow lint in `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`).
- Extract the new `case` block into a scratch shell function under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. Feed it the four acceptance bodies (fetch the #40581 body with `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/comments/7223004983 --jq .body`) and confirm each label. Do not add a committed test harness for this.

## Scope Boundaries

- No change to the dedup auto-close path (`:780-810`), the `completed` branch, or label names.
- No change to review templates. The labeler must tolerate them as written.

title: docs(workflow): gate workflow-strategy steerage in issue creation and review guidance
body:
## What

Add one canonical rule for **workflow-strategy changes**, with short pointers from every surface that creates or reviews issues. The rule: behaviour that matches a deliberate design decision is not a bug. A change to workflow strategy needs maintainer direction before it becomes dispatchable work.

## Origin and maintainer direction

Maintainer direction (2026-11-27, interactive session, after the #40581 re-review):

> yes, definitely need some gating of any workflow strategy steerage issues that might cause unnecessary frictions and hinder progress. both the review-issue-pr agent should know this, and log-issue-aidevops and anywhere else that creates issues

Maintainer comment on #40581: "`origin:interactive` is just a provenance signal — not an action signal … the correct workflow is to use verbose intentional labels, like the `needs-*` labels, or `hold-for-review` … this is why i gate-keep workflow strategy on this repo."

This issue is maintainer-directed, so the rule it adds does not apply to this issue itself.

## Why

Observed failure on #40581:

1. `/log-issue-aidevops` Step 3.7 runs the alignment check for enhancements only, and skips "bugs with clear reproduction steps" (`.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md:183`). Designed behaviour (idle interactive PR takeover and merge: GH#23425, GH#38291) was therefore filed as a bug.
2. `review-issue-pr.md` 2.1 tells reviewers to recommend approval for "correct and actionable" issues (`:137`). Nothing there separates a defect from a request to change strategy. The first review recommended Approve and proposed a new `commit-and-pr --hold-for-review` flag, plus a guidance change that would push agents to hold PRs for human review. The maintainer rejected it, and the re-review declined the issue.
3. `.agents/AGENTS.md:45` tells every session to file findings as auto-dispatch tasks immediately, with no exception for strategy changes. Workers, the pulse and ambient self-improvement can therefore file and dispatch strategy steerage with no maintainer in the loop.

## Tier

`tier:standard`. All decisions are made below, with exact text. The work is placing short edits in 7 existing files and creating 1 new reference doc.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- NEW: `.agents/reference/workflow-strategy.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md:45`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md:100-111`, `:123`, `:137`, `:309`, `:400-408`, `:457-463`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md:50-70`, `:183`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/brief.md:96-139`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md:66`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/self-improvement.md:107-110`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md:33`

Do not edit `.agents/scripts/commands/log-issue-aidevops.md` or `.agents/scripts/commands/new-task.md`. Both are git symlinks (mode 120000) to the `workflows/` files. `/new-task` reaches the rule through `workflows/brief.md`.

### Implementation Steps

**1. NEW `.agents/reference/workflow-strategy.md`** (exact content; add the SPDX header lines used by sibling reference docs):

```markdown
# Workflow-Strategy Changes

Workflow strategy is the maintainer's decision. An issue that changes it without maintainer direction adds friction for every repository that uses the framework: new holds and waits, or labels with a second meaning. Precedent: GH#40581 reported designed takeover-and-merge behaviour as a bug, and the first review recommended a new hold flag as the fix.

## What counts

A change is a workflow-strategy change when it alters any of these:

- **When work moves on its own**: dispatch, takeover or handover, merge, close, release, and their defaults, opt-ins and opt-outs.
- **What stops work**: new gates, holds, waits, required reviews or approvals, throttles.
- **What a label or marker means**: giving a provenance or status label an action effect (for example treating `origin:interactive` as "do not merge"), or giving one label a second meaning.
- **Who owns work**: the boundaries between interactive sessions, workers and the pulse.

Fixing code so that existing gates and labels behave as documented is not a strategy change; file it as a bug (for example GH#40590, a labeler applying the wrong label, or GH#40580, enforcing an existing rule).

**Maintainer direction** means an OWNER or MEMBER asked for the change, in the current session or on the issue, or signed an approval of a review that recommends it.

## The test

Does the reported behaviour match a documented or deliberate decision? Check `reference/` and `workflows/`, then the change that introduced the behaviour (`git log -S '<symbol>'` and its linked issue). If it does, the request is a strategy change, even when it comes with a reproducer.

Before proposing a new control, point to an existing one:

| Need | Existing control |
|------|------------------|
| Hold one issue or PR for a maintainer decision | `hold-for-review` |
| Keep a PR away from workers | `no-takeover` |
| Keep an issue out of dispatch | `no-auto-dispatch` |
| A task whose deliverable is a PR, not a merge | PR-only completion contract (`workflows/full-loop.md`) |
| Interactive PR merge throughput | opt-ins in `reference/auto-merge.md` |

## Rules

- **Maintainer-directed**: proceed normally. Quote or link the direction in the brief.
- **Interactive, no direction**: do not file it as work. A maintainer gets one recommendation and a yes/no question; anyone else gets the existing control.
- **Headless workers, pulse, ambient self-improvement**: never file a strategy change as `bug` or with `auto-dispatch`. If an observed failure needs one, deduplicate, then file one `enhancement` + `hold-for-review` issue titled `proposal: …`. Name the decision it would change (with a link) and the evidence that its rationale no longer holds. It appears in the maintainer queue (`/decisions`). Otherwise record it in memory or drop it.
- **External reporters (`/log-issue-aidevops`)**: file designed behaviour as `enhancement`, citing the decision and the existing control, never as `bug`. `needs-maintainer-review` still gates it.
- **Reviewers (`workflows/review-issue-pr.md`, `workflows/triage-review.md`)**: recommend Decline (works as designed) and name the existing control. Without maintainer direction, never recommend Approve for a strategy change, and never offer a narrower new hold, flag or guidance route as the fix.

`hold-for-review` is the internal decision hold (`reference/task-lifecycle.md` "Canonical split"). Never use `needs-maintainer-review` for this; it means missing external-author authority. Do not create new labels.
```

**2. `.agents/AGENTS.md:45`**: replace the whole line with this. It must stay byte-light: the file is 23,984 bytes against a 24,000-byte CI limit (`.github/workflows/agents-md-size-check.yml:39`), and this line is +6 bytes.

```text
- Capture worker-dispatchable findings as auto-dispatch tasks now; a worker-ready issue is the decision to implement, not a request for approval. Workflow-strategy changes need maintainer direction: `reference/workflow-strategy.md`. Triage: `reference/worker-discipline.md`.
```

**3. `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`**:

- In 0.3 Framing critique, add this bullet after the "Security/setup advisory suppression" bullet (`:109`):
  `- **Designed behaviour reported as a bug** → find the change that introduced the behaviour (\`git log -S\`, its linked issue) and the docs that describe it. If it is deliberate, the request is a workflow-strategy change: apply \`reference/workflow-strategy.md\` (GH#40581).`
- `:123` "How to Verify" cell: `Check docs, design decisions; designed behaviour → \`reference/workflow-strategy.md\``
- `:137`: append to the end of the "Correct and actionable issue" bullet: ` This does not cover workflow-strategy changes: without maintainer direction, recommend Decline and name the existing control (\`reference/workflow-strategy.md\`); never turn one into a narrower new hold, flag or guidance route.`
- `:309` template row: `| Architectural intent | [Aligned / Contradicts / Unclear — cite the decision it keeps or changes; a workflow-strategy change needs maintainer direction] |`
- `:400-408` "Issue is Not a Bug" template: after `- [Link to docs]`, add `- [Existing control that already gives the requested behaviour, e.g. \`hold-for-review\`, \`no-takeover\`]`.
- `:457-463` "Fix Defeats a Recent Architectural Decision": after the template's closing fence, add the line: `Use this only when the issue reports a real defect. When the issue's goal is to change the decision itself, use "Issue is Not a Bug" and recommend Decline.`

**4. `.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md`**:

- `:50`: change "run these 6 checks" to "run these 7 checks".
- After item 6 (`:70`), add:
  `7. **Workflow-strategy check (GH#40581)**: if the reported behaviour matches a documented or deliberate decision, it is not a bug. Apply \`reference/workflow-strategy.md\`: file it as \`enhancement\`, cite the decision and the existing control (\`hold-for-review\`, \`no-takeover\`, config opt-ins), never as \`bug\`.`
- `:183`: replace with `Skip for bugs with clear reproduction steps, unless the reproduced behaviour is deliberate design (pre-composition check 7); then it is an enhancement.`

**5. `.agents/workflows/brief.md`**: before `## Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)` (`:139`), add:

```markdown
### 7. Workflow-strategy check (GH#40581)

If the brief changes when work moves, what stops it, what a label means, or who owns it, apply `reference/workflow-strategy.md` first. Behaviour that matches a documented decision is not a bug, and a strategy change needs maintainer direction before `auto-dispatch`.
```

**6. `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md:66`**: this agent is sandboxed and cannot read reference files, so the rule goes inline. Replace the line with:
`1. **Problem Validation**: Reproducible? Real bug or expected behavior? Behaviour that matches a documented decision is not a bug: recommend Decline and name the existing control (for example \`hold-for-review\`, \`no-takeover\`). Never recommend Approve for a change to when work is dispatched, taken over, merged or closed, what holds it, or what a label means, unless a maintainer has directed it in the thread (GH#40581).`

**7. `.agents/reference/self-improvement.md`**: after the `**Framework-level** …` paragraph (`:109`), add:
`**Workflow-strategy changes** (when work moves, what stops it, what a label means, who owns it) are never filed as \`bug\` or \`auto-dispatch\` without maintainer direction; see \`reference/workflow-strategy.md\`.`

**8. `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md:33`**: append to the Outcome B bullet:
` A workflow-strategy change is never an obvious fix: without maintainer direction in the brief, use Outcome C (\`reference/workflow-strategy.md\`).`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/reference/workflow-strategy.md`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`
- `.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md`
- `.agents/workflows/brief.md`
- `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md`
- `.agents/reference/self-improvement.md`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`

### Scope Boundaries

- Guidance only. No script, validator, label or workflow changes. Classifying a change as strategy is a judgment call, not a keyword match.
- Do not change merge, dispatch or takeover behaviour, or the meaning of any label.
- Do not add more examples or sections than the text above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.agents/reference/workflow-strategy.md` exists with the content above.
- [ ] `rg -n "workflow-strategy.md" .agents` lists pointers in all 7 edited files. `triage-review.md` has the inline rule instead.
- [ ] `wc -c < .agents/AGENTS.md` is ≤ 24000.
- [ ] Applied to #40581 as originally filed, the new log-issue check 7 files it as `enhancement`, not `bug`. The new review guidance gives Decline, matching the maintainer's re-review (issuecomment `7223004983`).
- [ ] Applied to #40580 and #40590, the guidance still treats them as bugs (existing rules enforced, not changed).

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` (includes Markdown formatting and the >500-line Markdown size gate).
- `wc -c < .agents/AGENTS.md`.
- `rg -n "workflow-strategy" .agents`.
- Read back each edited section once, and check that no numbered list or table structure broke.

title: Canonical maintenance-gc: recover gc.log blocked by reflogs referencing pruned commits
body:
## What

Extend the canonical maintenance path (`canonical-recovery-helper.sh maintenance-gc`, implemented in `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh`) to recover when a canonical repository's shared Git directory holds a `gc.log` caused by reflogs that reference pruned commits. Today the helper repairs stale locks and temporary pack debris (#39722) but has no step for this case, and the canonical guard correctly blocks direct `git reflog` and `rm` of `gc.log`, so an interactive session cannot recover.

## Why (observed 2026-11-27, Linux runner host, heavily used managed repo)

- `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror` printed Git's `The last gc run reported the following. Please correct the root cause and remove .git/gc.log. Automatic cleanup will not be performed until the file is removed.`
- `gc.log` held more than 500 lines, all the same six warnings repeated: `reflog of 'refs/heads/<branch>' references pruned commits`, for three local branches and their `refs/remotes/origin/` counterparts. The branch tips themselves are intact commits; only older reflog entries point at objects a previous prune removed.
- While `gc.log` is younger than `gc.logExpiry` (default 1 day), every automatic gc is skipped. When one does run (daemonized `git gc --auto --no-quiet`), the same reflog warnings are written again, so the block re-arms each cycle.
- `git count-objects -vH`: 1919 packs, 62.75 GiB `size-pack`, 226.8 million in-pack objects, 28 garbage files (924 MiB). One daemonized `gc --auto` (`repack -d -l --cruft`, then `pack-objects --all --reflog`) had been running for 11 hours at about 86% CPU and 1.3 GB RSS when observed.
- `maintenance-gc` dry run: 7 stale `tmp_pack_*` candidates (about 241 MB), 26 skipped as fresh, `gc.pid` skipped as live. It does not mention `gc.log` or the reflog warnings.
- Attempted read-only `git reflog show` in the canonical checkout was refused by `git.canonical-worktree` (`canonical worktree mutation via 'git reflog'`). There is no sanctioned alternative.

## How

1. In `canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh` `maintenance-gc`, add a dry-run report for `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/gc.log`: its age, line count, and the distinct `reflog of '<ref>' references pruned commits` refs it names.
2. With `--apply`, only when no live gc holds `gc.pid`, run `git reflog expire --stale-fix --expire=never <ref>` for each named ref that still exists (this drops only entries pointing at missing objects and keeps the rest), confirm that `git reflog expire --dry-run --all` no longer reports the warning, then remove `gc.log`. Record each ref and the removed file through `audit-log-helper.sh`.
3. Leave `gc.log` in place and report it when its contents include anything other than the known reflog warning, so unknown gc failures are not silently cleared.
4. Allow read-only `git reflog show`/`git reflog exists` in `canonical-git-command-guard.py` if it is safe to classify them separately from `expire`/`delete`.
5. Consider reporting pack count and `size-pack` in the dry run, with a hint when the pack count far exceeds `gc.autoPackLimit`, so a multi-hour gc is visible rather than mistaken for a hang.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh` (maintenance-gc)
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh` (subcommand wiring, if needed)
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py` (read-only reflog subcommands)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`

Reference pattern: the stale-lock and tmp-pack candidate handling added for #39722 in the same hygiene script.

## Verification

- In a fixture repository, create a branch, add reflog entries, delete the referenced objects and prune so that `git gc` writes `references pruned commits` to `gc.log`. The dry run reports the refs; `--apply` clears the warning and removes `gc.log`; a subsequent `git gc --auto` runs without the skip message.
- A `gc.log` with any other content is reported and left in place.
- `--apply` refuses while `gc.pid` belongs to a live process.
- ShellCheck clean; existing hygiene and guard tests pass.

## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #40599)

The previous worker's PR #40599 (`GH#40596: fix(canonical): repair gc.log stale-reflog warnings in maintenance-gc`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (5 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md
.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh
.agents/scripts/canonical_git_ref_queries.py
.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `8a179b5bbe9bbe696921aa82b5d19049cd815207`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/40599/head:recovered-40599
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick 8a179b5bbe9bbe696921aa82b5d19049cd815207
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #40599's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`.

_Routed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)._

title: Headless workers still pause on broad /dev/* external_directory asks after GH#40255
body:
## Observed

GH#40255 (fixed by PR #40263, first released in v3.39.283) narrowed headless worker device access so concrete reads and simple final device redirects no longer stop a worker. On v3.39.289 a headless worker in a managed private repository still paused with `permission_required` on this request:

- capability: `external_directory` via `bash`, pattern `"/dev/*"`
- risk shown in the request comment: high; "No additional model rationale was available."
- worker stage: tool execution, during a PR checkpoint continuation; committed work had been pushed, so nothing was lost

The worker log lives on another runner, so the exact command is not available here. The permission request comment deliberately omits raw tool metadata. Two other issues in the same repository hold `/dev/*` requests from before the fix; one more holds `~/*`.

## Why it matters

Each wall parks an issue under `needs-maintainer-permissions` until a maintainer runs a `sudo` approval or withdrawal. Granting `/dev/*` wholesale is too broad, so these holds usually end in withdrawal and redispatch, and the work is lost time either way.

## Likely cause (unverified)

`permission-broker-runtime-read.mjs` accepts only `RUNTIME_DEVICE = /^\/dev\/(?:null|stdin|stdout|stderr|fd\/[0-9]+)$/` with a recorded concrete target. A command shape that is not a "simple final device redirect" still escalates to the parent wildcard. Candidates: a redirect in the middle of a pipeline (`cmd 2>/dev/null | jq`), `</dev/null` input redirection, `/dev/tty`, `/dev/urandom` reads, or `>/dev/null 2>&1` inside `&&` chains.

## Worker-ready scope

1. Record the concrete target of the `/dev/*` ask in the permission request comment, as a normalized path only, so future holds show which device and command shape triggered them. Never record command arguments or values.
2. Extend the bounded exception to the device paths and redirect positions above that are safe: `/dev/null` in any redirect position, `</dev/null`, and read-only `/dev/urandom`/`/dev/random`. Keep `/dev/tty`, block devices and any write other than to `/dev/null` held.
3. Keep broad `/dev/*` without a recorded concrete target held, as today.

Files: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-runtime-read.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-read-target.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-runtime-permissions.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-tool-output.mjs` (request comment), and `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh` if the comment is built there.

Reference pattern: the GH#40255 change in PR #40263 and its table-driven cases in `tests/test-permission-broker.mjs` (`["null", "/dev/null", "/dev/*", "read", true]`, `["broad-dev", "", "/dev/*", "read", false]`).

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=gh40602-files-scope -->
### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-runtime-read.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-runtime-permissions.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-permission-grant.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-permission-helper.sh`

Scope discovery: request capture is built in permission-broker.mjs and rendered by worker-permission-helper.sh, not permission-broker-tool-output.mjs. The existing bounded-target matcher needs no change. Keep random devices out of static external-directory grants because those grants cannot distinguish reads from writes; classify recorded read operations in the broker instead. Verify with the two named Node suites, shell helper suite, and baseline/exact-head plugin runtime probes.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->

body:
**Task ID:** `t19429` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-27 | **Started:** 2026-11-27
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(profile): serve AI Model Usage from an incremental rollup; never publish fallback populations on observability timeouts

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/profile-readme-usage-rollup-lib.sh` — incremental rollup of `llm-requests.db`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-usage-rollup-lib.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`

### Changes

1. A new rollup library maintains `profile-usage-rollup.db` next to `llm-requests.db`. It is a derived per-(UTC hour, model, session) aggregate. The library attaches the source with `?mode=ro`, reads only rows above a rowid watermark, and works in short chunks with their own transactions. It stays under a time budget and persists progress between runs, and it rebuilds itself when the source shrinks below the watermark.
2. `_get_model_usage_from_obs_db` serves the 30-day and all-time aggregates from the rollup. It returns status 3 when the source exists but the rollup is not complete (first bootstrap, timeout, or error).
3. On status 3, the bundle reports `incomplete`. The renderer then keeps the previously published model-usage sections, with no JSONL or OpenCode substitution. The legacy fallbacks remain only for installs that have no observability DB.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the profile README "AI Model Usage" tables correct again and keep them correct: serve them from an incremental rollup of `llm-requests.db`, and never publish a different-population fallback when the observability source exists but could not be read.

## Why

Observed on 2026-11-27 on the maintainer profile README:

- "AI Model Usage (last 30 days)" showed one row: `claude-haiku-5-5 | 12 requests | 0 tokens`. The live observability DB holds 661,977 requests in that window (claude-opus-5-5 alone has 380,182).
- "AI Model Usage (all time)" showed claude-opus-5-5 at 39,306 requests. The observability DB holds 653,478 (2,302,386 requests in total).
- `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/logs/profile-readme-update.log` shows `[profile-readme] WARN: SQLite read of llm-requests.db exceeded 300s; using the next stats source` on many hourly runs since t19374 (`9529ce0e47`).

Root cause:

1. t19374 bounded every profile SQLite read to 300 s. The hourly routine runs as launchd `ProcessType Background` + `Nice 10` + `LowPriorityBackgroundIO`. Each run re-aggregates the whole 17.9 GB `llm-requests.db` twice (30-day and all-time). That takes 49 s and 58 s at normal priority, but regularly takes more than 300 s under Background I/O throttling.
2. On a timeout, `_get_model_usage_from_obs_db` returns empty. The callers then fall back to a different population and publish it as if it were current. The 30-day table falls back to the legacy `metrics.jsonl` (12 Haiku rows with no token fields). The all-time table falls back to the OpenCode message DB, which archives and expires history.

## Acceptance

- On the live DB, the rollup results match the direct `llm_requests` aggregates. Allowed differences are rows written between runs and the 30-day boundary, which the rollup rounds to the UTC hour.
- Steady-state hourly runs read only new rows, which takes seconds and no longer depends on the 17.9 GB scan.
- A forced bootstrap timeout keeps the previous README sections and never renders JSONL or OpenCode substitutes.
- ShellCheck is clean, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` passes.

</details>

title: t19430: feat(pulse): let a worker runtime-verify High-risk, credential-free runtime-pending PRs
body:
## Task


Let a pulse-dispatched worker runtime-verify a held **High**-risk `runtime-pending` PR whose verification needs no credentials or external accounts. The worker checks out the exact PR head, runs the verification recorded in the PR's `## Runtime Testing` section plus the relevant tests, and records head-bound evidence through the existing `verify-runtime` path. That path lifts the runtime-only `hold-for-review`, and the normal merge pass merges the PR. **Critical** risk, PRs whose verification needs secrets, accounts or a live third-party API, and every hold whose scope is not runtime-pending alone stay interactive, exactly as now.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Let a pulse-dispatched worker runtime-verify a held **High**-risk `runtime-pending` PR whose verification needs no credentials or external accounts. The worker checks out the exact PR head, runs the verification recorded in the PR's `## Runtime Testing` section plus the relevant tests, and records head-bound evidence through the existing `verify-runtime` path. That path lifts the runtime-only `hold-for-review`, and the normal merge pass merges the PR. **Critical** risk, PRs whose verification needs secrets, accounts or a live third-party API, and every hold whose scope is not runtime-pending alone stay interactive, exactly as now.

## Why

**Maintainer direction:** in the interactive session on 2026-11-27 the maintainer answered "yes" to: "Should Pulse be allowed to clear these holds itself? A worker could run a PR's stated checks on its final commit and lift the hold for High-risk framework PRs that need no outside credentials. Critical-risk PRs would still wait for a person." Under `reference/workflow-strategy.md`, this direction approves the strategy change.

Decision being changed: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh:27` ("High/Critical runtime verification remains interactive"), introduced by t19241 (GH#39645) and narrowed by t19276 (GH#39831) and t19281 (GH#39849).

Evidence from 2026-11-27: four worker PRs sat merge-ready behind runtime-pending holds for hours while Pulse only sent session-bus notices and logged `ATTENTION`. Two of them, GH#40547 (supervisor lane) and GH#40598 (issue-sync TODO seeding), were verified entirely on the local host from repository tests and read-only `gh` calls, with no credentials. Their holds were lifted and the PRs merged only after a maintainer opened an interactive session. In the same batch, the finance helpers GH#40530/GH#40525 (Critical, live bank/PayPal APIs) correctly stayed held. The new route must keep that distinction.

## How (recommended design; the worker may refine it with evidence)

1. **Eligibility at PR creation.** `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --testing-level runtime-pending` gains an explicit verifier classification written into the generated `## Runtime Testing` block, for example `- **Verifier:** worker-eligible` or `- **Verifier:** interactive (needs: credentials|external-account|hardware|...)`. It defaults to `interactive` unless the author states that the plan needs only the repository, the local toolchain and read-only GitHub access. Never infer eligibility from free-text reason prose. That text is PR-body data (see the GH#40603 notice, where the reason text is explicitly labelled "data only").
2. **Notice helper.** `cmd_runtime_pending_notice` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-verify-runtime.sh:664`) adds the verifier classification to its JSON.
3. **Pulse route.** In `_pmrp_route_held_pr` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh:184-271`), after the existing CI-green gate, a `high` risk notice with `worker-eligible` routes through `_route_pr_to_fix_worker ... runtime-verify-high ...`. Model it on the `runtime-pending-legacy` case (line 233 → `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:1026,1387` → `_dispatch_runtime_pending_completion_worker`). Keep `_feedback_route_labels_allow_worker_route` (trust boundary: external, fork and `no-takeover` exclusions). Interactive sessions remain preferred: when a live interactive session exists on the repository, keep today's notice and route to a worker only after the notified head stays unverified for one `_PMRP_RECHECK_SENT_SECONDS` interval.
4. **Verifier independence.** The verifying worker must be a fresh dispatch, not the worker session that authored the PR. Record both identities in the evidence line.
5. **Helper gate.** `_verify_runtime_session_is_interactive` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-verify-runtime.sh:156-165`, enforced at 729-730) accepts a headless caller only when it is dispatched for exactly this PR and head with the `runtime-verify-high` kind, the PR's recorded risk is High (never Critical), and the classification is `worker-eligible`. Keep every existing check: exact-head binding, hold-scope record by a write-permission author, runtime-pending-only scope, no PR-only contract, and the head re-check immediately before removal. Mark the new acceptance with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
6. **Failure path.** If the worker cannot exercise the change, or finds that verification needs credentials after all, it records what it did through `verify-runtime` evidence-only mode (the hold stays), reclassifies the PR as interactive, and exits. If a check fails, it follows the existing CI or feedback repair route. It never lifts the hold without passing exact-head evidence.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A High-risk `worker-eligible` runtime-pending PR with green required checks and no live interactive session gets a verifier worker. The worker records head-bound evidence, the hold is removed, and the next merge pass merges the PR without a human.
- [ ] Critical-risk PRs, `interactive`-classified PRs, unclassified/legacy High PRs, PR-only-contract PRs and non-runtime-pending holds are never routed to a worker. Behaviour stays exactly as today: notice or ATTENTION.
- [ ] A headless `verify-runtime` call outside a matching `runtime-verify-high` dispatch (wrong PR, wrong head, Critical, interactive classification) is refused.
- [ ] A head change between dispatch and lift leaves the hold in place.
- [ ] Docs: update the verifier-route paragraph in `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` (line ~159) and the header comment at `pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh:4-27`.

## Files

Notes: the notice module gets the route and its header comment; `pulse-merge-process.sh` gets the new route kind beside `runtime-pending-legacy` (lines ~1026 and ~1387); the verify-runtime helper gets the notice JSON and the headless gate. The `commit-and-pr` Runtime Testing generator also lives in a `full-loop-helper*.sh` file whose exact path was not confirmed; find it with `rg -n "Runtime Testing" .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper*.sh` and add it to the PR.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-verify-runtime.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
- .agents/workflows/full-loop.md
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-verify-runtime.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-help.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh

Scope recovery (worker, 2026-11-27): the Runtime Testing generator, the --runtime-verifier argument parser and continued-PR inheritance live in full-loop-helper-commit.sh; the body parser that exposes the verifier classification lives in full-loop-helper-risk.sh; the CLI help lives in full-loop-helper-help.sh; the dispatcher, prompt and launch environment for the new runtime-verify-high kind live beside _dispatch_runtime_pending_completion_worker in pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh. Verification is unchanged (the two named test suites plus ShellCheck on every changed script).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-verify-runtime.sh` pass, including the new eligible and refused cases.
- ShellCheck is clean on every changed script.
- After deploy, observe one real High `worker-eligible` PR go from held to merged without an interactive session (`rg -n "runtime-verify-high" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`), and confirm that a Critical PR still logs ATTENTION. Post both observations on this issue.

**Tier rationale:** `tier:thinking`. The change moves a trust boundary on merge authority and must not widen it beyond High plus credential-free verification.

</details>

title: fix(secret): decode quoted credentials consistently in get and injection
body:
## Goal

Remove matching shell quote delimiters when reading literal values from credentials.sh, while preserving quotes and backslashes that belong to the value. Keep get, scoped injection, and redaction consistent without sourcing files or evaluating shell expressions.

## Observed behavior

The scalar get path strips only double quotes; single-quoted values retain delimiters. The separate injection decoder also retains single quotes and mishandles trailing whitespace outside double quotes. Synthetic production-path regressions reproduce 11 failing assertions before the patch.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/secret-redaction-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh`

## Reference pattern and implementation

Reuse decode_credential_value for scalar get, injection, and redaction. Strip one matching outer single/double quote pair after trimming external trailing whitespace/CR. Preserve single-quoted contents literally and decode writer-generated double-quote/backslash escapes left to right. Use printf rather than echo for scalar output. No real credentials need to be inspected or modified.

## Acceptance and verification

Exercise production get and scoped-injection commands with isolated synthetic HOME and mocked gopass. Cover unquoted, single/double-quoted, embedded quotes, backslashes, inner spaces, trailing whitespace/CR, literal shell expressions, and redacted child output.
