title: mailbox-search-helper: Spotlight backend returns [] for live Mail.app V10 messages; add emlx fallback and index warning
body:
## Observed

`mailbox-search-helper.sh search "<address>" --backend spotlight` returned `[]` for three client addresses. A direct scan of Mail.app storage (`rg -l -i -F -e <address> -g '*.emlx' ~/Library/Mail/V10`) found 213 matching `.emlx` files (20 unique messages after Message-ID dedup).

`mailbox-search-helper.sh index-status` reported `{"backend":"spotlight","available":true,"indexed_emails":251593}` at the same time, so the empty result looked like "no mail" rather than "not indexed".

`mdfind` full-text queries return hits only from an archived `/Volumes/<disk>/Mail/V2` store, never from the live `~/Library/Mail/V10` store, which suggests Spotlight on this macOS install does not index the current Mail.app store (Full Disk Access / Mail privacy indexing).

## Impact

Email-history research silently returns nothing; an agent may report "no client correspondence" when there are live threads.

## Proposed fix

Files: `.agents/scripts/mailbox-search-helper.sh` (spotlight backend and `index-status`).

1. In `index-status`, report the indexed count for `~/Library/Mail/V*` separately (e.g. `mdfind -onlyin ~/Library/Mail -count 'kMDItemContentType == "com.apple.mail.emlx"'`) and warn when it is 0 while `.emlx` files exist on disk.
2. In `search` (backend auto/spotlight), when Spotlight returns 0 results and `~/Library/Mail/V*` contains `.emlx` files, fall back to a bounded `rg -l -i -F --glob '*.emlx'` scan and parse headers (Message-ID dedup, prefer INBOX/Sent over Drafts/Outbox/SendLater autosaves).
3. Emit a `backend_used` / `fallback_reason` field in the JSON result.

## Verification

- With a known address present in a live Mail.app message, `search "<address>"` returns at least one result.
- `index-status` shows the live-store count and the warning when the count is 0.
- ShellCheck clean.

title: fix(canonical): maintenance-gc misses a live repack after gc.pid takeover
body:
## Problem

`canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh` decides "gc is running" only from the PID in `<common-dir>/gc.pid` (`_cgh_gc_is_running`, and the `gc-pid-live-or-foreign` lock skip). Git itself treats `gc.pid` as stale once it is older than 12 hours, so a second `git gc --auto` can take over the file while the first gc is still repacking. After the takeover, the original repack is invisible to `maintenance-gc`.

## Observed evidence (point-in-time, 2026-11-27, Linux, 24 cores, 125 GiB RAM)

- A canonical repository with ~1,950 packs (~63 GiB) had `git gc --auto` running for 13h36m. Its `pack-objects --all --reflog` child had used 11h52m CPU, so it was progressing, not hung.
- A second `git gc --auto`, triggered from a linked worktree of the same repository, rewrote `gc.pid` and started a second full cruft repack (~6 GiB RSS) on the same object store. The host was using 67 GiB of swap.
- The second gc's process group was stopped manually; the first continued.

## Risk

If the newer gc exits first, `maintenance-gc --apply` sees a dead `gc.pid` and may treat the repository as idle: it could remove `gc.log`, stale-looking temp packs, or run another foreground gc while the original repack still writes to `objects/pack/`.

## Proposed fix

1. In `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh`, add a live-process check: any `git gc`, `git repack` or `git pack-objects` process whose cwd (via `/proc/<pid>/cwd` on Linux, `lsof -p` on macOS) or `--git-dir`/`.tmp-<pid>-pack` argument resolves to the same common dir counts as a running gc. title: commit-and-pr keeps a stale body when an open draft PR for the head references the issue with For #N
body:
## What happened

A worker opened an early draft PR with `gh-write-helper.sh pr create --draft` and a body that referenced the issue with `For #N`. It then ran `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue N`. That run:

- did not find the existing PR as a continuation, so `issue_open_pr_guard_check` returned 0, not 3;
- went to `_create_pr`, which printed `PR #M created` for the existing PR;
- applied `hold-for-review` and the merge summary, but left the hand-written draft body, with no `## Runtime Testing` section and no closing keyword.

When the body was changed to `Resolves #N` and the same command ran again, the guard found the PR as a continuation. `_reconcile_recovered_pr_metadata` then regenerated the body correctly.

Observed on PR #40612 for issue #40607.

## Expected

- `commit-and-pr` regenerates the body of any open PR for the current head branch, or refuses with guidance.
- It never reports an existing PR as created while keeping a stale body.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`: `_create_or_continue_pr` and `_create_pr`. `_reconcile_recovered_pr_metadata` runs only when `recovered=1`.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`: `_commit_and_pr_publish`, the `issue_open_pr_guard_check` call.
- The `issue_open_pr_guard_check` implementation. It appears to match only closing references, not an open PR whose head is the current branch.
- `gh_create_pr` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`: how it returns an existing PR URL for the same head.

## Verification

Reproduce with a stubbed GitHub in `tests/test-full-loop-squash-continuation.sh` or `tests/test-full-loop-worker-pr-linkage.sh`:

1. Create an open draft PR for the head branch whose body has `For #N`.
2. Run `commit-and-pr --issue N`.
3. Assert that the PR body was regenerated (it has `## Runtime Testing` and the expected closing keyword), or that the command refused before pushing.

body:
## Task


Make the profile README `session-time --period profile` collection bounded and incremental, so the hourly profile routine finishes in minutes under launchd Background priority. Today it does not.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session_time_db.py` / `.agents/scripts/session-time-interval-engine.py`: add an incremental derived store, or reuse the existing `--cache-file` path, so each run reads only rows newer than a persisted watermark per source DB. Per-session interval state must stay correct across the watermark. Immutable monthly archive segments (`archive_segments`, GH#40419) can be summarised once and keyed by file identity (size + mtime).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh:294` `_get_profile_session_times`: bound the step with `timeout_sec`, as `_profile_sqlite_read` does at line 370. On timeout, report an explicit incomplete status and keep the previously published "Work with AI" sections, following `_render_preserved_model_usage_sections` in `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh`. Never publish zeros or unavailable values as fresh data.
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-usage-rollup-lib.sh`. It uses a rowid watermark, chunked short read-only transactions, a time budget, resumable bootstrap and a rebuild when the source shrinks.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/session_time_db.py`
- `.agents/scripts/session_time_db_roots.py`
- `.agents/scripts/session-time-interval-engine.py`
- `.agents/scripts/session_time_aggregate.py`
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the profile README `session-time --period profile` collection bounded and incremental, so the hourly profile routine finishes in minutes under launchd Background priority. Today it does not.

## Why

Observed on 2026-11-27 on the maintainer host (aidevops v3.39.290/291, macOS, `llm-requests.db` about 17 GB plus OpenCode session DBs and monthly archives):

- The 19:00Z profile routine was still inside `contributor-activity-helper.sh session-time --all-dirs --period profile --format json` after 70 minutes.
- Its Python child, `session-time-interval-engine.py --period profile --all-dirs`, had used 42 s of CPU in those 70 minutes, at 0% CPU and state `RN`. It is I/O-bound under the routine's `ProcessType Background` / `LowPriorityBackgroundIO` throttle.
- A second diagnostic run of the same step was still running after 29 minutes and was cancelled.
- The previous run (17:06Z to 17:54Z) took 48 minutes. Overlapping hourly runs log `Profile README update already running; skipping overlapping refresh`, so the README refreshes only every 1–2 hours.
- This is the same mechanism fixed for AI Model Usage in t19429 / GH#40606 (PR #40610, v3.39.291): a full year-window re-scan of large SQLite sources on every run, starved by Background I/O. That fix moved model usage to an incremental rowid-watermark rollup (`.agents/scripts/profile-readme-usage-rollup-lib.sh`). Session time still re-reads everything:
  - `SESSION_QUERY` in `.agents/scripts/session_time_db.py:28` joins `session` and `message` for every root DB and archive segment since `now - 1 year`, evaluating `json_valid` and `json_extract` per row.
  - `OBS_QUERY` (`session_time_db.py:34`) scans `llm_requests` over the same window.
- No timeout bounds the step (`_get_profile_session_times` in `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh:294`). Its fallback is an all-`unavailable` payload only on error, not on slowness.

## Acceptance

- On a host with a multi-GB OpenCode DB and `llm-requests.db`, a steady-state `contributor-activity-helper.sh session-time --all-dirs --period profile --format json` completes in under 60 s at Background priority (`taskpolicy -b`). The first build may resume across runs.
- Parity: incremental output equals the current full-scan output for `day`, `week`, `28d` and `year` on the same snapshot (record the command and diff in the PR).
- A timed-out or incomplete session-time step keeps the previously published sections instead of rendering them as unavailable or zero.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` passes; ShellCheck and the Python lint used by CI are clean.

title: Footprint defer: claimed no-auto-dispatch blocker forces full dispatch_with_dedup re-run every pulse cycle
body:
## Observed

A candidate issue deferred by `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` against a blocker that is `status:claimed` + `no-auto-dispatch` (an interactive maintainer claim) is fully re-evaluated by `dispatch_with_dedup` on every pulse pass, even though the blocker and the overlapping file are unchanged.

Evidence from one runner's `pulse.log` (repo and issue numbers replaced with placeholders):

```
[footprint-defer] event=wake issue=#<candidate> repo=<owner>/<repo> blocker=#<blocker> wake_reason=blocker_coordinator_recheck
[pulse-wrapper] DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_ATTEMPT #<candidate>
[footprint-defer] event=deferred issue=#<candidate> blocker=#<blocker> expires_at=<+6h> suppressed=0 wake_reason=none
[dispatch_with_dedup] (t2117) Dispatch deferred ... FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#<blocker> files=docs/workflows/<file>.md)
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1 ... elapsed_ms=16163
```

This sequence repeats 2 times per pulse cycle (a third attempt in the same cycle short-circuits on `skip:already_assigned`). Each pass costs about 16–18 s of wrapper time, and the log shows the same pattern dozens of times across about 6 hours. The blocker is an interactive claim that has not been updated for about 10 days, so the cost keeps recurring for as long as the claim stays open.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason()` (around line 316) always returns `blocker_coordinator_recheck` for `parent-task` blockers and for blockers labelled both `no-auto-dispatch` and `status:claimed`. That bypasses `_footprint_defer_should_suppress()` on every cycle, and the recorded `expires_at` window has no effect for these blockers.

## Suggested direction

When the live check re-defers against the same blocker with the same `blocker_hash` and an unchanged blocker `updatedAt`, suppress later passes until `expires_at` or until the blocker changes. Keep the live check for parent-task coordinators if their footprint really is computed differently. Also consider skipping the duplicate same-cycle attempt before the dedup layers run.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` — `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason`, `_footprint_defer_should_suppress`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` — existing `blocker_coordinator_recheck` case (around line 802)

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` passes.
- With a deferred candidate whose claimed `no-auto-dispatch` blocker is unchanged, later pulse cycles log a suppressed defer with no 16 s `dispatch_with_dedup` pass. When the blocker's labels, body footprint or `updatedAt` change, the candidate is re-evaluated in the next cycle.
<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=gh40634-maintainer-brief -->
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Maintainer brief (review of GH#40634)

This section is the implementation contract. It supersedes "Suggested direction" above: do not key suppression on blocker `updatedAt`, and do not add a separate same-cycle skip.

## What

Make the durable footprint defer use the same per-blocker footprint rule as the live in-flight check, so an unchanged overlap stays suppressed and a released blocker wakes the candidate on the next pass.

## Why

Reproduced at `dc2b6e5d58` by sourcing `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` with a stubbed `gh`:

- A `status:claimed` + `no-auto-dispatch` blocker with an unchanged footprint wakes the defer every pass with `blocker_coordinator_recheck` (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:316-322`). The live check then finds implementation evidence, defers again, and the loop repeats. This is the reported 16 s `dispatch_with_dedup` pass, twice per cycle: the second same-cycle attempt also goes through `_dispatch_skip_for_footprint_defer` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:651`) and wakes again.
- The opposite failure: a `status:claimed` blocker without `no-auto-dispatch` stays suppressed when it has no implementation evidence. GH#36817 (`01a96ea308`) made every claimed issue need evidence at `dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:1078-1082`, but the wake rule still matches only `no-auto-dispatch` + `status:claimed`. The candidate waits up to the 6 h TTL even though the live check would dispatch it.
- A `status:in-review` blocker whose footprint is scoped to its linked PR files (GH#40406, `faf14df3d0`, `dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:1092-1104`) wakes with `blocker_footprint_changed` on every pass. `_footprint_defer_record_overlap` hashes the PR-scoped files (`:238`), but the wake rule hashes the brief body paths (`:323-326`).

Root cause: `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason` copies the per-issue footprint rule from `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` instead of calling it, and the copy has drifted twice. Keying on `updatedAt` would not fix this. Implementation evidence (ledger entry, live local claim stamp, linked open PR) can disappear without any change to the blocker issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:298-329` — wake rule; `:1071-1111` — per-issue rule in `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh:297-334` — `gh` mock gains a `pr list` branch; `:792-808` — Test 23 expectation and new cases after it

### Implementation Steps

1. Move the per-issue rule at `dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:1073-1104` (skip `parent-task`; claimed issues need `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence`; in-review non-claimed issues use `_footprint_pr_scoped_paths`) into one helper, for example `_footprint_issue_live_paths repo num is_parent is_claimed is_in_review body result_var`. It returns its paths through `printf -v`, like `_footprint_get_inflight` (`:1126-1141`), and prints nothing when the issue reserves no footprint. Keep the `footprint_stale_coordinator` and `footprint_pr_scoped` log lines inside it.
2. Make `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` call the helper once per row in the current shell. Never call it inside command substitution: that would lose the GH#38055 open-PR memo and fetch the PR list once per claimed issue.
3. Rewrite `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason`. Keep the lifecycle check (`:309-315`). Read the `parent-task`, `status:claimed` and `status:in-review` flags from the blocker labels, the repo from `state_json .repo_slug`, and the number from `.blocking_issue`. Call the helper. No paths means `blocker_coordinator_released`. Otherwise hash `printf '%s\n' "$paths" | sort -u` exactly as `_footprint_defer_record_overlap` does (`:238`, `:241`); a different hash means `blocker_footprint_changed`; an equal hash prints nothing, so the defer stays suppressed. Update the comment at `:298-304`.
4. Tests: change Test 23 to expect `blocker_coordinator_released` for `parent-task`. Add these cases with `MOCK_BLOCKER_LABEL` / `MOCK_BLOCKER_EXTRA_LABEL` and a PR-list env var on the existing `TEST_BIN` mock, plus an isolated `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_LEDGER_DIR` (HOME is already isolated at `:46`): (a) claimed + `no-auto-dispatch` blocker with a linked open PR (`Resolves #401`) stays suppressed on two consecutive calls and `suppressed_count` reaches 2; (b) the same blocker with no PR, ledger or stamp wakes with `blocker_coordinator_released`; (c) a claimed blocker without `no-auto-dispatch` and no evidence wakes with `blocker_coordinator_released`; (d) an in-review blocker recorded with PR-scoped inflight data, whose linked PR changes files that differ from its body paths, stays suppressed.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_footprint_defer_should_suppress` (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:383`) is the only caller of the wake rule; `_footprint_get_inflight` / `_footprint_check_overlap` read the in-flight cache; `_dispatch_skip_for_footprint_defer` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:309-318`) calls the suppress path.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `_footprint_defer_wake` and `_footprint_defer_write_json` write the defer state under `~/.aidevops/cache/footprint-defers`; the defer schema `aidevops-footprint-defer/v1` is unchanged.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` (Tests 11-11b, the GH#38055 memo test at `:528`, the in-review scope cases at `:580-588`, and Tests 12-24); `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` Test 20b reads defer state but does not depend on wake reason names.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the defer JSON fields and `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` are unchanged; only the `wake_reason` string `blocker_coordinator_recheck` becomes `blocker_coordinator_released`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` is deployed by `setup.sh`; `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh:161-163` holds display-only line hints that are already stale and need no change.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because existing defer records stay valid: an inactive record is ignored, and an active one is checked against the new rule on its next pass.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR restores the old wake rule; defer records need no cleanup.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** The wake rule runs outside the reservation lock, as it does today. A blocker that loses its evidence just after a suppressed pass is re-evaluated on the next pass, which is the same window as today.
- **Migration/rollback:** Mixed old and new records are safe because neither version writes the wake reason into the comparison hash.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Only diagnostics read the wake reason string (`pulse-diagnose-issue.sh:805` prints it as-is); a runner on the old version keeps the old loop until it updates.
- **Idempotency/retry:** A repeated suppressed pass only increments `suppressed_count`; a failed `gh pr list` read gives `[]`, which wakes into the live check, and the live check applies the same no-evidence rule.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** A failed blocker read still keeps the defer suppressed (Test 19); the GH#38055 memo stays limited to the rebuild, so a suppress pass reads the PR list at most once.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** the first command covers the wake rule, the refactor of the in-flight cache, the open-PR memo and all defer cases; the second covers the defer diagnostics; `shellcheck` covers both edited files.

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-diagnose-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deferred candidate whose claimed blocker still has implementation evidence and an unchanged footprint logs `event=suppressed` on later passes, with no `event=wake` and no `DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_ATTEMPT` for that candidate.
- [ ] A claimed blocker, with or without `no-auto-dispatch`, that has lost all implementation evidence wakes the defer with `blocker_coordinator_released` on the next pass.
- [ ] An unchanged in-review blocker whose footprint is scoped to its linked PR files stays suppressed.
- [ ] Regression: the GH#38055 test still shows one open-PR fetch per rebuild, and no existing case in `test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` changes result except the renamed reason in Test 23.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

body:
## Task


Headless workers on macOS runners end with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet` when a brief needs a Linux userland, a container runtime or a WordPress site, without trying the substitutes the runner already has. Observed in `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` over about a month: about 11 issues and 15 attempts with details such as "this runner is darwin; the approved workflow requires Linux and `bwrap` was not found", "macos/arm64 cannot execute the approved Linux integration test", and "the required isolated WordPress runtime is unavailable in this worktree" (5 attempts on one issue). The same runner had a running OrbStack Docker engine (`docker info` → `OrbStack aarch64`), `orb` for Linux VMs, `php`, `npx` (WordPress Playground CLI) and LocalWP. Each such block needed an interactive session to resolve.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Headless workers on macOS runners end with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet` when a brief needs a Linux userland, a container runtime or a WordPress site, without trying the substitutes the runner already has. Observed in `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` over about a month: about 11 issues and 15 attempts with details such as "this runner is darwin; the approved workflow requires Linux and `bwrap` was not found", "macos/arm64 cannot execute the approved Linux integration test", and "the required isolated WordPress runtime is unavailable in this worktree" (5 attempts on one issue). The same runner had a running OrbStack Docker engine (`docker info` → `OrbStack aarch64`), `orb` for Linux VMs, `php`, `npx` (WordPress Playground CLI) and LocalWP. Each such block needed an interactive session to resolve.

## Why

`runner_capability_unmet` should mean no runner-local route exists. Today the worker contract (`headless-runtime-contract.sh`) only says to check repository-declared tools and never install, so workers read a platform mismatch as final. Host VPN clients are the one real exception: connecting or switching a host VPN changes routing for every concurrent session and the operator.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh`: after the existing missing-tool rule, add one rule. A missing Linux userland, container runtime or WordPress site is not `runner_capability_unmet` until the local substitutes were tried, using disposable labelled resources. Never connect, disconnect or switch a host VPN. Use the class only when no substitute exists, the substitute failed (name the command and error), or the brief or repo doc forbids it.
- `.agents/reference/platform-support.md`: new "Local runtime substitutes (headless workers)" section listing detection commands and routes: OrbStack/Docker containers (`docker run --rm`, labels per `tools/containers/disposable-resources.md`), OrbStack Linux VMs (`orb create`/`orb run`) for tools like `bwrap`, Apple `container` CLI when present, WordPress Playground / Docker WordPress per worktree (`tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md`), and LocalWP only read-only or via `local-site-sync-helper.sh`. Covers VPN limits and when the class still applies.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh`
- `.agents/reference/platform-support.md`

## Acceptance

- The contract text renders in the worker prompt (`headless-runtime-contract.sh` existing tests pass).
- A live probe on a macOS runner shows each documented detection command resolving (`docker info`, `orb version`, `npx --version`, `php --version`).
- ShellCheck clean; markdownlint clean on the changed doc.

title: feat(sessions): full-text search of user messages across all OpenCode session databases
body:
## Problem

Users often ask an agent to "find the session where I asked X". The current lookups match only session metadata:

- `session-attachments-helper.sh sessions --title TEXT` matches the title.
- `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh sessions --query TEXT` matches id, title, directory and project id (`_sessions_query_db` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-sessions.sh`).

Auto-generated titles describe the first message, so later requests in a long session are invisible to these lookups. In the observed case, the session was titled after its first message ("continue from checkpoint ..."). The request the user remembered came two days later as a follow-up message, so no title search could find it.

## Evidence

- In one project, about 18 of roughly 250 top-level interactive sessions were opened only to find an earlier session (titles like "Find ... session" or "Пошук сесії ...").
- The agent had to compose its own SQL: `session` -> `message` (role user) -> `part` (type text, not synthetic), with `LIKE` on the text. It repeated this for the shared database, its archive, and every per-project `XDG_DATA_HOME` database under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/*/opencode/` (and their archives).
- Scanning only user text parts kept each query to about 1.5-6 s on a ~5 GB shared database opened with `file:<path>?mode=ro`.

## Proposed change

Add a content-search mode, for example `opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh sessions --text TEXT [--role user|assistant|any] [--directory PATH] [--include-archive] [--limit N] [--json]`, or a `search` subcommand in `session-attachments-helper.sh`. It should:

1. Enumerate every database the way `opencode-db-inventory-lib.sh` does: shared, archive, and per-project interactive databases.
2. By default, search only text parts from the chosen role (skipping tool output and synthetic parts), in top-level sessions.
3. Accept several terms with any/all matching, because SQLite `LIKE` is case-insensitive only for ASCII; Cyrillic and other scripts need explicit variants without ICU.
4. Print the database source, session id, title, directory, message time and a short excerpt.
5. Open databases read-only and stay time-bounded.

Then add the mode to `.agents/reference/memory-lookup.md`, Tier 2, item 5.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-sessions.sh` (new `--text` option), or `.agents/scripts/session-attachments-helper.sh` (new `search` subcommand)
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-inventory-lib.sh` (reuse the database enumeration)
- `.agents/reference/memory-lookup.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-session-lookup-helper.sh` (extend the existing test)

## Verification

- Fixture database with a session whose title lacks the term but whose later user message contains it: `--text` returns that session with an excerpt; `--query` does not.
- A Cyrillic term is found; matches only in tool output are excluded by default.
- It runs against a live WAL database without writing to it.

title: t19435: fix(release): release status runs git fetch in the canonical checkout and trips the canonical Git guard
body:
## Task


Make `aidevops release status <PR>` complete without mutating the canonical checkout, so it never trips the canonical Git guard. `aidevops release --help` documents `status` as read-only.

## Done when

- [ ] `aidevops release status <PR>` run from the canonical checkout performs no `git fetch` or `update-ref` there, completes tag discovery from local evidence, and prints `RELEASE_TAG=<tag>` when the tag is known locally.
- [ ] Regression: `reconcile`, new `release` and `recover-aggregate` still fetch tags in their control worktree before discovery; status read-only handling must not reach those modes.
- [ ] Status output keeps the `RELEASE_LANE`, `RELEASE_EXECUTOR`, `RELEASE_RECEIPT` and `RELEASE_TIMING` keys unchanged.
- [ ] ShellCheck and changed-file linters are clean.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


**Root cause (verified):** GH#38741 (`28bf479b73`, "skip control worktree for read-only release status") stopped `status` from creating the release control worktree, so `REPO_ROOT` comes from `_full_loop_release_resolve_repo_root`. That function returns the canonical checkout when the caller is not inside a linked worktree (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:22-39`, `:1164-1166`). Tag discovery still begins with `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" fetch origin --tags --quiet` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:539`, inside `_full_loop_release_find_tag_for_pr`). `status` reaches that through `_full_loop_release_existing_command` (`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:1971`). In the canonical checkout the fetch is a ref mutation, and the guard blocks it.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:522-544` — in `_full_loop_release_find_tag_for_pr`, do not run `git fetch` into a canonical `REPO_ROOT` in `status` mode.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh` — extend the existing git-stub cases (the `*" fetch origin --tags --quiet"*) return 0 ;;` pattern at ~L269/386/426) with a status-mode case where `fetch` fails as the guard does, asserting that discovery still runs on local refs.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_full_loop_release_find_tag_for_pr` is called from `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:1971` (status + reconcile), `full-loop-release-helper.sh:318` (new release existing-guard) and `full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh:1138`. Only the `status` path runs without a control worktree. Reconcile, release and recover-aggregate prepare one (`full-loop-release-helper.sh:1166`) and must keep fetching.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the fetch at `:539` is the only canonical mutation on the status path. `_full_loop_release_recover_lane_tag` (`:552`) may also write `refs/tags/*` via `update-ref` (`:516`). Check whether status reaches it, and keep status read-only there too.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh` (git-stub based) and `test-full-loop-release-reconcile-command.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** none. Output keys (`RELEASE_LANE`, `RELEASE_RECEIPT`, `RELEASE_TAG`, `RELEASE_TIMING`) are unchanged; `rg -n "RELEASE_TAG=" .agents/scripts` lists every consumer.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the deployed copy under the user's aidevops agents directory is refreshed by `setup.sh` / release deploy; no generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because status persists no state; the only release state files (receipt under `_full_loop_release_receipt_path`, lane via `release_lane_read`) are read, not written, on this path.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because the change adds no files, refs or worktrees; reverting the edit to `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` restores the current behaviour.

### Implementation Steps

1. Pick the smallest read-only option that keeps signature verification intact, and record the choice in the PR decisions. Two options:
   - (a) In `status` mode, skip the fetch and run discovery on existing local tags/objects, with one-line notes such as `RELEASE_TAG_FETCH=skipped (read-only status; run reconcile from a linked worktree to refresh)`.
   - (b) Use read-only remote evidence (`git ls-remote --tags origin`) to detect a newer remote tag, and report it without fetching objects.

   Thread the mode through an explicit argument or a variable set by `_full_loop_release_existing_command`. Do not infer it from the cwd.
2. Keep reconcile, release and recover-aggregate fetching exactly as now. They run in the control worktree.
3. Extend the discovery test as described above, then run the verification commands.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** status must stay non-mutating, so concurrent status calls and a live release executor cannot race on refs. Preserve that.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. This is a read path with no persisted state.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** keep every existing output key. Add notes rather than renaming fields, because pulse and session-bus routing read `RELEASE_LANE`/`RELEASE_RECEIPT`.
- **Idempotency/retry:** status is replayable. Reconcile must keep refreshing tags so a stale local store cannot hide a new tag.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** when local tags are stale, status must say so and point to `aidevops release reconcile <PR>`. It must not report a wrong tag as authoritative or exit as if discovery failed.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-command.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the discovery test covers the status-mode read-only branch (positive) and the reconcile-mode fetch (regression). The command test covers status/reconcile dispatch and output keys. ShellCheck/linters cover the changed shell files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. The change is local to one read path in the release reconciler.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## Origin

Found during the interactive full-loop that released v3.39.292 (source PR #40639). Run from the canonical checkout, or from any directory outside a linked worktree, `aidevops release status 40639` printed lane and receipt state, then failed tag discovery:

```text
RELEASE_RECEIPT=published
RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-tag-fetch state=start
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git fetch'. Use a linked worktree for edits. ...
RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-tag-fetch state=finish elapsed_seconds=1 result=failed
RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-tag-discovery state=finish elapsed_seconds=1 result=failed
```

This happened twice in one session (once while the lane was `preparing`, once after `terminal/published`). The same command run from a linked worktree completed tag discovery.

## What

Make `aidevops release status <PR>` complete without mutating the canonical checkout, so it never trips the canonical Git guard. `aidevops release --help` documents `status` as read-only.

## Why

Status is the documented inspect path for exit-8 (pending) releases, and the release-lane session-bus notices point operators at it. When it fails in the default location, operators either misread the failure or retry from ad-hoc worktrees.

## Tier

`tier:standard`. This is a narrow fix in one function's read-only path. The approach choice is bounded (below) and needs no new infrastructure.

## Context & Decisions

- Not in scope: changing the canonical Git guard. It is correct to block canonical ref mutation; the defect is that a documented read-only command mutates.
- Not in scope: re-adding a control worktree to `status`. GH#38741 removed it deliberately for performance.
- Impact today: cosmetic or operator-confusing only. Publication and receipts were correct (`terminal_receipt: published` for v3.39.292).

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:522-560` — `_full_loop_release_find_tag_for_pr`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:1942-1975` — `_full_loop_release_existing_command` (status/reconcile entry)
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:22-39,1164-1166` — repo-root resolution and the GH#38741 status skip

title: Detect fseventsd memory runaway on macOS runners and ask the user to restart it
body:
## Problem

On a macOS runner, `fseventsd` can grow without bound under sustained worktree churn (fresh worktrees, package installs, cleanup deletes). Nothing in the framework notices, and the runner degrades for days: workers still dispatch, but load-sensitive steps such as browser verification fail repeatedly with timeouts and aborted requests, and each failed attempt is burned as a worker session.

## Evidence (one runner, observed 2026-11-28 00:24 UTC)

- Uptime 3 days 7 hours, 16 CPUs, 128 GB RAM.
- `fseventsd`: 8.0 GB RSS, 177-218% CPU, 60 hours accumulated CPU time; `top` attributes about 90 GB including compressed pages.
- Swap 63.3 GB used of 64 GB; 54-55 GB in the compressor; under 0.5 GB free pages; `kernel_task` at 66% CPU.
- One-minute load average 17-30 on 16 CPUs while worker processes were mostly idle.
- About 400 linked worktrees under the worktree base directory across all managed repos.
- Downstream effect: a project's ordinary-account browser verification step was attempted ten times over two days across three runners and failed every time on load (heading readiness timeouts, `net::ERR_ABORTED` critical assets). Its brief now tells workers to stop when the load average is at or above the CPU count, so the issue cycles through dispatch, a 1-5 minute session and a `runner_capability_unmet` release.

The usual remedy is `sudo killall fseventsd` (launchd restarts it) or a reboot. Both need the user, so the framework should detect the state and ask.

## Proposed change

Add a read-only runaway check beside the existing Backblaze health check and surface it through the same reminder path:

- Reference pattern: `_backblaze_health`, `_backblaze_action_line` and the `health`/`reminder` subcommands in `.agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh`.
- New check (macOS only): read `fseventsd` RSS and %CPU with `ps -o rss=,pcpu= -p "$(pgrep -x fseventsd)"`, plus `sysctl -n vm.swapusage`. Report `fseventsd_health=ok`, `runaway:<rss_gb>` (RSS above a threshold, suggested 2 GB, overridable by environment) or `unknown`.
- Action line for `runaway`: one sentence asking the user to run `sudo killall fseventsd` in a terminal or reboot, naming the observed RSS and swap use. Never attempt sudo.
- Pulse: when `runaway` is reported, record it with `throttle-report-helper.sh report` so the capacity effect is visible instead of silently failing load-sensitive workers.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/optimise-macos-indexing-backups.md`

The helper gets the new health function and action line, includes the result in `health` and `reminder` output, and adds the JSON field `fseventsd_health`. The workflow documents the check under "macOS coverage". Pulse wiring: the call site that already runs the Backblaze `reminder` (locate it with `rg -n "optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh" .agents/scripts`); if it needs a change, add that file to this scope in the PR.

## Verification

- `optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh macos health` prints `fseventsd_health=ok` on a healthy host.
- With the threshold set below the current RSS (environment override), it prints `runaway:<n>` and `reminder` emits the one-line action.
- ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 compatible; every function returns explicitly.

title: prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-file has no size cap and times out on large capture files
body:
## What

`prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-file` (and `check-file` / `sanitize-file`) loads the whole file into a Bash variable with no size cap, so large capture files time out instead of returning a verdict. Bound the file path the same way the stdin path is already bounded, and give large structured captures a scan that finishes.

## Why

A headless data-enrichment worker in a managed project repo stopped `BLOCKED` on 2026-11-27 because the required capture scan gate never returned: `scan-file` on a 152,692,688-byte page-capture JSON timed out at 120 s, and timed out again on a bounded retry. The worker correctly refused to use an unscanned capture, so the issue went to `status:blocked`. Earlier captures of the same document were 938 bytes and scanned without trouble; the new capture embeds rendered page images.

Root cause, observed in the deployed helper:

- `_main_dispatch_file_cmd()` (`.agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh`, around line 1453) runs `content=$(cat "$file")` and passes the full content to `cmd_scan` as an argument. There is no byte cap.
- The stdin path already caps input: `_pg_read_stdin_capped()` (around line 755) uses `max_bytes=10 MiB` and warns on truncation. The file path does not share that cap.

## How

1. In `_main_dispatch_file_cmd()`, stop reading the whole file into a variable. Reuse the capped buffering from `_pg_read_stdin_capped()` (for example, feed the file through the same capped reader) so file and stdin scans share one limit.
2. For a file over the cap, do not silently scan a prefix and report "clean". Either (a) scan it in bounded chunks with overlap and merge the findings, or (b) exit with a distinct non-clean code and a clear message (for example `oversize: <bytes> > <cap>`) so the caller can fail closed with a named reason instead of timing out. Prefer (a) if it finishes inside the worker's 120 s tool budget for a ~150 MB file; otherwise (b).
3. For JSON captures, consider skipping long base64/data-URI values (image bytes cannot carry readable prompt text) before pattern matching, and say so in the output. Make this opt-in or clearly logged, so it does not weaken the guard for text.
4. Document the cap and the oversize exit code in the helper usage text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scan-file` on a 150 MB JSON file returns a verdict (clean, findings, or explicit oversize) in under 60 s on a normal runner, never a timeout.
- [ ] File and stdin scans enforce the same documented cap.
- [ ] An oversize file is never reported as clean on a truncated prefix.
- [ ] Existing small-file behaviour and exit codes (0 clean, 1 findings) are unchanged.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh
# Synthesise a large capture-like JSON (about 150 MB with base64 noise) under the agent workspace tmp dir, then:
time .agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-file <that-file>
# Small-file regression:
printf 'hello world\n' | .agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-stdin
```

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh`

## Context

- One downstream project issue is blocked on this. It gets a retry once this fix is deployed.
- Found by the supervisor pulse blocker-recovery pass, 2026-11-28.

title: fix(recovery): terminal-blocker pending exhausts budget in queue stage; seed, holds and unclassified intakes never complete
body:
## Observed (supervisor pulse, 2026-11-28 ~01:45Z, one macOS runner)

`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` does not finish a full pass at the default budget (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS`=45). It also fails at 240s.

- 45s default: the queue stage returned no actionable entries in this pass, and the `seed` stage ended `rc=124`.
- 240s (`env BLOCKER_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS=240`): about 60 queue entries were checked. Most were `decided_unchanged` or emitted helper `rearm_decision` lines. The pass then ended:
  - `incomplete stage=entry rc=124` at `entry_comments` for one issue in a large private repo with ~40 queued entries
  - `incomplete stage=queue reason=budget_exhausted`
  - `incomplete stage=seed rc=124` (seed_policy for a single small repo)
  - `incomplete stage=holds rc=124` after about 10 `hold_list` repos
  - `incomplete stage=unclassified reason=budget_exhausted`, `incomplete stage=queue reason=unobserved_entries`

Only 4 actionable JSON entries were emitted in the 240s pass. The seed, holds and unclassified intakes never completed. A pulse at the default budget therefore never reaches the unclassified-hold or persistent-exclusion intakes.

## Related, closed

#38692 (decided human_decision holds starve budget), #40471 (one high-comment entry rc=124 starves queue), #38232 (seed cursor starvation). This pass looks like a regression or residual of those: `decided_unchanged` entries are cheap, but each `rearm_decision` entry still pays the issue, comments and revision fetches, and the budget is shared across the queue, seed, holds and unclassified stages.

## Suggested direction (worker decides)

- Give `seed`, `holds` and `unclassified` a reserved per-stage budget slice, so queue exhaustion cannot starve them. Alternatively, persist a cross-pass cursor per stage, as was done for seed in #38232.
- Skip the `entry_comments` and `entry_revision` fetches for entries whose last helper `rearm_decision` was `revision_changed`/`dependency_blocked` within the current pass window.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (budget env handling near the top, around lines 40–64; stage loop)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (existing coverage for bounded intake markers)

## Verification

Run `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` at the default budget on a runner with 50+ queued entries. The output must include completed `seed`, `holds` and `unclassified` stage lines (no `rc=124` or `budget_exhausted` for those stages) in at least one of two consecutive passes. Existing circuit tests stay green.
